records.qtitle: Connecting educational institutions with broadband network
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government has taken any initiative to connect all the educational institutions in the country with a broadband network;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details of the status of the project; and<br/><br/>(c) the services Government plans to deliver using the network along with the details thereof?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE<br/>MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT<br/> (DR. SHASHI THAROOR)<br/><br/>(a)	Yes, Sir.<br/><br/>(b)	The National Mission on Education through Information and Communication Technology (NMEICT) aims to extend computer infrastructure and connectivity to over 25000+ colleges and 2000 polytechnics in the country including all the 419 Universities/Deemed Universities and Institutions of National Importance. As on 31.03.2013, 400 universities and nearly 20117, colleges in the country have been connected. <br/><br/>(c)	There are various components of the NMEICT Mission which include the provision of e-books and e-journals free to the learners, support for the generation of e-contents for Under-Graduate and Post-Graduate level, the creation of web and video courses under NPTEL (National programme in Technology Enhanced Learning) in all branches of engineering and physical sciences, development of virtual laboratory, the development of vocational education modules, talk to a teacher, etc.  By extending computer infrastructure and connectivity, the reach of these facilities are ensured to the academic community.<br/>*****

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN POVERTY ALLEVIATION be pleased to state:	<br/>(a)	whether it is a fact that Government has categorized the people earning Rs. 1 lakh per annum as Economically Weaker Section  (EWS);<br/>(b)	whether it is also a fact that people with annual income of Rs. 1-2 lakh have been categorized as Lower Income Group (LIG);<br/>(c)	the basis for categorizing various sections of the people; and<br/>(d)	the benefits these categorized people are likely to get under various housing schemes of Government ?
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF HOUSING & URBAN POVERTY ALLEVIATION<br/>(SHRI AJAY MAKEN)<br/><br/>(a)& (b) : Yes Sir. This Ministry has categorized the urban poor households earning uptoRs. 1 lakh per annum as Economically Weaker Section (EWS) and those having a household income between Rs. 1-2 lakh as Lower Income Group (LIG) for availing benefits under the schemes being implemented by this Ministry.<br/><br/>(c)  :		These classifications are based on various income and expenditure parameters as well as cost of housing in urban areas viz., growth in Per Capita Income,  minimum wages for non- agricultural Workers, Consumer Price Index , Consumer Food Price Index ,monthly per capita expenditure and  RESIDEX : National Housing Bank (NHB)’s property price tracking index. <br/><br/>(d) :        The households categorized as EWS/LIG will be entitled to capital subsidy as per relevant scheme guideline for Jawaharlal Nehru Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM)/Rajiv AwasYojana (RAY) and interest subsidy under Interest Subsidy Scheme for Housing the Urban Poor (ISHUP) [ being revamped as Rajiv RinnYojana (RRY)]. Also they will be entitled to the houses constructed under Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP) which encourages Public Private Partnership (PPP) model for housing. Thus the increased income criteria will enlarge the set of urban poor who are entitled for housing benefits as stated above. <br/><br/>                    ******

records.qtitle: Cities not covered by air travel
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a) whether many tier-II and tier-III cities of the country are not adequately<br/>covered by air travel;<br/>(b) if so, the details of such cities and towns;<br/>(c) the steps Government has taken to provide proper and affordable air<br/>connectivity to tier-II and tier-III cities; and<br/>(d) the details of the same?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION<br/>(SHRI K. C. VENUGOPAL)<br/><br/>(a) and (b): At present scheduled air services are available to/from 76 airports in<br/>the country.Details are given at Annexure-I.<br/>(c) and (d): Operations in domestic sector have been deregulated and flights are<br/>being operated by concerned airlines on the basis of commercial viability subject<br/>to adherence to Route Dispersal Guidelines laid down by Government in 1994 with<br/>a view to ensure better connectivity to remote regions of the country. According to<br/>these guidelines, all scheduled operators are required to deploy in the North<br/>Eastern region, Jammu & Kashmir, Andaman & Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep<br/>(Category-II routes) at least 10 percent of their deployed capacity on trunk routes<br/>(Category-I routes). Further, at least 10 percent of the capacity thus required to be<br/>deployed on Category-II routes, is required to be deployed for connectivity<br/>exclusively within these regions (Category -II A). All scheduled operators are<br/>required to deploy at least 50 percent of their deployed capacity on trunk routes<br/>(Category-I routes) onto Category III routes.<br/>Further, to enhance regional connectivity in the country, Government introduced a<br/>separate category of Scheduled Air Transport (Regional) Services in 2007.The<br/>Scheduled Regional Operator operates mainly in the region for which they have<br/>been granted permission. However, in operational exigencies, they can connect cities, except metro cities, of other regions also.<br/><br/>                          *****

records.qtitle: Erratic power situation in the country
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether Government has taken note of the erratic power situation across the country, especially in rural areas;<br/><br/>(b) 	if so, the details of the power generation capacity and demand in the country;<br/><br/>(c) 	whether Government has taken step to raise the power generation capacity in the Twelfth Plan; and<br/><br/>(d) 	if so, the details thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF POWER<br/><br/>( SHRI JYOTIRADITYA M. SCINDIA  )<br/> <br/><br/>(a) :		Most of the States/UTs have been facing power shortage in the country.  During the period April, 2012 to March, 2013, the peak and energy shortage in the country including rural areas were 9.0% & 8.7% respectively. However, supply and distribution of electricity in a State/UT is the responsibility of the respective State/UT Government which makes arrangements for supply of power to various categories of consumers / areas (including rural as well as urban) in the State/UT.  <br/><br/>(b) :		The total All India Installed Capacity of electric generating stations as on 31st March, 2013 was 2,23,343.60 MW and the demand was 1,35,453 MW.  <br/><br/>(c) & (d) :	Yes, Sir.  Government has planned Capacity addition of 88,537 MW during 12th Plan period (2012-2017) and instituted processes for rigorous monitoring of capacity addition in the 12th Plan.  Capacity addition in the first year of the 12th Plan is 20,623 MW.   <br/>   	<br/>***********<br/>

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a)	 whether the number of sick Public Sector Enterprises(PSEs) has been on the rise;<br/>(b)	if so, the details thereof;<br/>(c)	whether  Government has taken any steps to revive these sick PSEs;<br/>(d)	if so, the details of the steps taken, expenditure incurred and result thereof, PSE-wise; and<br/>(e)	if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF HEAVY INDUSTRIES AND PUBLIC ENTERPRISES<br/> (SHRI PRAFUL PATEL)<br/><br/><br/>(a) & (b): As per the Public Enterprises Survey: 2011-12, that was laid in the Rajya Sabha on 27.2.2013, and based on the definition of “sickness” given in the Govt. of India Resolution dated 6th December, 2004, constituting Board for Reconstruction of Public Sector Enterprise’s (BRPSE), the number of sick Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) are 63 in 2011-12 as against 81 in 2004-05.<br/>(c) to (e): The Government of India established the Board for Reconstruction of Public Sector Enterprises (BRPSE) in December, 2004 for advising the Government for strengthening, modernizing, reviving, and restructuring of CPSEs. After recommendations of BRPSE, the Government has, upto March, 2013, approved revival of 44 CPSEs envisaging total assistance of Rs. 27249.62 crores as per details given in Annex. In case of 2 sick CPSEs, namely, Bharat Coking Coal Ltd. and Hindustan Fluorocarbons Ltd., their Holding Companies namely, Coal India Ltd. and Hindustan Organic Chemicals Ltd. are implementing the revival plan.  Till March, 2013, 15 sick CPSEs have been declared turnaround which have posted profits consecutively for 3 or more years after the assistance from the Government.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether Government has launched a National Rural Livelihood Mission;<br/>(b) 	if so, the details thereof; and<br/>(c) 	the details of allocation, target and achievement under the Mission during the last two years, State-wise?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SHRI PRADEEP JAIN ‘ADITYA’)<br/><br/>(a)&(b): The Government is implementing National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM) in a mission mode in a phased manner for targeted and time bound delivery of results. NRLM’s mission is to reduce poverty by enabling the poor households to access gainful self-employment and skilled waged employment opportunities resulting in appreciable improvement in their livelihoods on a sustainable basis, through building strong and sustainable grassroots institutions of the poor. NRLM aims to reach out to all the rural poor families (BPL families) and link them to sustainable livelihoods opportunities. It will nurture them till they come out of poverty and enjoy a decent quality of life.  The salient features of the NRLM are:-<br/> (i) 	at least one member from each identified rural poor household, preferably a women, to be brought under the Self Help Group (SHG) network in a time-bound manner, the ultimate target being full coverage of BPL families;<br/>(ii) 	setting up of strong institutions of the poor in the form of SHGs and their federations, Producers Groups etc. for reducing dependence on external agencies;<br/>(iii) 	a multi pronged approach envisaged for continuous capacity building of the targeted families, SHGs, their federations, government functionaries, bankers, Non  Government Organization (NGOs) and other key stakeholders;<br/> (iv)	subsidy to be available in form of revolving fund and capital subsidy as an incentive for inculcating the habit of thrift and accumulation of their own funds towards meeting their credit needs in the long run and immediate consumption needs in the short run;<br/>(v)	Universal financial inclusion of all poor households, SHGs and their federation;<br/>(vi)    in order to ensure affordable credit, the NRLM has a provision for subsidy on interest rates above 7 percent per annum for all eligible SHGs who have availed of loans from mainstream financial institutions, based on prompt loan repayment;<br/>(vii)	to look at stabilizing and enhancing existing livelihoods and subsequently diversifying them;<br/>(viii) to pursue skill up-gradation and placement projects through partnership mode; and<br/>(ix)  to promote convergence with other programmes of the Government<br/><br/>(c):	The Government was earlier implementing the Swarnjayanti Grameen Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) which has been restructured as National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM). In order for the States/Union Territories to transit to NRLM, the following three criteria are required to be met:-<br/><br/>1.	The States should either set-up a society or re-designate an existing society as State Rural Livelihood Mission (SRLM) and place a full time Chief Executive Officer (CEO) to head it.<br/>2.	A multidisciplinary team of professionals should be put in place in the State society and also at various levels in the first phase in districts and blocks.<br/>3.	Prepare a 7 year State Perspective Implementation Plan (SPIP) and Annual Action Plan under NRLM ready.<br/><br/>So far, the Ministry has approved Annual Action Plan of 19 States who have met the above criteria and funds have been released/sanctioned to them. These States are Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Jharkhand, Haryana, Jammu & Kashmir, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Mizoram, Odisha, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal. A statement indicating allocation made under SGSY / NRLM, targets and achievements during the years 2011-12 and 2012-13 is annexed as annexure I.<br/><br/>*********<br/>

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a)     whether Government has taken any step to promote food processing in the country;<br/><br/>(b) 	if so , the details thereof;  and<br/><br/>(c)	how many such food processing industries have been set up in  the past  three years , the details thereof?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES<br/>(DR. CHARAN DAS MAHANT)<br/><br/>(a) to (c): The Government is implementing the Schemes of Infrastructure Development with components i.e. Mega Food Parks; Integrated Cold Chain Projects and Abattoirs; Technology Upgradation/Establishment/Modernization of Food Processing Industries; Quality Assurance, Codex Standard, R&D and other Promotional activities; Human Resource Development; National Mission on Food Processing and Strengthening of Institutions for promotion and development of Food Processing sector in the country.<br/>	<br/>Under the scheme for Technology Upgradation / Establishment / Modernization of Food Processing Industries of XI Plan, the Government extend financial assistance in the form of grant–in– aid to entrepreneurs @ 25 % of the cost of Plant & Machinery and Technical Civil Works subject to a maximum of  Rs. 50 lakhs in general areas and @ 33.33 % subject to a maximum of Rs. 75 lakhs in North-Eastern and difficult areas. <br/><br/>	Further the Government had launched a Centrally Sponsored Scheme – National Mission on Food Processing (NMFP) during 2012-13, the first year of the XII Five Year Plan. The major programmes/Schemes covered under the NMFP during 2012-13 are:-<br/><br/>(i)	Scheme for Technology Upgradation/Establishment/Modernisation of food processing industries<br/>(ii)	Scheme for Cold Chain, Value addition and Preservation of Infrastructure for Non-horticultural Products.<br/>(iii)	Scheme for Human Resource Development (HRD)<br/>(iv)	Scheme for Promotional activities.<br/> <br/>To implement various Schemes for promotion and development of Food Processing Sector, the Government has made a plan allocation of Rs. 5990 crores during the XII Plan.<br/><br/>A statement indicating the number of food processing units assisted during the past three years under the aforesaid scheme is at Annexure.<br/><br/>*****

records.ans_text: MINISTER OF SHIPPING<br/>(SHRI G.K. records.qtitle: Humiliation of passenger by the Airline
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a) whether it is a fact that an ex-major of the Armed forces was humiliated by an<br/>Airline accusing him of security threat because of being of a minority community;<br/>(b) whether it is a fact that he was offloaded along with his baggage;<br/>(c) the number of similar incidents that took place in the recent past; and<br/>(d) the details and what punitive action Government has taken or proposes to take<br/>against the Airline?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION<br/>(SHRI K. C. VENUGOPAL)<br/><br/>(a) and (b): A complaint was received on 13th July 2012 from Ex Major Mohd.<br/>Ali Shah who was to travel from Delhi to Guwahati on 28th June, 2012 by SpiceJet<br/>Flight No. SG 893. As informed by the complainant, he was offloaded at Delhi<br/>Airport.<br/>(c): No such incident has been reported after this incident.<br/>(d): Airlines can not discriminate passengers on the basis of religion, cast, creed<br/>etc. Passengers usually take up such complaints with the airlines concerned. In the<br/>instant case, the complaint received by Directorate General of Civil Aviation<br/>(DGCA) was forwarded to M/s SpiceJet with the direction to resolve the issue.<br/>If found necessary, the DGCA will intervene in the matter.<br/>                         *****

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: 3213. SHRIMATI JAYA BACHCHAN: <br/><br/>Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a) whether Government has taken note of the high Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) in the country;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof;<br/><br/>(c) whether the current infant mortality rate is far more than the target set under the Millennium Development Goals; and<br/><br/>(d) if so, the steps Government has taken to meet the Millennium Development<br/>Goals target on time?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE<br/>(SHRI ABU HASEM KHAN CHOUDHURY)<br/><br/>(a) & (b): Yes. At present, Infant Mortality Rate is 44 per 1000 live births in the country as per Sample Registration System 2011 report of Registrar General of <br/>India.<br/><br/>(c):  The Millennium Development Goal 4 is to   reduce child mortality by two third.<br/><br/>At present India’s IMR stands at 44 per 1000 live births (SRS 2011) against MDG trarget of 28 per 1000 live births. However, 14 States/UTs namely Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Goa, Andaman & Nicobar Islands, Chandigarh, Daman & Diu, Delhi, Lakshadweep, Puducherry, Manipur, Maharashtra, Nagaland, Sikkim and Tripura have already achieved MDG 4 of IMR.<br/>(d): The following interventions under Reproductive and child health programme of NRHM are being implemented to meet the MDGs on time:<br/><br/>1)	Prevention and treatment of Anaemia by supplementation with Iron and Folic Acid tablets during pregnancy and lactation. <br/>2)	Name Based Tracking of Pregnant Women to ensure complete antenatal, intranatal and postnatal care<br/>3)	Operationalizing Community Health Centers as First Referral Units (FRUs) and Primary Health Centers (24X7) for round the clock maternal care services. )<br/>4)	Promotion of Institutional Delivery through Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) and Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK): Promoting Institutional delivery to ensure skilled birth attendance for reducing both maternal and neo-natal mortality. <br/>5)	Strengthening Facility based newborn care: Newborn care corners (NBCC) are being set up at all delivery points. Special Newborn Care Units (SNCUs) and Newborn Stabilization Units (NBSUs) are also being set up at district hospitals and CHCs respectively for the care of sick newborn including preterm babies.<br/>6)	Home Based Newborn Care (HBNC):  Home based newborn care through ASHAs has been initiated to improve new born practices at the community level and early detection and referral of sick newborn babies<br/>7)	Capacity building of health care providers: Various trainings are being conducted under National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) to build and upgrade the skills of health care providers in basic and comprehensive obstetric care of mother during pregnancy, delivery and essential newborn care.<br/>8)	Adolescent Reproductive Sexual Health Programme (ARSH) – for adolescents to have better access to family planning, prevention of sexually transmitted Infections, counselling and peer education.  <br/><br/>9)	A new initiative Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram (RBSK) has been launched on 6th February, 2013 for Child health screening and early intervention services to provide comprehensive care to all the children in the community. The purpose of these services is to improve the overall quality of life of children through early detection of birth defects, diseases, deficiencies, development delays including disability.<br/><br/>

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a)	whether Government has taken note of the poor banking network in rural areas; <br/>(b)	if so, the details of the density of bank branches in rural areas, State-wise;<br/>(c)	whether Government has taken any step to ensure proper access to banking facilities in rural areas; <br/>(d)	if so, the details thereof; and <br/>(e)	if not, the reasons therefor?<br/>
records.ans_text: The Minister of State in the Ministry of Finance<br/>(Shri Namo Narain Meena)<br/> <br/>(a) to (e):- As per Census 2011, 58.7% households reported availing banking services in the country. The percentage of rural population availing banking services was 54.4%, as per Census 2011 as against 30.1%, as per Census 2001. <br/><br/>As on 31st December, 2012 there are 100,277 branches of Scheduled Commercial Banks (SCBs) in the country,  out of which  36,972 (36.9%) bank branches are in the rural areas and 26,595 (26.5%) in semi-urban areas, constituting 63 per cent of the total numbers of branches in semi-urban and rural areas of the country. The State-wise details of number of bank branches functioning in rural areas as on 31st December 2012 is given in Annex.<br/> <br/>The Government and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) are taking various initiatives from time to time to expand banking network in the country. Under `Swabhimaan” campaign of the Government, banking facilities to over 74,000 unbanked habitations having population in excess of 2000 have been provided during 2010-12.  <br/><br/>The RBI under its Branch Authorization Policy has permitted domestic SCBs (excluding Regional Rural Banks) to open branches in Tier 2 to Tier 6 centres (with population upto 99,999 as per census 2001) without the need to take permission from RBI subject to reporting. The domestic SCBs have also been advised that while preparing their Annual Branch Expansion Plan, they should allocate at least 25% of the total number of branches proposed to be opened during a year in unbanked rural centres with population upto 9999). <br/><br/>The RRBs are also permitted to open branches in Tier 2 to Tier 6 centres without having the need to take permission from RBI in each case, subject to reporting, provided they fulfill certain conditions prescribed by RBI.<br/><br/>*****<br/> <br/>Annex		<br/>

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a)	the targets under the first phase of Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission;<br/><br/>(b)	whether Government has taken any initiative to provide solar power devices, i.e. solar heater, solar cookers, solar lights etc. in rural areas;<br/><br/>(c)	if so, the details thereof; and<br/>(d)	if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY<br/>(DR. FAROOQ ABDULLAH)<br/><br/>(a):	The target under the first phase of Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission are: <br/>(i)	1000 MW Grid Connected Power Plants<br/>(ii)	200 MW off grid solar applications<br/>(iii)	7 Million Sq m Solar Thermal collector area<br/>(b)&(c):	Yes, Sir. Under off-gird and Decentralized Solar Applications scheme of Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission, the Ministry provides a subsidy of 30% of the cost of the solar lighting systems, solar water heating systems and solar cookers. The subsidy is limited to Rs. 81/- per watt peak for solar lighting systems, Rs. 3000-3300/- per square meter of collector areas for solar water heating systems and Rs. 3600/- per square meter of collector areas for solar cookers for installation of systems in the country including  rural areas. <br/><br/>(d):	Does not arise<br/>******

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a)	whether there has been demand for voting by the overseas Indians recently;<br/>(b)	whether Government has any plan to provide voting rights to the People of Indian Origin or Non-Resident Indians (NRIs);<br/>(c) if so, the details thereof; and<br/>(d) if not, the  reasons therefor?
records.ans_text: A N S W E R<br/><br/>MINISTER OF LAW AND JUSTICE<br/>(DR. ASHWANI KUMAR)<br/><br/>(a) to (c): Under section 20A of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 every citizen   of India:—<br/>(a) whose name is not included in the electoral roll;<br/>(b) who has not acquired the citizenship of any other country; and<br/>(c) who is absenting from his place of ordinary residence in India owing to his employment, education or otherwise outside India (whether temporarily or not), <br/>is entitled to have his name registered in the electoral roll in the constituency in which his place of residence in India as mentioned in his passport is located. -<br/><br/>(c):	The following steps are being taken by the Government to ensure uninterrupted supply of fertilizers to the farmers:-<br/><br/><br/>(a)	The month-wise demand is assessed and projected fertilizers for streamlining the supplies through timely placement of indents for railway rakes through their state institutional agencies like Markfed etc.<br/><br/>iii)	Regular weekly Video records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a)	whether Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is planning to launch its own Global Positioning System;<br/><br/>(b)	if so, the details of the same;<br/><br/>(c)	the details of the expenditure incurred on the projects; and<br/><br/>(d)	the details of the benefit of such a project?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PG & PENSIONS AND IN THE PRIME MINISTER’S OFFICE<br/>(SHRI V.NARAYANASAMY):<br/><br/>(a) & (b)	No,  Sir. Indian Space Research Organization (ISRO) is not planning to launch its own Global Positioning System. However, ISRO is developing an indigenous regional navigation system known as Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (IRNSS) with a constellation of seven satellites which will provide positioning and navigational services in Indian mainland and surrounding region upto 1500 Km.<br/><br/>(c)	The estimated budget for realization of seven satellites with two ground spare satellites and the associated ground segment is Rs.1420 Crore, the launch cost of the seven satellites using PSLV is Rs.630 Crore totalling to Rs.2050 Crore.<br/><br/>(d)	IRNSS ensures availability of reliable positioning and navigational services within the country. Some of the areas where IRNSS can be used are for civil aviation, high sea and inland waterway navigation, rail transport, offshore exploration, patrol services and fleet monitoring.<br/><br/>***

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN POVERTY ALLEVIATION be pleased to state: <br/>(a)	whether  it is a fact that the National Association of Street Vendors of India has been demanding certain safeguards/protections for their survival;<br/>(b)	the details of the demands of the Association and the time since when pending with Government; and <br/>(c)	Government’s response to the demand and the details in this regard?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF HOUSING AND URBAN POVERTY ALLEVIATION<br/><br/>     (SHRI AJAY MAKEN)<br/><br/>(a) to (c) :  The Ministry of Housing & Urban Poverty Alleviation has been receiving representations from various hawkers’ associations including National Association of Street Vendors of India  demanding for the safeguards/protections of the street vendors.<br/><br/>In order to protect the rights of urban street vendors and to regulate street vending activities, The Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Bill, 2012 was introduced in Lok Sabha on 6th September, 2012. Hon’ble Speaker, Lok Sabha had referred the Bill to the Standing Committee on Urban Development for examination. The Standing Committee on Urban Development has tabled its report in the Parliament on 13.3.2013.  <br/>                          *******

records.qtitle: Special tribunal in all districts for settling fire and other manmade disaster cases
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a) whether it is a fact that Government is considering to bring in a legislation by creating special tribunals in all the 640 districts of the country to settle cases of compensation pertaining to fire and other manmade disasters;<br/><br/>(b) whether the National Advisory Council (NAC) has sought a comprehensive law on safety of victims; and<br/><br/>(c) what are the details in this regard?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI MULLAPPALLY RAMACHANDRAN)<br/><br/>(a):   No Sir. <br/><br/>(b) & (c):   A representation from the Association of the victims of the Uphaar tragedy on the issue, forwarded by National Advisory Council(NAC), was received by the Ministry of Home Affairs.  The matter has been examined in detail in consultation with various departments/ministries. Government has noted the fact that there are provisions in various Acts for payment of compensation like Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010 and Railway Act, 1989 etc., Government also noted that there are fundamental differences in road accidents on the one hand and the fire accidents/man-made disasters on the other.  Unlike the former, it is not possible in the latter to pin-point any particular offender right at the beginning without due enquiry.   In view of these reasons, it has been decided not to frame a separate law to deal with man-made disasters or to set up special tribunals.   <br/><br/>********<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Shutting down of OVLs operation in Sudan and South Sudan
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a)   the reasons for shutting oil production by ONGC Videsh Limited (OVL) at Greater Nile Petroleum Project in Sudan and South Sudan in this year;<br/>(b)  whether OVL proposes to resume the production soon, after the resolution of the dispute: and<br/>(c)    the details thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS<br/>(SMT. PANABAAKA LAKSHMI)<br/>(a) South Sudan seceded from Sudan with effect from 9th July, 2011.  South Sudan is a land locked country and oil produced in South Sudan was exported using the transportation facilities of Sudan.  Normal petroleum operation continued in both Sudan and South Sudan till December, 2011. The Government of South Sudan enforced shut down of oil production from fields in South Sudan in January, 2012 due to failure of negotiations between both the governments to agree on the charges for transportation, transit fee and processing of South Sudan oil through facilities of Sudan.<br/>	<br/>(b) and (c): Yes, Sir.  ONGC Videsh Limited(OVL) is looking forward for resumption of production from South Sudan as soon as direction from the Government of South Sudan and Sudan are received. <br/>	<br/>Sudan and South Sudan have signed an Oil Agreement in September, 2012 wherein charges for transportation, transit fee and processing charges have been agreed to.<br/>However, certain other security and border related issued remain to be sorted out so that production can be commenced from South Sudan.	<br/><br/>******

records.qtitle: Levy of service tax on film fraternity
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government has levied service tax on artists and film fraternity;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof;<br/><br/>(c) whether Government has taken note of the protests by artists against this tax;<br/><br/>(d) whehter Government plans to withdraw these taxes;<br/><br/>(e) if so, the details thereof; and<br/><br/>(f) if not, the reasons therefor?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE<br/>(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM)<br/><br/>(a) & (b) : (i) With effect from 01.07.2012, new comprehensive approach of taxation of services based on negative list has been introduced. In the said approach all the services are subjected to service tax except<br/>•	services mentioned in the negative list <br/>•	services exempted from service tax  <br/>(ii) Specific exemptions given in relation to artists and film industry, are as follows:<br/>•	Services by a performing artist in folk or classical art forms of music, dance or theatre<br/>•	Services in relation to use of copyright for original literary, dramatic, musical & artistic work<br/> Other services of the artists have become taxable with effect from 01.07.2012 subject to threshold limit of Rs. 10 lakh per annum for such artists.<br/><br/>(c): Yes, sir<br/><br/>(d), (e) & (f): The government has already granted relief by restricting the exemption on temporary transfer of copyright of cinematograph film for exhibition in a cinema hall or a cinema theatre only w.e.f. 01.04.2013.  This would reduce the cost of film as the film producers can pass on the input tax credit for discharging the tax liability on their output services of temporary transfer of copyright of such films for TV/satellite broadcasting.<br/><br/>********<br/>

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: GOVERNMENT OF INDIA<br/>MINISTRY OF EARTH SCIENCES<br/>RAJYA SABHA<br/>STARRED QUESTION No. *286<br/>TO BE ANSWERED ON MONDAY, MARCH 18, 2013<br/><br/>MODERNIZATION OF INDIAN METEOROLOGICAL DEPARTMENT<br/><br/>*286. SHRIMATI JAYA BACHCHAN: <br/><br/>          Will the Minister of EARTH SCIENCES be pleased to state: <br/><br/>(a)	whether the current weather forecasting system in the country is equivalent to International standards;<br/>(b)	whether Government has any plan to modernize the Indian Meteorological Department (IMD);<br/>(c)	if so, the details thereof; and<br/>(d)	if not, the reasons therefor?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>MINISTER FOR MINISTRY OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY AND<br/>MINISTRY OF EARTH SCIENCES<br/>(SHRI S. JAIPAL REDDY)<br/><br/>(a) to (d): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. <br/> <br/>STATEMENT LAID ON THE TABLE OF THE RAJYA SABHA IN REPLY (a) to (d) TO STARRED QUESTION NO. *286 REGARDING “MODERNIZATION OF INDIAN METEOROLOGICAL DEPARTMENT” TO BE ANSWERED <br/>ON MONDAY, MARCH 18, 2013 <br/><br/>(a)	Yes Sir. The weather forecasting systems in the country are comparable to most of the countries in the world with respect to rainfall forecasting. Efforts are being made to optimize the level of efficiency of the forecasting systems.<br/><br/>(b)	Yes Sir. Earth System Science Organization (ESSO) - IMD has already implemented Phase-I of the Modernization during 2007-12.<br/><br/>(c)	Under the Phase-I of the modernization of ESSO - IMD, the following state-of-the-art systems were commissioned:<br/><br/>•	Observing systems such as Automatic Weather Stations (AWS), Automatic Rain Gauges (ARG), Doppler Weather Radars (DWR) etc.<br/>•	Monitoring/early warning systems<br/>•	Analysis-visualization-product dissemination systems<br/>•	High Performance Computing (HPC) <br/>•	Communication/IT systems<br/>•	Real-time data assimilation-forecast systems etc. <br/><br/>Further, several manual operations have been fully automated. All the scientific staff engaged earlier have been provided due training to develop appropriate skills for customization of sector specific (like agriculture, aviation etc.) warning and forecasting services. <br/><br/>In order to capture the characteristics of the severe weather in real time, 24X7 monitoring system comprising 675 Nos. of AWSs; 1024 Nos. of ARGs; 17 S and C-Band DWRs have been commissioned at Chennai, Sriharikota, Machilipatnam, Visakhapatnam, Kolkata, Mumbai, Bhuj, Hyderabad, Nagpur, Patiala, Delhi Palam, Lucknow, Patna, Mohanbari, Agartala, Delhi Lodi Road and Jaipur.  Only DWR at Bhopal is under commissioning.   <br/><br/>High Performance Computing (HPC) systems have been used to enhance the weather forecasting capacities by assimilating all available global satellite data for forecast generation.  The global model that was earlier run at 50Km grid scale are now run at 22Km grid. The regional scale model run earlier at 27Km grid is replaced by 9Km and 3Km grid scale models. The accuracy of short range (up to 3-days in advance) monsoon forecasts has improved from 50-60% to 70-95%. The skill of district level medium range rainfall forecast (up to 5-7days in advance) has improved from 60-70% to 75-85% in monsoon season and  from 70-75% to 85% in non-monsoon seasons.  <br/><br/>As far as the track and landfall forecasts of the tropical cyclones are concerned, the performance evaluation of the updated forecast systems for the past 5-years, have demonstrated enhanced forecast skill by about 18%.  ESSO-IMD currently operates 5- Doppler Weather Radars (DWR) at Chennai, Machilipatnam, Visakhapatnam, Kolkata, Sriharikota on the east coast along with a network of Automatic Weather Stations (AWS) and Automatic Rain Gauges (ARG) for continuous weather surveillance over the Bay of Bengal. <br/><br/>ESSO-IMD has operationalized its location specific nowcasting (near real-time) weather service for severe weather (Thunderstorms; heavy rainfall from lows/depressions over the land) across the country. This service activity currently covers 117 urban centres on experimental basis under which nowcast of 3-6hour range is issued. Origin, development/movement of severe weather phenomena are regularly monitored through DWRs and with all other available observing systems.<br/>	<br/>Integrated Agro-meteorological Advisory Service (AAS) is rendered now on twice-weekly basis in collaboration with State Agricultural Universities (SAUs), institutions of Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), etc. District level weather forecast for next 5-days in respect of:<br/><br/>•	Rainfall<br/>•	maximum temperature, minimum temperature, <br/>•	wind speed, wind direction, <br/>•	relative humidity and clouds <br/>•	weekly cumulative rainfall forecast <br/><br/>are provided. Further, crop specific advisories to help the farmers are issued and widely disseminated. The AAS of ESSO-IMD has been successful in providing the crop specific advisories to the farmers through different print/visual/Radio/ IT based media including short message service (SMS) and Interactive Voice Response Service (IVRS) facilitating for appropriate field level actions. <br/><br/>(d)	Does not arise.<br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan

No.	Class	Increase in Fare in (paisa per PKM) <br/>		<br/> 	 <br/>1	Second Class Ordinary (Suburban)    2 Paise <br/>2	Second Class Ordinary (Non-Suburban)3 Paise <br/>3	Second Class (Mail / Express)	    4 Paise <br/>4	Sleeper Class 	                    6 Paise <br/>5	AC Chair Car 	                   10 Paise <br/>6	AC 3-Tier 	                   10 Paise <br/>7	First Class 	                    3 Paise <br/>8	AC 2-Tier 	                    6 Paise <br/>9	AC First Class 	                   10 Paise <br/><br/>With a view to rationally insulate Railways’ finances, particularly in the context of deregulation of High Speed Diesel (HSD) oil, it has been proposed to introduce a dynamic pricing mechanism for adjusting tariffs in sync with movements in fuel cost in either direction, say twice a year, in the Railway Budget for 2013-14, Presently the proposal entails implementation of the Fuel Adjustment Component (FAC) – linked revision only in the case of freight tariffs with effect from 1st April 2013. SINGH)<br/><br/>(a):	Yes, Sir.<br/><br/>(b):	Yes, Sir.<br/><br/>(c):   The State/UT-Wise details are attached at Annexure. records.qtitle: Promotion of SEZs in backward regions
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: <br/>a)	whether Government has taken note of the backwardness of few regions in terms of industrialization;<br/><br/>b)	the details of such regions identified by Government;<br/><br/>c)	whether Government has taken any steps to promote new Special Economic Zones in such areas;<br/><br/>d)	if so, the details thereof; and<br/><br/>e)	if not, the reasons therefor?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY<br/>(DR. D. PURANDESWARI)<br/><br/>(a)	to (e):	  While backward regions are not defined under Special Economic Zones (SEZs) Act, 2005 and Rules framed there under, however, Rule 5(2) of the SEZ Rules, 2006 prescribes a lower minimum land area requirement for setting up of a multi-product and a specific sector SEZ in Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram, Manipur, Tripura, Himachal Pradesh, Uttaranchal, Sikkim, Jammu and Kashmir, Goa or in a Union Territory.  Further, the said Rules prescribe a lower minimum built up area requirement in respect of the SEZs located in B1 and B2 category cities as per classification indicated in Annexure IV of the SEZ Rules.<br/><br/>The Government, on the basis of inputs/suggestions invited from stakeholders has reviewed the policy and operational framework governed by the Rules of the Special Economic Zone (SEZ) scheme and is presently engaged in inter-ministerial consultations for finalization of a proposal for SEZ policy and operational framework reform through necessary changes in the Rules, targeting a more investor friendly environment and smoother operation of the SEZ scheme. <br/><br/>*************<br/><br/>

records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS<br/>(SMT. PANABAAKA LAKSHMI)<br/>(a): Yes, Sir.  ONGC Videsh Limited(OVL) is planning to participate in the Exploration Bid Rounds of Myanmar and Sri Lanka.<br/><br/>(b):  Earlier, OVL had submitted proposals to Sri Lanka for allotting Exploration Blocks M1 and M3 in Mannar Basin part and C1-C5 in Cauvery Basin Part of Offshore Sri Lanka.  However, in recently announced Exploration Bidding Round these blocks have been included for open bidding.<br/><br/>(c): ONGC Videsh Limited(OVL): OVL is having Exploration Blocks in Cuba, Columbia, Brazil, Libya, Nigeria, Kazakhstan and Iraq.  OVL is having blocks in Venezuela, Syria and Myanmar for Exploitation (Development Projects). <br/>OVL is having producing projects in Russia, Syria, Vietnam, Colombia, Sudan, South Sudan, Venezuela and Brazil.	<br/><br/>Oil India Limited(OIL): OIL is involved in exploration and exploitation of oil and gas in nine countries, namely USA, Venezuela, Libya, Gabon, Iran, Yemen, Nigeria, Egypt and Timor Leste.<br/><br/>Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL): Presently IOCL has participating interests in 10 overseas Exploration and Production (E&P) blocks viz. three in Libya, two in Yemen and one each in Iran, Gabon, Nigeria, Venezuela and USA.<br/><br/>GAIL (India) Limited:  GAIL is currently participating in two blocks namely A-1 and A-3 in Mynamar where gas discoveries is being made and GAIL is the Non-Operating partner with 8.5% Participating Interest(PI).<br/><br/>Bharat Petro Resources Limited(BPRL):  BPRL a 100% subsidiary of Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited(BPCL) has PI in 14 Exploration Blocks in five countries, viz. Brazil, Mozambique, Indonesia, East Timor and Australia.  <br/><br/>Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited(HPCL):  HPCL had acquired blocks in Oman(Block 56), Australia (WA-388-P) and Egypt (South Sinai & South Quesir) for exploration and production of oil and gas.<br/><br/>(d):  It is always beneficial to the countries to get the hydrocarbon blocks in other countries. <br/>•	To support India’s energy security;<br/>•	To build balanced portfolio of exploration, discovered and producing assets in focus countries; and<br/>•	To build a team that excels in performance through assimilation of best practice and technologies through knowledge sharing with the experts of International Oil Companies(IOCs).<br/><br/>*******<br/><br/><br/>	<br/><br/><br/><br/>

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether Government has undertaken any study to find out the level of contamination in underground water;<br/><br/>(b) 	if so, the details thereof;<br/><br/>(c) 	if not, the reasons therefor; and<br/><br/>(d) 	the steps Government has taken to provide safe drinking water in these areas? <br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF DRINKING WATER AND SANITATION<br/>(SHRI BHARATSINH SOLANKI)<br/><br/>(a)to(d): The State Governments have been advised to test for chemical contamination in drinking water sources at least once in a year and for bacteriological  contamination atleast twice in a year.   States enter reports on the IMIS about the quality affected habitations that have been identified by them through by regular testing of drinking water sources in water quality testing laboratories.  As reported by the State Governments on the online Integrated Management Information System (IMIS) of the Ministry, as on 1/4/2012, there were 1.04 lakh rural water quality affected habitations with excess chemical contamination in one or more of their drinking water sources that were remaining to be covered with safe drinking water supply in the country.  The State/UT-wise number of remaining water quality affected habitations as on 1/4/2012 is at Annexure. <br/><br/>Rural water supply is a State subject. This Ministry supplements the efforts of the States by providing them with technical and financial assistance under the centrally sponsored National Rural Drinking Water Programme (NRDWP) for providing safe and adequate drinking water supply facilities in rural areas of the country. A budgetary allocation of Rs.10,500 crore has been made for the NRDWP in 2012-13. Up to 67 per cent of the NRDWP funds allocated to States on 50:50 Centre: State sharing basis (90:10 for North-East States and Jammu & Kashmir) can be utilized for provision of safe drinking water in rural areas of the country. Further, 5% of NRDWP funds are earmarked and allocated on 50:50 Centre: State sharing basis (90:10 for North East States and Jammu & Kashmir) to those States facing problems of chemical contamination in drinking water or with Japanese Encephalitis or Acute Encephalitis Syndrome affected high priority districts. Further up to 10 per cent of NRDWP funds allocated to States could be utilized for sustainability of drinking water sources through artificial recharge of ground water and other methods, which   may also dilute the level of contamination in aquifers. In addition, 3% of the NRDWP funds allocated to the States are earmarked for Water Quality Monitoring and Surveillance (WQMS) activities on a 100% Central share basis   which, inter alia, includes testing of drinking water sources at the Panchayat level by using simple field test kits, setting up of new district/sub-district water quality testing laboratories and upgrading of existing water quality testing laboratories. <br/><br/>

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan

Implementation of RKVY has resulted in enhancing allocation for agriculture & allied sectors by the States from Rs.8770.16 crore (4.88%) in 2006-07 to Rs.29413.12 crore (6.82%) in 2011-12 (RE).<br/><br/>	A statement indicating the State-wise funds allocated, released and expenditure reported by the States during the last three years and current year as on 28th February is annexed.	<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Change in criminal law in anti dowry laws
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a) whether it is a fact that Government expert panel has recommended a change in the criminal law in the anti-dowry laws;<br/><br/>(b) whether it is also a fact that section 498A of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and enabling laws require amendments following reports of their misuse;<br/><br/>(c) whether courts and other Committees have emphasized the need for caution in exercising the drastic power of arrest under section 498A of IPC; and<br/><br/>(d) if so, the details in this regard and the action likely to be taken thereon?<br/>
records.ans_text: (a) to (d)	The Law Commission of India, in its 243rd Report, has recommended amendments to section 498A, making it non-bailable and compoundable. The Hon''ble Committee on Petitions of Rajya Sabha, in its 140th  Report also recommended, inter-alia, effective steps to be taken by State Governments to curb misuse of section 498A of IPC. As the subject matter comes under the ambit of the Concurrent List of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India, the matter has to be consulted with the State Governments / Union Territory Administrations. The Report of the Law Commission has, therefore, been referred to all the State Governments/ UT Administrations for their views. Accordingly, an advisory has been issued to all the State Governments/ UT Administrations on 16.01.2012. <br/><br/><br/><br/>***** <br/>

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: 2701. SHRIMATI JAYA BACHCHAN: <br/><br/>Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a) whether it is a fact that over ten thousand children have died during the last<br/>five years in the Kalawati Saran Hospital in New Delhi alone;<br/><br/>(b) the number of children died during the same period in the country;<br/><br/>(c) the number of children died due to the negligence of doctors or the Para-medical staff and due to the mal-functioning of the ventilator or other such equipments; and<br/><br/>(d) the reasons for such a large number of deaths of children and the steps taken<br/>by Government to save the children? <br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE<br/>(SHRI GHULAM NABI AZAD)<br/><br/>(a):	 During 2008, 2009, 2010, 2011 and upto 31st July, 2012, out of the 1,37,078 admitted children 10,081 children died in the Kalwati Saran Children Hospital (KSCH).<br/><br/>(b):	Since the Public Health is a State Subject; no such information is maintained centrally. However, as far as other two Central Government Hospitals in Delhi namely, Safdarjung Hospital and Dr. RML Hospital are concerned, 1034 children and 5960 children died in Dr. RML Hospital and Safdarjung Hospital respectively during the last five years.<br/>(c):	In so far as three Central Government Hospitals in Delhi, viz. Safdarjung Hospital, Dr. RML Hospital and LHMC & associated Hospitals are concerned, no children died due to the negligence of doctors or the Paramedical staff and due to the mal-functioning of the ventilator or other such equipments.<br/>(d):	 There are various common causes for above stated deaths in KSCH which include preterm & other ill-defined condition in perinatal period; Bronchopneumonia & other respiratory infection; Neonatal septicemia & other septicemia; Meningitis & meningococcal infection; Intestinal infections & other diseases; occurrence of more than 50% of these deaths within 1st 48 hours of admission indicating that these patients were brought late and in a critical condition; receiving extremely sick infants from referral by Hospitals of Delhi and neighboring States, etc. For modifiable causes i.e. infections advanced antibodies are being used and best of care being provided using high end equipments like warmers, ventilators monitors etc.   Government is also providing assistance for capacity building of health care providers in basic and comprehensive obstetric care; name based tracking of pregnant women to ensure antenatal; intra-natal and postnatal care; launch of new initiative namely Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakaram; etc., which provide timely treatment of women and infants near their home and improved access to health care and early referral of sick children which can also reduce mortality.<br/><br/>

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: <br/><br/>       (a)	whether it is a fact that a former Additional Solicitor General has criticized the manner in 	which cases are handed over to the law officers and the interest of Government is jeopardized;<br/>       (b)	whether it is also a fact that the cases were handed over to the law officers just a few minutes before the time of hearing in the courts; and <br/>       (c)	whether Government would act in such a way that its interests are not jeopardized financially and otherwise?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/><br/>MINISTER OF LAW AND JUSTICE<br/>(DR. ASHWANI KUMAR)<br/><br/>(a) to (c)	Yes, Sir. However, it is denied that the interest of Government is jeopardized. Efforts are being continuously made to enhance efficiency in the conduct of Government litigation in courts, for example:<br/><br/>(i)	All important cases are identified in advance & urgent steps are taken to brief the Law Officers and Senior Counsels alongwith panel counsels & officers from the concerned Departments so that interest of Government is safeguarded;<br/><br/>(ii)	Paper books are completed with documents collected from counsel for opposite side as well as from Supreme Court registry where some documents are missing;<br/><br/>(iii)	Weekly list matters are sent well in advance so that effective representation is made at the time of hearing;<br/><br/>(iv)	Contractual staff have been hired by Department of revenue (CBDT & CBEC) & posted in Central Agency to overcome the shortage of manpower in Central Agency Section to some extent;<br/><br/>(v)	Legal Cells of CBDT, CBEC, Ministry of Defence and Legal Cells of all the paramilitary forces like BSF, CISF and CRPF are functioning & cases are monitored on daily basis by them in co-ordination with the Central Agency Section?<br/>

records.qtitle: Loss of foodgrains due to faulty storage
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.min_name: CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
records.qn_text: (a) 	the quantum of foodgrains lost due to faulty storage system during the last three years, year-wise and the estimated loss of revenue as a result thereof;<br/><br/>(b) 	whether it is a fact that Madhya Pradesh has faced a pressing shortage of bags;<br/><br/>(c) 	whether it is a fact that silo bags and inflatable balloon warehouse, a technically advanced form of storing grains has been developed in the country recently;<br/><br/>(d) 	whether it is a fact that the said bags could help curb grain wastage to a great extent;<br/><br/>(e) 	whether Government would use such bags and warehouse in future to avert the losses of foodgrains; and<br/><br/>(f) 	what are the details in this regard?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD & PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION<br/>(PROF. K.V. THOMAS)<br/><br/>(a):	 Foodgrain losses are not allowed to occur due to faulty storage system.  However, some losses may occur during storage of foodgrains due to loss of moisture, spillage, pest infestation, birds, rodents, thefts, exposure to rains, floods, negligence on the part of concern persons in taking precautionary measures etc..  In case of negligence of officials, action is taken against them invariably.  Details of foodgrains lost alongwith value during the last three years due to storage loss and theft /pilferage, as reported by FCI are as under:<br/><br/>Year		Storage loss *	Theft/pilferage <br/>	Quantity<br/>(lakh tons)	Value of Loss<br/>(Rs.in crores)	Quantity<br/>(Tons)	Amount<br/>(Rs.)<br/>2008-09	0.58	101.31	1.15	17422<br/>2009-10	1.31	228.36	34.02	486227<br/>2010-11	1.56	292.91	9.05	89100<br/>2011-12	1.57	321.55	14.01	376291<br/> <br/>* Figures for 2010-11 and 2011-12 are provisional.<br/>...2/-<br/><br/>...2...<br/><br/><br/>(b):	The requirement of bags was made available to the State of Madhya Pradesh.  For Rabi Marketing Season (RMS), 2012-13, Government of Madhya Pradesh initially placed an indent with DGS&D for supply of only 1.44 lakh bales for procurement of wheat.  Subsequently, indents for 1.25 lakh bales and additional 50,000 bales were placed by the State Government with DGS&D belatedly in April and May, 2012 respectively.  The entire indented quantity of 2.69 lakh bales of jute bags and another 17,260 bales against additional indent was supplied to Government of Madhya Pradesh by June, 2012.  In addition to this permission to use 40,000 new HDPE/PP bags and 4379 old HDPE/PP for wheat procurement was also given to the State Government.  The State Government had also purchased jute bags directly from market through open tenders.  The requirement of bags to procure revised estimates of 80 lakh tons against the initial estimate of 65 lakh tons by Government of Madhya Pradesh was made available.  <br/><br/>(c), (d), (e) & (f):	Silo bags or inflatable balloon warehouse for foodgrain storage is hermetically sealed storage system which ensures bulk mechanical handling and storage of foodgrains.  Silo bags storage system can be deployed at farm level, mandi level and in open fields.  Although, hermetic storage of foodgrains is very old technique and has been used in different ways from a long time.  In India it is currently introduce in the form of polyethylene silo bags for storage of wheat.  Silo bags are polyethylene bag with a measurement of 60 meters in length, 2.75 meters in diameter and 220 micron thickness.  Its laminated plastic sheet is made of three layers of co-extruded polyethylene.  The first two layers make the bag weather proof and act as a Ultra Violet (UV) filter and the third layer is black in colour and protects the grain from sunlight.  <br/><br/>A Study to find out the suitability of Silo bags for the safe storage of wheat in open complex was undertaken by Indian Grain Storage Management and Research Institute (IGMRI), Hapur in FCI depots in Delhi and Punjab.  The results after one year of storage of wheat of Rabi Marketing Season (RMS), 2011-12 in silo bags indicate that there was no variation in average moisture content in stored wheat and no live insects were observed in the silo bags.  The overall grain quality was found good upto one year of storage period.  The study has been extended for one more year and will complete in October, 2013.<br/><br/>Government of Madhya Pradesh has stored about 20,000 tons of wheat in silo bags at two locations during RMS 2012-13 on a pilot projects basis.<br/>***<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Off the air GSM monitoring equipments
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether nearly 51 private companies are under the Government scanner for importing passive "off -the-air" interceptive devices;<br/><br/>(b) 	whether Telecom Department has served show-cause notices to these companies and has asked them to surrender such devices;<br/><br/>(c) 	whether any of Government Departments is having such devices and if so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor;<br/><br/>(d) 	whether according to Government notice, use of "off-the-air" GSM monitoring equipments is illegal;<br/><br/>(e)	 number of companies that did not comply with Government instruction to surrender such equipments; and<br/><br/>(f)	 reasons for allowing import of such equipments and the details thereof?
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY<br/> (SHRI KAPIL SIBAL)<br/><br/><br/>(a) to (f)	A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.<br/><br/><br/>STATEMENT TO BE LAID ON THE TABLE OF RAJYA SABHA IN RESPECT OF PARTS (a) TO (f) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.*307 FOR 14th DECEMBER, 2012, ON “OFF-THE-AIR GSM MONITORING EQUIPMENTS”.<br/><br/>(a) & (b) : Sir, a list of equipment, imported by private agencies during 2007-2010, containing details of import of multi channel GSM/CDMA receiver, transmitter and trans-receivers, compiled by Central Board of Excise and Customs was forwarded by Ministry of Home Affairs to Department of Telecommunications for examination.  During scrutiny, it came to notice that such kind of multi channel GSM /CDMA receivers, transmitter and trans-receivers are dual use items which can be used in normal mobile Base Transceiver stations (BTS) for legitimate operations of Telecom Service Providers and others. Equipment like mobile phones, filters etc were also included in the said list. <br/><br/>	Since, no private agency so far has confirmed or found to have imported ‘off-the-air monitoring equipment’, therefore, no show-cause notice has been issued to any private agency.<br/><br/>(c) : In order to sensitize the State Government and other Law Enforcement Agencies (LEAs), Union Home Secretary had a meeting with all Chief Secretaries and Directors General of Police on 31.05.2011 and directed to make special efforts to locate and seize such equipment which has no authorization. One of the central designated agencies has been nominated to take safe custody of such equipment from Government law enforcement agencies, if any.<br/><br/>(d) : The monitoring of telephone conversation is governed by the provisions of Section 5(2) of Indian Telegraph Act, 1885 and guided by Rule 419A of Indian Telegraph (Amendment), Rules 2007. Thus, unauthorized use of any equipment including ‘Off-the-air monitoring equipment’ for interception and monitoring is illegal.<br/><br/>(e) & (f) : As per the verification carried out so far, no case from any company regarding availability of ‘Off-the-air monitoring equipments’ and usage thereof, could be established. But, taking cognizance of the risk posed by such equipment, the equipment which could be used to tap the communication off-the air have been moved to ‘Restrictive List’ from the ‘Open General Licence’ (OGL) list vide Department of Commerce notification No. 53/2009-14 dated 15-07-2010.<br/><br/><br/>**********

records.qtitle: Study model to allow students free time in schools
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a)  whether it is a fact that Government of Kerala has come out with a study model to allow students to bunk the classes to spend time on innovative ideas; <br/><br/>(b)  whether it is also a fact that such students would get certain concessions in attendance and some extra marks to their total scores at the end of the academic year; and<br/><br/>(c) whether Central Government is considering to implement such proposals all over the country and if so, the details in this regard?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT<br/>(DR. SHASHI THAROOR)<br/>(a) & (b)   The Department of Education, Government of Kerala has evolved a strategy to engage school children in creative and innovative ideas, as an additional/extended learning activity without affecting the learning hours as envisaged in the Right to Education (RTE) Act. Grace marks ranging from 18-30 are added at the end of the academic year to promote children to spend time on innovative ideas. <br/><br/>(c)	Education is in the concurrent list and it is for the respective State Governments to frame policies in such matters. However, the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE), an autonomous body under the Ministry of Human Resource Development (HRD), has implemented the scheme of Continuous and Comprehensive Evaluation (CCE). Under the CCE, a candidate has to undergo assessments in Scholastic as well as Co-Scholastic Areas such as Life Skills, Attitudes & Values, Participation & Achievement in activities involving Literacy & Creative Skills, Scientific Skills, Aesthetic Skills and Performing Arts, etc. <br/><br/>*******

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan

records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT<br/>( SMT. DEEPA DASMUNSI )<br/><br/>(a) &(b): 	 DDA has informed that a water cycling plant is proposed at its office in  Vikas Sadan.  Being at planning stage, the quantity of water likely to be salvaged per day at the proposed plant is being worked out.<br/>(c)&(d):	DDA has also informed that in case of new Group Housing Societies it has been made mandatory to provide dual pipe system and mini sewage treatment plant within the premises for treatment of sewage and utilizing the treated water for the purpose other than for drinking.<br/>******
