DEEPA DASMUNSI)<br/><br/>(a)	to (c) : There is no such proposal nor any survey has been conducted by Ministry.  However, the guidelines issued by Ministry of Urban Affairs & Employment vide letter D.O. No. K-13011/17/86-DDIIA dated 08.02.1988  and as clarified by Ministry of Urban Development from time to time are applicable for any construction in Lutyens Bungalow Zone.<br/><br/>**********

records.qtitle: Anganwadis working in their own buildings
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a)	the number of Anganwadis that are functioning as on date and the number out of them functioning in their own buildings;<br/>(b)	the number of Anganwadi likely to be constructed in near future and the estimated cost thereof; <br/>(c)	whether the children of the women working under Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) would be given any facilities there; and <br/>(d)	what are the details in this regard ?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT <br/>(SHRIMATI KRISHNA TIRATH)<br/><br/>(a):    	As on 31.10.2012, 13,19,097 Anganwadis (AWCs)/ Mini-AWCs are functioning in the country.  As per information available for 11,98,607 AWC buildings, 3,58,970 AWC buildings are functioning from Government Buildings, 2,57,081 from School premises and 42,232 from Panchayat buildings as on 30.06.2012.<br/><br/>(b),   (c) & (d): Under the Strengthening and Restructuring of Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) Scheme, Government has approved a provision of construction of 2 lakh AWC buildings @ Rs. 4.50 lakh per AWC building during  12th Five Year Plan Period in a phased manner with cost sharing ratio of 75:25 between Centre and State other than the North Eastern States  where it will be 90:10. <br/><br/>			In addition, States/ UTs have also been requested to leverage funds under various schemes like MP Local Area Development Scheme, MLA Local Area Development Scheme, Backward Regions Grant Fund, Panchayati Raj Institutions, Multi-Sectoral Development Programme, Rural Infrastructure Development Fund, Integrated Action Plan, Mahatama Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act.(MGNREGA), 13th Finance Commission, Additional Central Assistance, State Plan and other area development project for construction of AWC Buildings. <br/><br/>Recently, the Ministry of Rural Development has also included construction of AWCs in the list of permissible  works in Schedule I under MGNREGA.<br/><br/>In so far as extension of facilities available under ICDS to children and women working under MGNREGA is concerned, the ICDS Scheme is a self-selecting Scheme, universal and open to all children below 6 years of age and Pregnant & Lactating Mothers who come and access services from AWCs.<br/><br/><br/>******<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: General cadre BSF officers facing stagnation
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a) whether some BSF officers belonging to the general cadre are deprived of some financial benefits, promotional opportunities and thus are facing acute stagnation;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the rank of officers who are denied these benefits and the reasons therefor;<br/><br/>(c) whether these officers are also denied career progression and benefits of "non-functional financial upgradation" which were approved way back in 2009 ifself;<br/><br/>(d) whether it is also a fact that some IPS officers enjoy  these financial benefits; and<br/><br/>(e) if so, the details thereof and the steps being taken to redress the grievances of aggrieved officers and if not, the reasons for the same?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI R.P.N. SINGH)<br/><br/>(a) & (b):  BSF General Duty Cadre officers are not deprived of any admissible financial benefits or promotional opportunities/ career progression available to them.  Promotions being vacancy based, are given to the eligible officers only on the availability of vacancies.  As such, there has not been any acute stagnation in career progression of General Duty Cadre officers.<br/><br/>(c) to (e):  The Central Armed Police forces (CAPFs) including BSF officers have not been denied career progression and benefits of non-functional financial upgradation.<br/><br/>Consequent upon the acceptance of the recommendations of the Sixth Central Pay Commission, the Govt. issued orders in 2009, for non-functional upgradation for the officers of Organised group ‘A’ Services and also a Scheme i.e. Modified Assured Career Progression (MACP) for grant of non-functional upgradations to all other Central Government Officers/employees.<br/><br/>IPS officers are from Organized Central group ‘A’ Service, whereas BSF and other CAPFs officers are not organized Group ‘A’ Services.  Therefore, different schemes, as mentioned above, are available to IPS officers and CAPFs officers. <br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Raids against manufacture and sale of adulterated food items
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: 1921. SHRIMATI JAYA BACHCHAN:<br/><br/>Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a) whether it is a fact that a number of raids were conducted all over the country<br/>and a number of persons arrested in connection with the sale and manufacture of spurious milk, ghee and other such products;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the number of persons arrested during the last three years, year-wise and State-wise; and<br/><br/>(c) the number of cases registered under the relevant Acts as a result of such raids and the number of convictions so far, State-wise and year-wise?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE<br/>(SHRI GHULAM NABI AZAD)<br/><br/>(a) to (c): Yes. Random samples of various food samples are drawn regularly by State/U.T Governments and action is taken against the offenders, in case samples are found to be not conforming to the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act and Regulations made thereunder. No separate data is centrally maintained for milk / ghee adulteration. However, as per the information made available by the States / UTs, details of cases registered, challaned and convicted for adulteration in food products including milk / milk products, during 2009, 2010 and 2011-12, are annexed.<br/> <br/>

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: 1907. SHRIMATI JAYA BACHCHAN:<br/><br/>Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a) whether it is a fact that the Plan Panel has proposed an increase of about 200 per cent in Plan allocations for the health and family welfare for the Five Year Plan (2012-17);<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details of benefits the general public may get and whether more hospitals would be opened in the country in the urban and rural areas in particular; and<br/><br/>(c) if so, the details thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE<br/>(SHRI GHULAM NABI AZAD)<br/><br/>(a)    The actual allocation for Ministry of Health and Family Welfare during 11th Plan period was Rs. 99491 crore. As per 12th Five Year Plan document of Planning Commission the tentative allocation for 12th Five Year Plan for Ministry of Health and Family Welfare is Rs. 300018 crore which is an increase of 202 percent.  <br/>	<br/>(b)  & (c) : Higher resources would inter-alia  support more activities in public healthcare including improving health infrastructure.  In order to provide tertiary health care service on a regional basis, the Central Government has launched a major health programme under Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (PMSSY) to improve the tertiary health care delivery system by inter alia establishing new AIIMS like Institutions and Up-gradation of existing Government Medical Colleges across the country. The flagship programme, National Rural Health Mission, aims to provide accessible, affordable and quality healthcare to people, living in rural areas.  <br/>--<br/>

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether Government is promoting/encouraging to construct toilets in every house in the villages all over the country;<br/>(b) 	the amount of assistance, aid, loan, etc. given by Government to construct toilets in the villages across the country;<br/>(c) 	whether any survey has been conducted in the country to ascertain the number of households that have toilets; and<br/>(d) 	if the answer to part (b) above be in affirmative, the amount given and if not, the reasons therefor?<br/>
records.ans_text: (a):	Yes Sir, The Government of India administers the Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan (NBA), a comprehensive programme to ensure sanitation facilities in rural areas with the main goal of eradicating the practice of open defecation and ensuring clean environment. The objective of NBA is to achieve sustainable behavior change with provision of sanitary facilities in entire communities in a phased, saturation mode with “Nirmal Grams’ as outcomes. The new strategy is to transform rural India into ‘Nirmal Bharat’ by adopting community saturation approach.  NBA goal is to achieve 100% access to sanitation for all rural households by 2022. NBA is operated in a project mode taking district as a unit.  The NBA projects at present cover 607 rural districts of the country. Under NBA, the provision of incentive for individual household latrine units has been widened to cover identified APL households who are SC/ST, small and marginal farmers, landless labourers with homesteads, physically challenged and women headed households along-with all BPL households.  The main components under the programme are provision of incentives for Individual Household Latrines (IHHL), School Sanitation and Hygiene Education (SSHE), financial assistance for Community Sanitary Complex, Anganwadi toilets and Solid and Liquid Waste Management (SLWM). <br/>(b):	An incentive of  Rs.4600 (Rs.5100 for difficult and hilly areas) consisting of central share of Rs.3200 (Rs.3700 in case of hilly and difficult areas) and State Government share of Rs.1400 is given with effect from 1.4.2012  to households belonging to BPL and Identified APL categories for construction of individual household toilets. In addition assistance upto Rs. 4500 is permitted under Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) for construction of the toilet. Under NBA Guideline, there is also provision for a loan from revolving fund for APL households, not covered by incentive for construction of toilets.<br/>(c):	Yes Sir, Census 2011 has data on number of households with toilets.<br/>(d):	Till date a total of Rs. 9553.39 crore have been released for implementation of Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan(NBA)( Earlier known as Total Sanitation Campaign(TSC)) to State Governments. A Budget provision of Rs. 3500 crore has been made for NBA in 2012-13. <br/>

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether it is a fact that the Coal India Limited (CIL) has agreed to enter into Fuel Supply Agreements (FSAs) with power companies even if they do not have electricity purchase agreements in place;<br/>(b) 	whether it is also a fact that there were many issues relating to the supply of coal between the Coal Ministry and Power Ministry and the status of the issues as of now;<br/>(c) 	whether it is also a fact that the southern grid would be connected with  the national grid in near future; and<br/>(d)	the details in this regard and what would be the flow of electricity across the country ?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE  IN THE MINISTRY OF COAL  <br/>(SHRI  PRATIK PRAKASHBAPU PATIL  )<br/><br/> <br/>(a): 	It  has  been agreed in a meeting   that   Coal India Limited (CIL)  will sign  Fuel Supply Agreements (FSAs) with Power Plants without waiting for long term  Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs). However only after the plant is commissioned and long term PPA is signed, supply of coal would commence. <br/><br/>(b):	 FSA models have been evolved through a process of  continuous  consultations between the concerned Ministries and other stake holders. The issues where there are disagreements are resolved through mutual discussions and deliberations. Many of such point of concerns have already been addressed and a few more are in the process of being resolved.<br/> <br/>(c) & (d):	The Southern Regional Grid is already inter-connected asynchronously with the Northern-Western-Eastern-North-Eastern (NEW) Grid through the following High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) links:<br/><br/>a)	HVDC Talcher-Kolar Bipole <br/>b)	HVDC Bhadrawati Back to Back <br/>c)	HVDC Gazuwaka Back to Back<br/><br/>Two high capacity Alternating Current (AC) inter-regional links of 765 kV connecting Raichur (Southern Region) and Sholapur (Western Region) are under construction. Further, a 765 kV D/C line between Narendra and Kolhapur has also been taken up for implementation by Power Grid.  AC interconnection of Southern Regional Grid with the NEW Grid will facilitate smooth flow of power in the integrated grid depending on demand and supply position.<br/>***<br/>

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a)	whether it is a fact that Department of Pharmaceuticals has sought the opinion of Law Ministry on the Supreme Court interim order restraining the Government from altering the current price mechanism for certain essential drugs;<br/><br/>(b)	whether Government would follow a particular methodology for pricing mechanism of essential drugs; and <br/><br/>(c)	if so, the details thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE(INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF STATISTICS AND PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS <br/>                           (SHRI SRIKANT KUMAR JENA)<br/><br/>(a):	The Department of Legal Affairs, Ministry of Law & Justice advice was sought on the order dated 11.10.2011 and 03.10.2012 of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in the case of All India Drug Action Network and Others Vs. Union of India and Others, in Writ Petition (Civil) No. 423 of 2003.  <br/><br/>(b) & (c):	The Department of Pharmaceuticals had prepared a draft National Pharmaceutical Pricing Policy, 2011 (NPPP-2011) based on the criteria of essentiality as per the medicines as under National List of Essential Medicines-2011 (348 drugs with specified dosage and strengths), as stipulated by the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare which was placed before the Group of Ministers(GoM). Based on the recommendations of the GoM, National Pharmaceuticals Pricing Policy-2012(NPPP-2012) was formulated and placed before the Cabinet.  The Cabinet considered NPPP-2012 in its meeting held on 22.11.2012 and approved the same with certain modifications.  Further action to notify NPPP-2012 has been undertaken.<br/>                          xxxxx<br/>

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a)	whether Government has decided to grant additional powers to Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to supersede bank boards in certain cases without amending banking laws;<br/><br/>(b)	whether it is a fact that the RBI may enable to grant new banking licenses to private entities;<br/><br/>(c)	the names of the business houses who have shown interest in entering the banking sector;<br/><br/>(d)	the conditions laid down by the RBI to grant new licenses to business houses; and<br/><br/>(e)	the details thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE<br/>(SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA)<br/><br/>(a):	Yes, Sir. To empower the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) exercise more regulatory and supervisory powers over the banking companies, it is proposed to be notified as the “appropriate Government” for the purposes of sections 388B to 388E of the Companies Act, 1956 relating to removal of managerial personnel.<br/>. <br/>(b), (d) & (e): RBI has issued draft guidelines for licensing of new banks in the private sector on 29.08.2011, whereby the following are the eligible promoters:<br/><br/>I.	Only entities / groups in the private sector that are owned and controlled by residents shall be eligible to promote banks. <br/><br/>II.	Promoters / promoter groups with diversified ownership, sound credentials and integrity that have a successful track record for at least 10 years in running their businesses shall be eligible to promote banks. RBI may seek feedback on applicants on these aspects from other regulators and enforcement and investigative agencies like Income Tax, CBI, Enforcement Directorate, etc. as appropriate. <br/><br/>III.	Entities/groups that have significant (10% or more) income or assets or both from/ in activities in real estate and capital market, including real estate construction and broking activities taken together in the last three years, shall not be eligible to promote banks. <br/><br/>RBI has placed the detailed draft guidelines dated 29.08.2011 on its website www.rbi.org.in. Further, Since RBI has not issued final guidelines for licencing of new banks in the private sector, it has not invited applications for grant of licence to any entity.<br/><br/>(c):	Does not arise.<br/> <br/>

records.qtitle: Improvement in reactor design by NPCIL
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: <br/>whether it is a fact that the reactor designs has been improved by the Nuclear Power Corporation of India Ltd. (NPCIL) in the country;<br/><br/>(b) 	whether it is also a fact that nuclear plants could be installed in cities;<br/><br/>(c) 	whether it is also a fact that in case of an accident there would be no long term impact on the humans near the plant; and <br/><br/>(d) 	the details in this regard?<br/><br/><br/>
records.ans_text: <br/>THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES & PENSIONS AND PRIME MINISTER’S OFFICE (SHRI V. NARAYANASAMY) :    <br/><br/>(a)	Yes, Sir.<br/><br/>(b)	No, Sir.  Nuclear power plants are located at sites which meet the criteria laid down in the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB) Code on Safety in Siting of nuclear power plants.<br/><br/>(c)&(d)	 All plants are designed for postulated design basis accidents, such that in case of such an accident no member of the public will get exposed to radiation dose beyond acceptable limits, thereby, ensuring that there would be no long term impact on the humans near the plant.  Even for beyond design basis accidents, where the radiation exposure to some members of the public could be higher, the probability of suffering long term health effects caused by such radiation exposure is very low.<br/><br/><br/>*****<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Retirement benefits to police at par with army personnel
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a) whether it is a fact that Government is considering to extend some benefits that are given to the retired army personnel to retired police force personnel;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details of the benefits that are given to retired army personnel; and<br/><br/>(c) whether there would be any difference between the two and if so, the<br/>details thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI R.P.N. SINGH)<br/><br/>(a) to (c) :  The Government has approved the proposal of this Ministry on 1.11.2012  to declare the retired Central Armed Police Force (CAPF) personnel from Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), Border Security Force (BSF), Central Industrial Security Force (CISF), Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) and Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) as Ex-Central Armed Police Force personnel (Ex-CAPF personnel). The status “Ex-CAPF” is quite distinct from “Ex-Servicemen” of Defence Forces.  Based on such designation of Ex-CAPF personnel, the State Governments concerned may extend benefits to them similar to the benefits being extended to the Ex-Servicemen of Defence Forces.<br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Purchase of fifteen Chinook heavy lift helicopters
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a)  whether  it  is   a  fact  that  Government  propose  to  buy  fifteen  Chinook  heavy-lift <br/> helicopters in near future;<br/><br/>(b)  what would be the cost involved for purchasing these helicopters;<br/><br/>(c)  the features of the helicopters that Government is likely to purchase and whether it has been cleared by the IAF; and<br/><br/>(d)  if so, the details in this regard?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF DEFENCE<br/>(SHRI A.K. ANTONY)<br/><br/>(a) & (b):  Yes, Sir. In the proposal initiated by Indian Air Force (IAF) for procurement of 15 Heavy Lift Helicopters, M/s Boeing with Chinook Helicopter has emerged as the L1 Vendor.  The cost of the Contract would depend upon outcome of the Contract negotiation with the L1 Vendor, which has not yet concluded.<br/><br/>(c) & (d):  The Field Evaluation Trials for these Helicopters conducted by the Indian Air Force have found them to be compliant with all the stated Air Staff Qualitative Requirements (ASQRs).  Divulging further details in this regard may not be in the interest of National security.<br/><br/>******<br/>

records.qtitle: Growing energy requirement of the country
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a)  whether it is a fact that the energy requirements of the country is growing and is projected to grow by 6.5 per cent per year till 2016-17;<br/><br/>(b) the percentage of oil in comparison to the total energy requirements for the year 2011-12 and the value thereof;<br/><br/>(c) the names of the countries where ONGC Videsh has projects; and <br/>(d) whether the Shale gas can be a game changer and if so, to what extent? <br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS     <br/>( SHRIMATI PANABAAKA LAKSHMI)<br/><br/>(a)  As per the draft 12th Five Year plan on Energy chapter, the growth of country’s energy requirements by 2016-17 is about 5.69%.  However, growth in demand for petroleum products is estimated at 4.7% and natural gas is about 19.2% during the period.<br/><br/>(b)  Oil and gas contributed 38.86% (including 19.84% gas contribution) of the country’s total energy requirements in 2011-12 (source: BP Statistics, 2012).<br/><br/>(c ) ONGC Videsh Limited has oil and gas projects in  Cuba, Venezuela, Columbia, Brazil, Libya, Nigeria, Sudan, South Sudan, Russia, Kazakhstan, Syria, Iraq, Iran, Vietnam and Myanmar.<br/><br/>(d)  Government has initiated the process of assessment of shale oil/ gas potential in the country. Resource estimation of shale oil/gas in selected Indian Basins has been taken up by United States Geological Survey (USGS), ONGC and Central Mine Planning and Design Institute Limited (CMPDIL). Further, a Draft Shale Gas Policy is being processed by the Government.<br/><br/>The quantum of shale oil/gas production will only be known after award of exploration acreages and completion of exploration, field development and production activities by the Contractors.<br/>*******

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a)	whether it is a fact that a solar surveillance system has been installed at the Corbett National park to detect sand and stone miners as well as the poachers;<br/>(b)	whether it is also a fact that such a system is being planned to be installed at other such vulnerable places, bird sanctuaries/national parks etc; and <br/>(c)	the details of response of the State Governments in this regard and the likely expenditure to be involved?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS (SHRIMATI JAYANTHI NATARAJAN)<br/><br/>(a), (b) & (c)	A pilot initiative of electronic surveillance (“e-Eye”), using long range, intelligent thermal and infrared cameras, has been implemented in the southern part of the Corbett Tiger Reserve for 24X7 surveillance to strengthen protection.  The said initiative has been successfully implemented and well received by the State.  Under the ongoing Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Project Tiger, funding assistance is provided to States, based on their demands as reflected in the respective Annual Plan of Operations, for such efforts.<br/><br/><br/>***

records.qtitle: Lowering age limit for widow pension
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a)	whether it is a fact that Government is planning to reduce the age for widow pension from 40 years to 18 years under the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP);<br/>(b)	if so, the details thereof and Government''s stand in this regard;<br/>(c)	whether it is also a fact that the persons with disability would also be covered under the scheme; and<br/>(d)	the number of widow pensioners in the country above the age of 40 years and the number of additional pensioners likely to be included?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SHRI LALCHAND KATARIA)	<br/><br/>(a)&(b): Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS) which is a component of National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) is applicable to widows in the age group of 40-79 years and belonging to household living below the poverty line (BPL) as per the criteria prescribed by the Government of India. A Committee on criteria for grant of benefits under the schemes of NSAP has recommended reduction of age limit from 40 years to 18 years under IGNWPS.<br/><br/>(c): BPL person with severe and multiple disabilities in the age group of 18-79 years are covered under Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS). <br/><br/>(d):  As per the reports received from the State Governments, 36 lakh widows are covered under IGNWPS. If the eligibility age reduced from 40 years to 18 years, the number of additional beneficiaries likely to be included are 9.25 lakh.<br/><br/>*********<br/>

records.qtitle: Safety and security of train passengers
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a)	whether it is a fact that Railways have stepped up security of passengers especially the women, in trains;<br/><br/>(b)	whether it is also a fact that there is lack of coordination between the Railway Protection Force and the Government Railway Police, so far; <br/><br/>(c)	whether Government would ensure better coordination between various forces responsible for safety and security of passengers rather than blaming each other; and<br/><br/>(d)	the details thereof and the action likely to be taken at the earliest for safety of passengers, especially the women?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS <br/>      (SHRI KOTLA JAYA SURYA PRAKASH REDDY)<br/><br/>(a) to (d):  A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.<br/><br/>*****<br/> <br/>STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (d) OF UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 920 BY SHRIMATI JAYA BACHCHAN TO BE ANSWERED IN RAJYA SABHA ON 30.11.2012 REGARDING SAFETY AND SECURITY OF TRAIN PASSENGERS.<br/><br/>(a):  Yes, Sir.<br/><br/> (b):  No, Sir. <br/><br/> (c) & (d): Railways maintain regular coordination with Government Railway Police and Civil Police at various levels. Coordination meetings are being held with Government Railway Police by Director General/ Railway Protection Force, General Managers / Chief Security Commissioners of Railway Protection Force and Divisional Railway Managers/ Sr. Divisional Security Commissioners to enhance security of Passengers especially the women in trains. Hence the question of blaming each other does not arise<br/>However, the following measures are being taken by the Government Railway Police and Railways for security of the passengers including women passengers in trains:-<br/><br/>1.	On an average, 1275 trains are being escorted by Railway Protection Force besides escorting of about 2200 trains by Government Railway Police daily. <br/><br/>2.	Ladies Special Local Trains have been introduced in sub-urban sections, which are being escorted during peak hours.<br/><br/>3.	Train escort parties have been briefed to keep extra vigil on the ladies compartments.<br/><br/>4.	Regular drives are being conducted to prevent entry of male passengers in ladies compartments and if found, they are prosecuted under the provisions of the Railways Act.<br/><br/>5.	RPF/ GRP personnel remain present on station platform at a place where the ladies coach of the train stops to provide assistance to lady passengers in case of any eventuality.<br/><br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Mobile services under bilateral investment treaties
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether it is a fact that some foreign investors have sent legal notices to Government against the cancellation of mobile services under certain bilateral investment treaties;<br/><br/>(b)	 whether it is also a fact that Government has set up a group to look into the claims of the foreign investors; and<br/><br/>(c) 	the contention of the investors’ claims and the reaction of Government thereto?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (SHRI MILIND DEORA)<br/><br/>(a)	Yes , Sir.<br/><br/>(b)	An Inter-Ministerial Group (IMG), under the chairmanship of Secretary (Telecom) has been constituted in Department of Telecommunications to evolve a coordinated response of the Government to the legal notices to Government from foreign investors against the cancellation of Unified Access Services Licence citing various provisions of bilateral investment treaties.<br/><br/>(c)	 Consequent to the Supreme Court’s decision dated 02.02.2012 that the licences granted to the private respondents on or after 10.1.2008 pursuant to two press releases issued on 10.1.2008 and subsequent allocation of spectrum to the licensees are declared illegal and quashed, Government has received legal notices from foreign investors for conciliation and amicable settlement of the foreign investment disputes under provisions of Bilateral Investment Promotion and Protection Agreements (BIPAs) or Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement (CECA) between their country and Government of India.  The legal notices are being handled by the IMG for amicable settlement.<br/><br/>******<br/>

records.qtitle: Proposal to fix market linked Minimum Support Price
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a)	whether it is a fact that Government proposes to fix market linked Minimum Support Price (MSP) for many forest produces to increase the income of crores of tribals and forest dwellers; <br/><br/>(b)	the names of the States that produce such items like seeds, leaves, and resins and the number of people engaged in the work with their annual income as of now;<br/><br/>(c)	whether any commission has been appointed by Government to fix the MSP of such forests produce and the prices fixed for each items separately;<br/><br/>(d)	the names of the State/Central agencies that will handle the procurement and disposal of such products; and<br/><br/>(e)	if so, the details thereof?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS       <br/>(SMT. RANEE NARAH)<br/><br/>(a) to (c):	Yes, Sir. On the recommendation of committee of Secretaries, Ministry of Panchayati Raj constituted a committee under the chairmanship of Dr. T. Haque on 23.08.2010 to suggest appropriate measures for implementation of provisions regarding Ownership, Price Fixation, Value Addition and Marketing of Minor Forest Produce (MFP). Government proposes to fix market linked Minimum Support Price (MSP) for 13 Minor Forest produces (Tendu, Bamboo, Mahua flower, Mahua seed, Sal leaf, Sal seed, Lac, Chironji, Wind honey, Myrobalan, Tamarind, Gums and Karanj) to increase the income of crores of tribals and forest dwellers.  <br/> <br/>The Minimum Support Price (MSP) Scheme is to be introduced in 9 Panchayat Extension to Scheduled Areas (PESA) States namely Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, Orissa, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh & Himachal Pradesh.  These are the States which produce items covered under MSP Scheme.<br/><br/>(d) & (e):	Tribal Cooperative Marketing Development Federation of India Ltd. (TRIFED) is proposed to be designated as the Nodal Agency entrusted with the task of coordinating and implementing the Scheme and implementing agency for procurement & marketing of Minor Forest Produce from their States designated by the respective State Governments.  <br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a)	whether a delegation of about hundred youth went to China recently to attend a special programme; <br/><br/>(b)	whether it is a fact that the youth from Arunachal Pradesh in that delegation were denied visa by the Chinese saying that Arunachal Pradesh actually belongs to China;<br/><br/>(c)	whether the Ministry has taken any objection to its decision to go ahead with the tour; and <br/><br/>(d)	the details thereof and the action proposed to be taken thereon?<br/>
records.ans_text: <br/>(a) & (b) A 100 member Indian youth delegation visited China from 12-21 July 2012. A lady delegate from Arunachal Pradesh could not travel as the Chinese authorities did not issue her a visa.  <br/><br/>(c) & (d) Government’s position that Arunachal Pradesh is an integral and inalienable part of India and that there should be no discrimination against visa applicants of Indian nationality on grounds of domicile and ethnicity has been clearly conveyed to the Chinese Government on several occasions including at the highest level.<br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government is considering increasing the price of diesel;<br/>(b) whether it is a fact that diesel consumption has shot up considerably in 2011-12 against overall rise of 2.9 per cent in petroleum products;<br/>(c) whether the proposed increase in price shall push up the inflation to alarming heights and affect the agriculture sector adversely;<br/>(d) whether it is also a fact that the sale of diesel cars have increased in recent years and there is a proposal to increase the annual road tax; and<br/>(e) if so, the details thereof and Government’s reaction thereto?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS<br/>(SMT. PANABAAKA  LAKSHMI)<br/>(a):	There is no such proposal, at present.  <br/><br/>(b):	Consumption of Diesel and all petroleum products and their growth during 2011-12 (provisional) is given below:<br/>	Product	Consumption (TMT)	Growth (%)<br/>Diesel	64,742	7.8%<br/>All Petroleum Products	1,47,995	4.9%<br/>	<br/>(c):        Does not arise in view of (a) above.<br/>(d) & (e):	As per information provided by the Department of Heavy Industries, Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM) has reported that the share of diesel passenger vehicles in the sales of total passenger vehicles during April – October, 2012 was around 59% as compared to 45% during the corresponding period of previous year. <br/>             <br/>The Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas has written to the Ministry of Finance for levying additional excise duty on Diesel cars.   <br/><br/>x-x-x-x-x <br/>

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a)	whether the Supreme Court had asked the Central Government and the States Governments of Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Delhi to produce information on the expenditure incurred by them to make the Yamuna river clean;<br/>(b)	whether it is a fact that the Court has asked the Central Water Pollution Control Board to collect samples of Yamuna water till Agra and submit a report on its cleanliness;<br/>(c)	whether the States and the Centre have since submitted their reports to the Court;<br/>(d)	the result of the samples taken; and<br/>(e)	the details thereof ?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS<br/>(SHRIMATI JAYANTHI NATARAJAN)<br/><br/>(a) The Hon’ble Supreme Court in the matter of ‘And Quiet Flows the Maily Yamuna’ WP(C) 725/1994 in its order dated 10.10.2012 directed Secretaries  of  Ministry of Urban Development and Ministry of Irrigation and Power, Chief Secretaries of Haryana and Uttar Pradesh, Vice-Chairman of Delhi Development Authority, Commissioners of the respective Corporations and the Chief Executive Officer of Delhi Jal Board to file affidavits indicating details of the amount spent project wise on preventing and controlling pollution in river Yamuna under various programmes. In compliance, the concerned authorities have filed their Affidavits in the Court.<br/><br/>(b) & (c)In compliance to directions of the Hon’ble Supreme Court, Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) has submitted on 12.09.2012 their water quality monitoring report on river Yamuna based on water samples of the river collected during August, 2012 from 14 locations in the stretch from Hathnikund to Agra in the states of Haryana, Delhi and Uttar Pradesh.  <br/><br/>(d) & (e) As per the report of CPCB, the cumulative assessment of the key parameters of water quality viz. pH, Dissolved Oxygen (DO), Bio-chemical Oxygen Demand (BOD),  Ammonia and Total Coliforms  indicates that  river  Yamuna  is not conforming to the desired levels from Hathnikund to Agra due to higher concentration of one or the other criteria pollutants despite excessive monsoon flow in the river. However, in terms of BOD, an important water quality parameter, the water quality in the stretch of river Yamuna from Hathnikund to Palla meets the prescribed standards, while it does not meet the desired standards in the river stretch from Nizamuddin Bridge in Delhi to Agra.  <br/><br/>*****

records.qtitle: Availability of drinking water in hilly States
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether Government is aware of the fact that a number of villages in many hilly States do not have drinking water facilities;<br/>(b) 	whether it is a fact that the water sources have dried up due to excessive digging for laying of roads;<br/>(c) 	whether it is also a fact that the womenfolk have to walk down about half-a-kilometer to fetch a can of water; and<br/>(d) 	the details of remedial steps that would be taken to supply safe drinking water?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF DRINKING WATER AND SANITATION<br/>(SHRI BHARATSINH SOLANKI)<br/><br/>(a)	Yes, Sir. Some habitations in the States including the hilly States are partially covered in terms of having less than adequate drinking water supply.  <br/><br/>(b)	The water sources dry up because of a number of reasons including excessive extraction of ground and surface water mainly for irrigation and industrial purposes, inadequate recharge of water in the sources, both surface water and ground water based, due to insufficient rains, depletion of tree cover and undergrowth in forests and catchment areas etc. However, the Ministry does not have any information regarding the water sources having dried up due to excessive digging for laying of roads.<br/><br/>(c)	 As per Census 2011, 22.10 % of rural households in the country have to travel more than half a kilometer for fetching drinking water in rural areas.<br/><br/>(d)	Under the centrally sponsored scheme, the National Rural Drinking Water Programme (NRDWP), the Government of India provides financial and technical assistance to States to supplement their efforts to provide adequate safe drinking water to the rural population. A budgetary allocation of Rs. 10,500 crores has been provided for NRDWP in 2012-13. Under NRDWP, the Government of India has given priority to cover partially covered habitations and quality affected habitations with safe drinking water schemes like handpumps, piped water supply schemes etc.  In the Twelfth Five year plan period, the focus is on providing drinking water through piped water supply, either by household connections or public standposts.

records.qtitle: New born babies abandoned in and around Jaipur, Rajasthan
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a)  	whether it is a fact that some new born babies were abandoned in and around Jaipur, Rajasthan recently; and<br/>(b) 	the details in this regard and the action taken thereon? <br/><br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SHRIMATI KRISHNA TIRATH)<br/><br/>(a) 	& (b): Yes, Sir. As per the information received from the Government of Rajasthan, Forty Three (43) abandoned babies were found in and around Jaipur during 2012-13 (upto 8th August, 2012). These abandoned babies were immediately admitted in Government Specialised Adoption Agency, Jaipur wherein they were medically examined. Fifteen (15) of these abandoned babies already have been placed into adoption after getting them declared legally free for adoption from Child Welfare Committee. <br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Surplus amount for expansion and overseas acquisitions
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a)	whether it is a fact that Government has asked the cash rich PSUs (Public Sector Units) to utilize surplus for expansion and overseas acquisitions to promote investments and growth;<br/><br/>(b)	the amount of surpluses, the Central PSUs have and could not plan for utilization of funds; and<br/><br/>(c)	the details in this regard?
records.ans_text: The Minister of State in the Ministry of Finance (SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA)<br/>(a) The Government has approved the implementation of a policy for acquisition of raw material assets abroad by CPSEs in October, 2011. The objective of the policy is to put in place a fast track and coordinated decision making process in order to facilitate acquisition of raw materials abroad by CPSEs for the requirement of manufacturing sector in the country.<br/><br/>(b)and (c) As per Public Enterprise Survey 2010-11 placed in the Parliament on 22.03.2012 all Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) taken together have a total cash and bank balance of Rs. 284153 Crores as on 31.03.2011.<br/>        Decisions on investment/utilization of surplus funds in various projects, expansion, diversification, joint ventures, subsidiaries etc. are taken by the Board of the CPSEs based on their corporate plans.

records.qtitle: Quality of water supplied in Delhi
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of URBAN DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:	<br/><br/><br/>(a)	whether it is fact that samples of water were taken from different areas of Delhi and most of them were found to be unfit for human consumption; <br/><br/>(b)	the number of samples that were found to be fit, area-wise; <br/><br/>(c)	whether it is also a fact that a number of diseases are caused by such quality of water that is not fit even for bathing; and <br/><br/>(d)	what remedial steps would be taken to supply safe drinking water to the people?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT<br/><br/>(SHRI SAUGATA ROY)<br/><br/><br/><br/>(a) 	: 	Delhi Jal Board (DJB) has informed that test report of water samples taken from different parts of Delhi show that water supplied by DJB is potable and fit for drinking as per the prescribed BIS 10500-2003 standards. <br/><br/>(b) 	:	Details of area-wise water samples tested and found fit for drinking as reported by DJB are as under:-<br/><br/><pre><br/><br/><br/>S.No.	Area	Total Nos. of Samples	Unsatisfactory Samples 	Percentage of unsatisfactory samples<br/>1	Civil Line	2040	58	.02<br/>2	Central	975	14	1.43<br/>3	Sardar Paharganj	1286	27	2.09<br/>4	Karol Bagh	1977	83	4.19<br/>5	Shahdara Zone	4606	32	.69<br/>6	Narela	1274	116	9.10<br/>7	South Zone 	5806	130	2.23<br/>	Total	17964	460	2.56%<br/><br/></pre><br/><br/>(c)	:	DJB has informed that water is supplied to the citizens of Delhi after treatment and purification.  Clorin is a germicide which annihilates numerous micro organism, bacteria and virus (water borne diseases).  As such, water is fit for drinking as well as bathing purposes.<br/><br/>(d)	:	DJB has also informed that for ensuring that water supplied to the citizens of Delhi is potable and meets the quality parameters as per standards of BIS 10500-2003, Seven laboratories equipped with hi-tech laboratory equipments work round the clock at all the Water Treatment Plants to monitor water quality starting from intake of raw water to various stages of treatment and supplies to the areas. Apart from these seven laboratories at the plants, six Zonal laboratories are located in different parts of the city.  Daily about 300-400 water samples are lifted from the consumers and tested in these zonal laboratories for Physical, Chemical and Bacteriological parameters for ensuring quality standards.  DJB also gets its water tested through its National Scientific Agency, namely, National Environment Engineering Research Institute. These test results are regularly analyzed and in case any local contamination is found, corrective measures are immediately taken to ensure potable water supply to the consumers.<br/><br/>****<br/>  <br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Audit of MGNREGA accounts by CAG
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: <br/>(a) 	whether there were any complaints regarding corruption and malpractices in the implementation of Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA);<br/>(b) 	whether the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) would be asked to audit the MGNREGA scheme taking into account the minute details such as job cards, muster rolls, bank pass books and payments made to workers to make the project financially prudent;<br/>(c) 	the quantum details of funds given to Gram Panchayats annually; and<br/>(d) 	whether the utilization of funds at the Gram Panchayat and district level along with Action Taken Reports and discrepancies observed, would be necessary for availing the funds further?<br/>
records.ans_text: <br/>ANSWER<br/>MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SHRI PRADEEP JAIN ‘ADITYA’)<br/>	<br/>(a):	The Ministry receives a large number of complaints about implementation of Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) in the country. The complaints mainly relate to cases of job cards not provided, misappropriation of funds, engagement of contractors, forgery of muster roll, manipulation in job cards, under payment of wages, non-payment of wages, corruption and other irregularities, use of machinery, delay in payments etc. As implementation of the Act is done by the State Governments in accordance with the Schemes formulated by them as per the provisions of the Act, all complaints received in the Ministry are forwarded to the concerned State Governments for taking appropriate action, including investigation, as per law.<br/>(b):	As per Section 24 of MGNREG Act 2005, the Central Government may in consultation with the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India, prescribe appropriate arrangements for audits of the accounts of the Schemes at all levels. Accordingly, in consultation with the CAG, the MGNREGA Audit of Schemes Rules, 2011, has been notified on 30th June, 2011. The Ministry has also requested for special financial and performance audits by CAG, to begin with, in the States of Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal. The CAG audit of MGNREGA in the Ministry of Rural Development and other States has already commenced.<br/>(c) & (d): MGNREGA is demand driven and Central funds are not released directly to Gram Panchayats. Funds are released to the States/UTs/Districts on the basis of agreed to Labour Budget and taking into consideration the performance and utilization of available funds. The details of Central funds released to States/UTs from 2009-10 onwards are given in Annexure. 1st tranche of Central share under MGNREGA is released to States/UTs/Districts taking into account availability and requirement of funds as per agreed to labour budget subject to settlement of accounts of the financial year before last and 2nd tranche is released provided Utilization Certificates of previous year and current year are submitted. <br/><br/>*********<br/>

records.qtitle: Loss of animal lives due to floods in Assam
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a)	whether it is a fact that due to heavy flood in Assam a  number of wild animals entered the cities and villages to save their lives but were killed by vehicles and the people there; and<br/>(b)	the steps being taken by Government to save the wildlife in the State? <br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS (SHRIMATI JAYANTHI NATARAJAN)<br/><br/>(a) As per the information received from the Government of Assam, there are no reports of wild animals entering into cities and villages during the floods and being killed by the people in Assam. Few animals straying in the nearby villages were driven back to the wild by the forest staff with the help of villagers. However, 36 number of wild animals (hog deer-24, swamp deer-2, sambar-1, wild boar-6, python-2 and fox-1) unfortunately died in road accidents during the recent flood in Assam.<br/><br/>(b)The protection and management of wildlife in the Assam is looked after by the State Government. Following steps have been taken by the Government of Assam to save wildlife in the state<br/><br/>1.Local youths, communities and Non-Governmental Organizations have been involved in saving wildlife.<br/><br/>2 Strength of field staff  has been augmented by engaging Assam Forest Protection Force and armed home guards in the protected areas.<br/><br/>3.Infrastructure has been strengthened by constructing large number of anti-poaching camps and patrolling paths in the protected areas.<br/><br/>4.Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 has been amended in Assam enhancing the punishment to the poachers up to a maximum of life imprisonment. The wildlife offences have been made cognizable and non-bailable.<br/><br/>5.Forest officers at all levels have been granted power to use fire arms for protection of forest and wildlife under the provisions of Indian Penal Code. They have also been granted immunity from prosecution without prior sanction of the Government.<br/><br/>6.Education and awareness programmes have been undertaken for protection of wild animals.<br/><br/>7.Round the clock patrolling and close monitoring has been ensured in the protected areas.<br/><br/>8.Sufficient number of wireless sets, arms and ammunition, GPS sets and vehicles have been made available to the staff engaged in wildlife protection.<br/><br/>Central Government provides financial assistance to State Governments including the Government of Assam under the Centrally Sponsored Schemes of ‘Integrated Development of Wildlife Habitats”, “Project Elephant” and “Project Tiger” for protection and management of wildlife and its habitats in the states. <br/><br/>*****

records.qtitle: Trapping of miners in Garo hills
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether it is a fact that a number of miners were trapped in a mine in Garo Hills recently;<br/>(b) 	the number of miners that could be saved/rescued and the number of miners still trapped in the mine;<br/>(c)	 whether it is also a fact that the mine-owners did not inform the authorities well in time; and<br/>(d) 	what are the details in this regard and whether Government would issue an advisory not to undertake such operations during rainy season?<br/>		<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR MINES<br/>(SHRI DINSHA PATEL)<br/><br/>(a) and (b):  	 Certain news paper reports have come to the attention of Government on an accident which occurred on 6.7.2012 at Nengkol in Rongsa Awe of Nangalbibra, South Garo Hills District, Meghalaya, supposedly causing death of 15 persons. In this context, as per available information, the following authorities/agencies have conducted search and rescue operations including investigations into the accident:<br/><br/>•	National Disaster Response Force;<br/>•	State Police Personnel;<br/>•	State Officials of the Directorate of Mineral Resources;<br/>•	Team of officials of the Directorate General of Mines Safety, Guwahati Region;<br/>•	Officials of the State Labour Department.<br/>A Magisterial enquiry was also conducted by the 1st Class Magistrate, South Garo Hills District, Meghalaya which found that there were no reports of missing labourers filed with the police and further during search and rescue operations, no victims (alive or dead) were found inside the mine.<br/>(c) and (d);  The mine owner did not inform any authorities about the occurrence of accident. The Government shall issue suitable advisory to the State Government after detailed reports are received in the matter.<br/><br/>*******<br/>

records.qtitle: Radiation from mobile phone towers casuing diseases
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether it is a fact that mobile phone towers emit radiation causing harmful effects and other ailments to people and even fauna in the country;<br/><br/>(b) 	whether apart from WHO, a number of experts/doctors and other specialists have also confirmed that radiation causes diseases like cancer;<br/><br/>(c) 	whether such tests/studies/surveys have been conducted in other countries also and if so, the details thereof; <br/><br/>(d) 	whether a number of people across the country have complained of such diseases; and<br/><br/>(e) 	the preventive measures Government proposes to take in view of such tests/studies, etc.?
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF HUMAN  RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT AND <br/>COMMUNICATIONS AND  INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY<br/> (SHRI KAPIL SIBAL)<br/><br/><br/>(a) to (e)	A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.<br/><br/>STATEMENT TO BE LAID ON THE TABLE OF THE RAJYA SABHA IN RESPECT OF PARTS (a) TO (e) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 283 FOR 31ST         AUGUST, 2012 REGARDING “RADIATION FROM MOBILE PHONE TOWERS CAUSING DISEASES”<br/><br/>(a)	World Health Organization (WHO) in its Fact Sheet No. 304, May 2006 on Electromagnetic Fields and Public Health (Base Stations and Wireless Technologies) has concluded that “considering the very low exposure levels and research results collected to date, there is no convincing scientific evidence that the weak RF Signals from base stations and wireless networks caused adverse health effects. From all evidence accumulated so far, no adverse short or long term health effects have been shown to occur from the RF Signals produced by base stations (mobile phone towers).<br/><br/><br/>International Commission on Non-Ionizing Radiation Protection (ICNIRP) guidelines of April 1998 states that, epidemiological studies on exposed workers and the general public have shown no major health effects associated with typical exposure environments. The studies have yielded no convincing evidence that typical exposure levels lead to adverse reproductive outcomes or an increased cancer risk in exposed individuals. ICNIRP, in its report of April 1998, has prescribed the following levels limiting EMF emission from Base Transceiver Stations (BTSs) as safe for general public: <br/><br/> Table is available in Annexure<br/>(f  is the frequency of operation in MHz) <br/><br/>In their Statement released in 2009, ICNIRP has stated that the scientific literature published since the 1998 guidelines has provided no evidence of any adverse effects below the basic restrictions and does not necessitate an immediate revision of its guidance on limiting exposure to high frequency electromagnetic fields. Therefore, ICNIRP reconfirms the 1998 basic restrictions in the frequency range 100 kHz–300 GHz until further notice.<br/><br/><br/>Further, in its Fact sheet No. 193 of 2011, WHO has stated that they will conduct a formal risk assessment of all studied health outcomes from radio frequency fields exposure by 2012.<br/><br/><br/>(b) & (c)	In its Fact Sheet No. 193 of 2011, WHO has stated that “Several large multinational epidemiological studies have been completed or are ongoing, including case-control studies and prospective cohort studies examining a number of health endpoints in adults. The largest retrospective case-control study to date on adults, Interphone, coordinated by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC), was designed to determine whether there are links between use of mobile phones and head and neck cancers in adults. The international pooled analysis of data gathered from 13 participating countries found no increased risk of glioma or meningioma with mobile phone use of more than 10 years. There are some indications of an increased risk of glioma for those who reported the highest 10% of cumulative hours of cell phone use, although there was no consistent trend of increasing risk with greater duration of use. The researchers concluded that biases and errors limit the strength of these conclusions and prevent a causal interpretation. Based largely on these data, IARC has classified radiofrequency electromagnetic fields as possibly carcinogenic to humans (Group 2B), a category used when a causal association is considered credible, but when chance, bias or confounding cannot be ruled out with reasonable confidence”.<br/><br/>The above mentioned finding of WHO is with respect to use of mobile phones and not to the Electromagnetic Fields from mobile phone towers.<br/><br/><br/>Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) has examined the issue and stated that there are no conclusive data available so far on this issue. The review of literature does not establish conclusive evidence on the safety or risk of radio frequency radiation (RFR) emitted from cell phone and cell phone towers but growing body of scientific evidences indicates some bio-effects and possible adverse health effects of RFR which merit further investigations.<br/><br/><br/>An Inter-Ministerial Committee (IMC) consisting of officers from Department of Telecommunications, Indian Council of Medical Research (Ministry of Health & Family Welfare), Department of Biotechnology and Ministry of Environment and Forest was constituted on 24.08.2010 to examine the effect of Electromagnetic Field (EMF) Radiation from base stations and mobile phones. <br/><br/>IMC in its report, has examined the 90 international and national studies/reference papers, related with the EMF radiation and has indicated that most of the laboratory studies were unable to find a direct link between exposure to radio frequency radiation and health; and the scientific studies as yet have not been able to confirm a cause and effect relationship between radio frequency radiation and health. The effect of emission from cell phone towers is not known yet with certainty. <br/><br/><br/>Department of Science and Technology has also convened a meeting on 03.07.2012 of an Expert Group on EMF radiation and recognized that the available scientific literature on the subject of health hazard from mobile tower radiation is not yet conclusive enough to derive norms based on credible scientific evidence.<br/><br/><br/>(d) & (e)  Complaints regarding alleged fear of health hazards from mobile tower radiation are being received and petitions have also been filed by individuals and NGOs in various Courts in this regard. Various media reports are also indicating health hazards due to radiation from mobile tower and mobile phones. <br/><br/>Department of Telecommunications (DoT) has adopted the International Commission on Non-Ionizing Radiation Protection (ICNIRP) norms in the year 2008 regarding Electro-magnetic Fields (EMF) emanating from mobile towers. Accordingly, all the Cellular Mobile Telephone Service (CMTS)/ Unified Access Service (UAS) licensees are submitting the compliance to the existing reference limits/ levels by way of submission of self certification of their Base Transmitting Stations (BTS) to the respective Telecom Enforcement Resource & Monitoring (TERM) Cells of DoT. Further, TERM Cells have carried out the testing of radiation levels for 28,862 BTSs upto 30.06.2012, and found that the radiations levels are in compliance of the prescribed limits for all the tested BTSs.<br/><br/><br/>Further, the Inter Ministerial Committee, constituted by DoT, has as a precautionary measure, inter-alia recommended for lowering of the Base Transmitting Station (BTS) Radio Frequency (RF) exposure limits to 1/10th of the existing ICNIRP prescribed limit and reduction of Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) level for mobile handsets from 2 Watt/Kg to 1.6 Watt/Kg. These recommendations of IMC have been accepted by DoT and the following directions for implementation have been issued: <br/><br/><br/>(i)	Directions for lowering of the mobile towers EMF radiation to 1/10th of the existing prescribed limits has been issued to the Mobile Operators vide DoT letter dated 30.12.2011. These directions are effective from 01.09.2012.  <br/><br/>	<br/>(ii) 	Directions for reduction of SAR value from 2 Watt/Kg to 1.6 Watt/Kg for Mobile Handset have been issued  to Mobile Handset  Manufacturers   vide DoT  letter dated 25.01.2012 and 17.08.2012. These directions are effective from 01.09.2012. <br/>	<br/>**********

records.qtitle: Punishment to students for protesting against quality of Mid Day Meal
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a)	whether it is a fact that a number of students were canned for protesting against quality of food served as Mid-Day-Meal in Vadodara, Gujarat recently; <br/> <br/>(b)	whether it is also a fact that such incidents happened earlier also but went un-noticed; and<br/> <br/>(c)	the details in this regard and the action thereon?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SHRI KAPIL SIBAL)<br/><br/><br/>(a) to (c):   It was reported in the local news paper ‘Divya Bhaskar Network’, Vadodara that 47 children were locked in the room by the class teacher for complaining against the mid day meal, and were beaten badly. The Government of Gujarat have reported that some students complained to class teacher against the mismanagement in serving of mid day meal on 13.7.2012 in Primary School of village Brahmanvashi, District Vadodara. The complaint was against the class teacher’s behavior and not due to quality or quantity of mid day meal served. No such incident has happened earlier. The State Government has suspended the class teacher and transferred the Principal and Vice Principal to other places. <br/>*****

records.qtitle: Corporal punishment to students for refusing to eat mid day meal
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a)	whether it is a fact that two students were beaten to unconsciousness for refusing to eat the mid-day-meal infested with insects in Bihar recently; and <br/><br/>(b)	the details in this regard and the action taken against the accused playing with the lives of children?
records.ans_text: <br/>MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SHRI KAPIL SIBAL)<br/><br/><br/>(a) & (b):	A news report captioned “Kids thrashed for refusing insect-infested school meal” was published in a news paper dated 16.07.2012. The Government of Bihar was directed to get the matter enquired into and has reported that the matter was investigated by District Education Officer, Vaishali and it was found that the report of serving insect infested Mid Day Meal was not true. Two students of Class VI, who were beating a junior student, were punished by the Head Master and the incident was not related to the Mid Day Meal programme. <br/>*****

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether Government is considering any move to amend the graft laws to enable the citizens to know the status of their complaint against the corrupt persons including the officials;<br/><br/>(b)	 the salient features of the amendments likely to be introduced; and<br/><br/>(c) 	in what way the citizens would be getting justice at an early date?<br/>
records.ans_text: Minister of State in the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions and Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office. (SHRI V. NARAYANASAMY)<br/>(a):    There is no such proposal with the Government.<br/>(b) & (c):   Does not arise.<br/>*****<br/><br/>

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a)	the number of States in the Indian Union that are under heavy debt;<br/><br/>(b)	whether such States approach the Centre for special financial package to get rid of the debt;<br/><br/>(c)	the criteria to grant financial packages to States under heavy debt; and<br/><br/>(d) the said grant that would be adjusted in future allocations to States seeking such packages?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE FOR FINANCE<br/>(SHRI  NAMO  NARAIN MEENA)<br/>(a) to (d): The Thirteenth Finance Commission (FC – XIII) has inter- alia prescribed annual debt to Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) targets for each State to be maintained during its award period 2010-15 so as to reach a combined debt target of 24.3% of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) by 2014-15 of all States from a level of 27% of GDP in 2008-09. As gleaned from Budget Estimates of States for 2012-13, debt/GSDP ratios of three States are estimated to be more than the targets prescribed in their respective Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Acts (FRBMAs). However the position may change during the fiscal year. The States are required to monitor their liabilities under their respective FRBMAs, enacted/amended by all States in line with recommendations of FC – XIII. <br/>The recent most comprehensive debt restructuring exercise was undertaken under the award of the Twelfth Finance Commission (TFC) (2005-2010). The Debt Consolidation and Relief Facility (DCRF), subject to compliance with prescribed conditions was extended to all States. This facility involved (i) consolidation of loans from Ministry of Finance (MoF), contracted till 31.03.2004 and outstanding as on 31.03.2005, for a fresh tenure of 20 years at an interest rate of 7.5% per annum and (ii) waiver of consolidated debt  based on fiscal performance of States. Under the scheme, loans extended by Ministry of Finance (MoF) amounting to Rs.1,13,601 crore, were consolidated and debt waiver of Rs.19,726 crore was provided to twenty six eligible States till 31.3.2010. Loans extended by MoF to the remaining two States, amounting to Rs. 8747 crore outstanding as on 1.4.2010 were consolidated as recommended by the Thirteenth Finance Commission (FC-XIII). <br/>Further as recommended by FC-XIII for its award period (2010-15), loans extended to States through Ministries other than MoF under Centrally Sponsored Schemes/ Central Plan Schemes and outstanding at the end of 2009-10, have also been written off to the extent of Rs. 2,050 crore till 31.3.2012.   <br/>FC XIII has also recommended reset of interest rates on loans from National Small Savings Fund, contracted up to 2006-07 and outstanding at the end of the year preceding the year of enactment/amendment of the States’ FRBMAs, at a common rate of 9% per annum. As estimated by FC XIII, interest relief of Rs.13,517 crore is expected to accrue to States on this account, during 2010-15. The benefit continuing beyond the award period of FC-XIII has been estimated to reach Rs.28,360 crore by the maturity of the last loan coming under purview. <br/>

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN POVERTY ALLEVIATION be pleased to state:<br/>(a)	whether Government has any plan to protect the rights of about 10 million street vendors across the country by introducing legislation in this regard; and<br/>(b)	the salient features of the proposed legislation in protecting the means of livelihood of such hawkers?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF HOUSING AND URBAN POVERTY ALLEVIATION<br/><br/>(KUMARI SELJA)<br/><br/>(a):  Yes, Sir.<br/>(b):  The salient features of the proposed legislation are given in the Annexure.<br/>     <br/>                                                                 ******** <br/> <br/>Annexure<br/><br/>       Annexure referred to in reply to Rajya Sabha USQ No.1958 for 29.08.2012              <br/><br/> The Salient Features of the Proposed Legislation: <br/><br/>?	Compulsory registration for every person intending to carry out street vending;<br/><br/>?	The street vendor shall have the right to carry on the business of street vending as mentioned in certificate of vending and right to reclaim  his/her goods if confiscated as specified in the scheme;<br/><br/>?	The appropriate Government is required to constitute a Town Vending Committee with minimum forty percent representation of street vendors;<br/><br/>?	The local authority in consultation with planning authority to make out a plan once in every five years to promote a supportive environment for urban street vendors to carry out their vocation;<br/><br/>?	For the redressal of grievances or resolution of disputes, the local authority to constitute a permanent Committee consisting of a person who has been a sub-judge or judicial magistrate or an executive magistrate as Chairperson and such other persons having such experience in street vending activities;<br/><br/>?	The appropriate Government to undertake promotional measures for making available credit, insurance and other welfare schemes of social security for the street vendors;<br/><br/>?	Street vendors carrying on street vending in accordance with the terms and conditions of his/her certificate of vending not to be prevented from exercising their right, to vend, by any person or police or any other authority, under any law in force.<br/><br/><br/>                                                                ********<br/><br/>                                                     <br/>

records.qtitle: Passing of secret information by army personnel
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a)  whether it is a fact that the defence rules do not permit any officer to identify themselves or their locations on social networking sites;<br/><br/>(b) whether it is also a fact that two officers of the Indian Army were honey-trapped by foreign female operative allegedly working for secret services;<br/><br/>(c)  whether the officers pass on some sensitive or secret information and were probed by the authorities; and<br/><br/>(d)  if so, the details thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF DEFENCE<br/>(SHRI A.K. ANTONY)<br/><br/>(a) to (d):  Yes, Sir.  Two instances have been reported where officers were compromised by alleged foreign operatives.  Inquiries were conducted and appropriate action has been initiated.<br/><br/>******<br/>

records.qtitle: Denial of admission to pregnant women by hospitals
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a)	whether it is a fact that a large number of women at an advanced stage of their pregnancy are denied admission, particularly when they are in labour pains, by many hospitals on one pretext or the other;<br/><br/>(b)	the number of women who gave birth to their children outside the hospitals and pavements as a result of such denials; and<br/><br/>(c)	 what action Government takes against such hospitals, which generally are given land on a very low price and which had agreed to treat the poor and needy patients free of cost or on subsidised rates?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: (a)to(c)	A statement is laid on the Table of the House.<br/> <br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO RAJYA  SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 238 FOR 28TH   AUGUST, 2012<br/>.....<br/><br/>	Since Health is a state subject, no such information is maintained centrally. It is the responsibility of the State Governments to ensure easy  access of people to healthcare facilities. However, as far as three Central Government Hospitals i.e. Safdarjung Hospital, Dr. RML Hospital and LHMC & its associated Hospitals in Delhi are concerned, there are no instances of refusal of admission to any pregnant woman coming to the hospital. <br/>	<br/>As reported by the Government of NCT of Delhi, presently 42 identified private hospitals in Delhi, which were allotted land at concessional rates by the land allotting agencies, are providing free treatment to the extent of 10% IPD and 25% OPD completely free of any charges to the eligible category of EWS patients. Directorate of Health Services, Government of NCT of Delhi, has not received any complaint in respect of denial of admission to pregnant women belonging to EWS category by those identified private hospitals.<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: ONGC agreement with Chinese firm on oil exploration
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a) whether it is a fact that the ONGC has singed an agreement with China’s National Petroleum Corporation on Hydrocarbon exploration, crude oil refining and building oil and gas pipelines;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof; and<br/><br/>(c) whether it will be beneficial to India, if so, in what way?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS<br/>(SHRI R.P.N. Singh)<br/>(a) and (b):  Yes Sir.  A Memorandum of Understanding(MoU) was signed between Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited (ONGC) and China’s National Petroleum Corporation(CNPC) on 18th June, 2012.<br/><br/>The MoU between ONGC and CNPC is signed with an intention to extend co-operation in the hydrocarbon sector for mutual benefits. The MoU agreed between ONGC and CNPC (Parties) for co-operation in following areas:<br/><br/>(i)	Exploration and Production in  countries other than India and China;<br/>(ii)	refining, treating and processing of crude oil and natural gas;<br/>(iii)	marketing and distribution of petrochemical products;<br/>(iv)	construction and operation of oil and gas pipelines; and<br/>(v)	other midstream or downstream projects the parties are interested in.<br/><br/>(c):  OGNC Videsh Limited(OVL), 100% arm of ONGC is intended to have benefits out of such co-operation. <br/>

records.qn_text: (a) 	whether in the recent case of molestation of a girl in the North eastern Region, a media house was allegedly involved;<br/><br/>(b) 	whether the entire episode was filmed by a personnel of that media house and no other crew from any other media unit was present or even aware of ;<br/><br/>(c) 	whether the ghastly act of molestation was repeatedly telecast by that media house on its channel thus making the life of the victim miserable; and<br/><br/>(d) 	what punitive action Government has taken against that channel and what regulatory steps it proposes so that such acts are not supported or sponsored by some unscrupulous media houses to increase their circulation/TRPs?
