records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) the target for tax collection for the financial year 2008-09;

(b) whether it is a fact that these tax collections have fallen short of the target; and

(c) if so, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM)

(a): A target of Rs.3,65,000 crore was fixed for collection of Direct taxes for Financial Year 2008-09 during the Budget Estimates. The target was subsequently revised to Rs.3,45,000 crore during Revised Estimates for Financial Year 2008-09. In Indirect taxes the Budget Estimates for Customs, Central Excise & Service Tax for 2008-09 were Rs.1,18,930; 1,37,874 & 64,460 crore respectively, while the revised targets for the year 2008-09 for Customs duty, Central Excise and Service Tax were fixed as Rs.1,08,000 crore, Rs. 1,08,359 crore and Rs. 65,000 crore respectively which added up to Rs. 2,81,359 crore.

(b) & (c): Yes, Madam. In the Financial Year 2008-09 an amount of Rs.3,38,212 crore was collected against the Revised Estimate of Rs.3,45,000 crore on the Direct taxes side. Thus there was shortfall of Rs. 6788 crore in collection of Direct Taxes. The shortfall was primarily on account of economic slowdown resulting from the global financial meltdown and consequent economic recession in developed economies. The economic slowdown dented the profits of companies and also resulted in lesser salary payouts, resulting in decrease in collection in Corporate Tax and personal Income tax. The stock market also remained subdued which impacted the collection of Securities Transaction Tax. Therefore, Direct taxes collection was below the Revised Estimate.
In Indirect Taxes, in the first half of 2008-09, the economy came under severe inflationary pressures. With a view to augment supply of essential items, the rates of basic Customs duty were reduced. By the middle of 2008-09, as the signs of economic slowdown became apparent, Government announced a series of stimulus packages in the form of reduction in Excise duty and Service tax rates to revive the economy. On 7th December, 2008, the Central Excise duty (& also CVD) was reduced by four percentage points across the board on non-petroleum items. Further on 24th February, 2009, the rate of Central Excise (& also CVD) on items attracting 10% of excise were reduced by two percentage point. The rate of Service tax was also reduced from 12% to 10% across the board on the same day. Further, the overall global economic meltdown affected the domestic economy both by way of reduced domestic production of goods and by way of reduced imports and led to reduced collection of Customs duty, Central Excise duty and Service tax.

records.qtitle: NON AVAILABILITY OF FORM O AT POLLING BOOTHS
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that, form 49(O) were not provided at a large number of polling booths in the recent general elections for the benefit of voters wanting to express their disapproval of the candidates contesting the elections, as per the media reports published in a section of the press;

(b) if so, the estimated number of booths in the country which were not having these forms; and

(c) the reasons therefore?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF LAW AND JUSTICE

(DR. M. VEERAPPA MOILY)

(a) Under the election Laws and Rules, there is no form titled ’49-(O)’. However, there exists Rule 49-O under the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 which provides an option to the elector not to record his vote. Under this Rule an elector, after his electoral roll number has been duly entered in the register of voters in Form – 17A and has put his signature or thumb impression, decides not to record his vote, a remark to this effect is then made against the said entry in Form 17A by the Presiding Officer and the signature or thumb impression of the elector is obtained against such remarks.

(b) & (c) Do not arise.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan

(b) if so, the current status of fire; and

(c) the steps taken to prevent recurrence of such fire incidents?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS

(SHRI JAIRAM RAMESH)

(a) & (b) Yes, Sir. A red alert was issued by the State for prevention of fire in the Corbett Tiger Reserve. As informed by the State, only 1.5 hectares of the said reserve was affected by fire due to successful fire prevention and control measures.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) the number of forests that caught fire this summer and the number of incidents of fire reported, giving the details, State-wise;

(b) whether the fire incidents were successfully controlled in all cases;

(c) the details of the damage caused by these fire incidents; and

(d) the long term arrangements made to control or prevent such incidents?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS

(SHRI JAIRAM RAMESH)

(a),(b) & (c) This information is not collated at the Central level. However, the same is being collected from the State/UT Forest Departments and will be placed on the Table of the House.

(d) The Government of India through its Centrally Sponsored Integrated Forest Protection Scheme provides financial assistance to the State/UT Governments to supplement their forest-fire prevention and control measures. The long term measures being taken to prevent and control forest-fires include:

(i) Setting up of Fire Fighting Cells with surveillance and communication equipments and mobility.

(ii) Fire mapping and preparation of Fire Management Plans.

(iii) Use of MODIS Satellite data through web-based facility for near real time detection of fire and intimation to the concerned State/UT Forest Department by the Forest Survey of India, Dehradun.

(iv) Creation and maintenance of Fire Lines by removal of fire hazards before the onset of fire season and during the season.

(v) Construction of Fire Watch Towers at strategic locations.

(vi) Construction of Water Storage Structures and storage of water.

(vii) Engagement of Fire Watchers during fire season.

(viii) Involvement of local people through Joint Forest Management Committees in surveillance, reporting and fire fighting.

(ix) Training and awareness of personnel and people.

records.qtitle: TECHNOLOGY FOR REMOVAL OF ARSENIC IRON FROM GROUND WATER .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that a technology has been developed by a CSIR laboratory for removal of arsenic/ iron from ground water by using ceramic membranes and another technology comprising of microbial cum adsorbent route;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether the technology has been used in areas having ground water affected with arsenic and leading to a number of health problems; and

(d) if not, the reasons therefor ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY AND EARTH SCIENCES

(PRITHVIRAJ CHAVAN)

(a & b) Yes Sir. A technology for removal of arsenic and/or iron from ground water using ceramic membrane module has been developed by Central Glass & Ceramics Research Institute (CGCRI), a CSIR laboratory in Kolkata for community application. CSIR has not developed any technology based on microbial cum adsorbent route for production of high quality drinking water from contaminated ground water.
The technology for arsenic and iron removal is essentially a hybrid type comprising of two steps:

i) Adsorption of arsenic by the colloidal media particles suspended in water, and
ii) Application of membrane based separation technique for solid-liquid separation using ceramic micro-filtration membrane modules.
The advantages are:

i) The level of purification achieved is as per WHO recommended limits for arsenic (<0.01 ppm) and iron (<0.3 ppm) in Drinking Water.
ii) Simultaneous removal of Arsenic and Iron from contaminated ground water makes the technology more superior.
iii)The technology is capable of treating ground water containing higher concentrations of arsenic (up to 2.7 ppm) and iron (up to 13 ppm).
Patents The technology is patented in USA (US Patent No. 7014771, dated March 21, 2006), Bangladesh (BD5912002, dated 28.03.2002), Chile (CL605-2002 dated 28.03.2002) and Taiwan (TW91106287 dated 29.3.2002). The patent has been filed in India (NF/235/2001)

(c) CGCRI/CSIR’s technology for arsenic removal has been used for purification of ground water in some of the arsenic/iron affected areas including West Bengal. There are 6 beneficiaries in West Bengal and 15 beneficiaries in North-East states. The technology is also available for societal/ commercial exploitation.

(d) Does not arise.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan

(a) whether it is a fact that Government is considering a proposal to withdraw CRPF from Kashmir and hand over the security operations to local police;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI AJAY MAKEN)

(a) to (c): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 367 FOR 29.7.2009

records.qtitle: ASSESSMENT OF WORKING OF EMPLOYMENT EXCHANGES .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government has assessed the working of employment exchanges against the present day complex nature of the job market;

(b) if so, with what results thereto;

(c) whether Government is considering any proposal to reorient, modernize or abolish the system; and

(d) if not, the reasons therefor ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT

(SHRI HARISH RAWAT)

(a)&(b): Employment Exchanges are functioning under administrative and financial control of the respective State Governments/Union Territory Administrations. The Working Group on National Employment Service, consisting of representatives of Central and State Governments reviews functioning of the Employment Exchanges in the country periodically and suggests corrective measures. State Governments have taken many initiatives such as training of registered job-seekers, organising career melas, job-melas, campus recruitment programmes, etc to increase placement in the private sector keeping in view the changed employment market scenario. These efforts are showing good results.

(c) The Employment Exchanges are being modernized through computerization by the State Governments/ Union Territory Administrations keeping in view the resources available with them. Though some of the Employment Exchanges are computerized, many of them still work manually resulting in handicap in dissemination of information to employers and job-seekers. Modernisation and upgradation of Employment Exchanges has now been identified as one of the Mission Mode Projects under the National-e-Governance Plan by Government of India with an objective to progressively support all the State Governments to make effective use of IT in various activities for providing better services to all the stakeholders.

(d) Does not arise.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government is considering a proposal to take steps under WTO against protectionist measures being taken by developed countries in a range of sectors including steel;

(b) whether it is a fact that world over protectionism has taken new forms that needs to be addressed; and

(c) the details of steps being considered or taken in this regard?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY

(SHRI JYOTIRADITYA M. SCINDIA)

(a) to (c) : The Government examines the tariff and non tariff measures (NTMs) imposed by developed countries especially on products of export interest for developing countries including steel. These protectionist measures inter alia include technical regulations, conformity assessment procedures, registration requirements, trade remedial measures, rules or origin, customs valuation etc. The Government collects information on these measures from the commercial missions, export promotion councils, industry associations, development agencies and reports of international organisation such as the World Trade Organisation (WTO). Based on inputs received and examination of these measures, the Government then takes up these at the bilateral level with the trading partner or at the appropriate committee in the WTO. An Inter-Ministerial Committee has been constituted to co-ordinate the plan to tackle NTMs imposed by India’s trading partners by taking an effective remedial action. An institutional mechanism in the form of a database of NTMs imposed by other countries on India’s exports has also been created.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that export scene is likely to remain grim this year too;

(b) if so, what are the reasons coming in the way of recovery of exports; and

(c) the steps being contemplated to address the problem?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY

(SHRI JYOTIRADITYA M. SCINDIA)

(a) to (c): Quick Estimates of monthly trade statistics for the first three months of the current financial year, 2009-10 indicate significant decline in India’s merchandise exports. While there are various contributory factors, global slowdown and recession, particularly in the developed countries, leading to erosion in demand, is a significant factor for the decline. The Government and RBI announced a number of measures in the Stimulus Packages and in the Budget, 2009-10 to arrest the decline in exports. Measures announced so far, particularly for export sector, are given in Annexure. Government closely monitors the different export sectors and need based measures are taken keeping in view the financial implications.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government is considering a proposal to regulate fees, admission etc. of deemed universities;

(b) whether Government also proposes to probe complaints of lack of transparency in higher education; and

(c) if so, what are the details in this regard?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SMT. D. PURANDESWARI)

(a): The University Grants Commission (UGC), in its meeting held on 22nd June 2009, approved the UGC (Fee Structure in Institutions Deemed-to-be-Universities) Regulations, 2009 and UGC (Admission in Professional Programmes of Study at Institutions Deemed-to-be-Universities) Regulations, 2009, which are at present with the Government for consideration.

(b) & (c): While there are no specific complaints received with regard to lack of transparency, the Central Government is committed for ensuring transparency in the higher education system. Accordingly, in order to ensure that all the vital information / details relating to higher educational institutions are placed in the public domain, the Government has issued a directive under section 20(1) of the University Grants Commission (UGC) Act 1956, to the Commission to direct universities and higher educational institutions recognized under clause (f) of Section 2 of the UGC Act, 1956 and institutions declared as Institutions ‘Deemed to be Universities’ under Section 3 of the UGC Act, 1956 to place on every such institution’s website full and complete information relating to availability of infrastructure and physical assets, admission criteria, details of fee structure, details regarding courses and academic curricula, information regarding faculty position, details regarding study centres etc.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) the quantum of withdrawals by States of the Northern and Southern regions from the National Grid, during the last four months;

(b) whether it is a fact that there have been overdrawals from the grid during that period; and

(c) the steps Government has taken to avert collapse of the grid?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER

( SHRI BHARATSINH SOLANKI )

(a) to (c) : The drawal of power by the States from the Grid varies on month to month and day to day basis and also in real-time depending on the demand for electricity and its availability from various sources at any point of time. The details of schedule, drawal and overdrawal/underdrawal by the States in the Northern and Southern Region during the last four months i.e. March to June, 2009 are at Annex.
The Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC) has issued directions from time to time impressing upon the need to maintain the safety and stability of the Grid in accordance with the provisions of the Indian Electricity Grid Code (IEGC) notified by the Commission under Section 178 of the Electricity Act, 2003. The Regional Load Despatch Centre, being the designated apex body for monitoring of grid operations in the region, take up the matter with over-drawing constituents as and when required. In case of persistent default, notices are issued under Clause 1.5 of IEGC by Regional Load Despatch Centre and Member Secretary, Regional Power Committee. The matter is also taken up by Central Transmission Utility, Central Electricity Authority and Ministry of Power whenever required.

records.qtitle: SALE OF RARE FILMS AS WASTE
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) Whether it is a fact that Pune based National Film Archives of India sold around 25,000 film reels as waste, last year;

(b) Whether it is also a fact that many of those reels related to old and rare titles of which copies may not be available anywhere; and

(c) If so, the action Government has taken in this matter?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING

(Dr. S. JAGATHRAKSHAKAN)

(a) : The National Film Archive of India (NFAI) weeded out 15,565 reels last year, after they were declared as unserviceable by a Committee constituted by NFAI in February, 2003 for this purpose after being approved by the Director of the said archive. After completing the necessary formalities the material was disposed of in July 2008.

(b) : As informed by NFAI, a few old titles had to be weeded out for the reasons mentioned in reply to part (a) above. However, these films could be available with the concerned producers, directors or the laboratories.

(c) : Government has undertaken an ambitious project of digitizing and restoring the films available in NFAI, to avoid permanent loss of the film heritage.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether any periodic review for implementation of environmental policies and/or of the steps taken to combat the global warming is conducted; and

(b) if so, when the last review was conducted and with what results?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS

(SHRI JAIRAM RAMESH)

(a) A Coordination Committee chaired by Prime Minister called Prime Minister’s Council on Climate Change to coordinate national action for assessment, adaptation and mitigation of climate change was constituted on 6th June 2007.

(b) The last Meeting of the Prime Minister’s Council on Climate Change was held on 3rd June 2008. As decided by the Council, the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) was released on 30th June 2008 to outline India’s strategy to meet the challenge of Climate Change. The National Action Plan outlines steps that will enable the country to adapt to climate change and enhance the ecological sustainability of India’s development path. National Missions envisaged under the NAPCC are at various stages of finalization.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that nursing homes in the Capital are generally a kind of commercial shops, fleecing the patients by prolonging the stay and the treatment, prescribing tests that are not always necessary;

(b) if so, what is the position with regard to nursing homes in other Metros of the country; and

(c) whether Government is considering any proposal like appointment of an ombudsman to look into such complaints of the patients and take action against erring nursing homes?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

(SHRI GHULAM NABI AZAD)

(a) to (c) Health is a State subject and regulation of private hospitals and nursing homes including the fees charged by them is the responsibility of the State Government.

Enactment of a central legislation for registration and regulation of clinical establishments is a priority for this government.

records.qtitle: EFFECT OF GLOBAL WARMING ON CROPS .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) the status of various crops this year including those that have arrived in the market;

(b) whether they have been affected in any manner or are likely to be affected by global warming; and

(c) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI SHARAD PAWAR)

(a) to (c): This is the season for sowing of Kharif crops, which will be harvested during the months of Oct-Nov and will reach market thereafter. As reported by the India Meteorological Department(IMD), during South-West Monsoon, 2009 (1.6.2009 to 15.7.2009), the country as a whole received 220.5 mm of rainfall against normal average rainfall of 300.8 mm, with 369 out of 533 meteorological districts of the country receiving less than normal rainfall. Due to deficit rainfall there is shortage of moisture, which has affected sowing in kharif season. The area coverage during Kharif-2009 under major crops is 432.26 lakh ha., which is 52.11 lakh ha. less than the corresponding area coverage during Kharif 2008 in the country, as per crop -wise details given below:

The Government of India in the Ministry of Agriculture is implementing through the State Governments various programmes like, the National Food Security Mission (NFSM), the National Horticulture Mission (NHM) and Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY) to increase agricultural productivity and production in the country.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government’s attention has been drawn to recent media reports about the spurious milk being manufactured at a large scale in North India;

(b) whether it is a fact that State owned milk producers like Mother Dairy and DMS etc. also procure milk from these vendors;

(c) if so, the details of the precautions these producers take or have taken to ensure that the quality of milk produced by them is genuine; and

(d) the action Government has taken against the spurious milk producers?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

(SHRI GHULAM NABI AZAD)

(a): Yes.

(b) & (c): The state owned milk producers like Mother Dairy and DMS procure milk from State Cooperative Federations after following strict quality norms before acceptance of milk and their quality control laboratory are fully equipped for testing purity and adulteration of milk.

(d) The Central Government has issued instructions from time to time to Food (Health) Authorities of the States/U.Ts, who are responsible for implementation of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act in their State and U.T to keep a strict vigil on the quality of milk and milk products and take necessary preventive action under the provision of PFA Act, 1954 and Rules 1955 made thereunder.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) when was the concept of rain water harvesting introduced in the country;

(b) whether any scientific advancements have been introduced in the concept since then;

(c) whether Government has made any assessments about the gains from this concept;

(d) if so, the details in this regard;

(e) whether any scientific advancement are proposed to be added to the concept and

(f) if so, the details in this regard?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS AND WATER RESOURCES

(SHRI PAWAN KUMAR BANSAL)

(a) to (f) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (F) OF THE STARRED QUESTION NO. *285 TO BE ANSWERED ON 23.07.2009 IN RAJYA SABHA REGARDING RAIN WATER HARVESING.

(a) to (d) Rain Water Harvesting in India is an old tradition. Rain water harvesting was traditionally used for water storage. Now, Rain Water Harvesting is. also being used for augmentation of ground water recharge. Central Ground Water Board (CGWB), first took up the scheme of Rain Water Harvesting during the Fifth Five Year Plan. There hag been continuous improvement and scientific advancement, in designs of harvesting structures and techniques of ground water recharge. CGWB has employed advanced techniques of water spreading, injection well recharge and subsurface dykes for artificial recharge to ground water. The impact assessment of demonstrative recharge projects carried out by Central Ground Water Board has revealed rise in ground water level in the range of 0.15 to 12 meter in different parts of the country, (e) to (f) A demonstrative scheme on "Rain Water Harvesting and Artificial Recharge oftjrouhd Water" has been, sanctioned during Eleventh Five Year Plan. The scheme includes further development of area specific rain water harvesting and recharge methodologies as its objective.

records.qtitle: WATCHING OF KOSI RIVER THROUGH SATELLITE .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Kosi river is now being watched through satellite;

(b) if so, the names of the agencies that are doing the job;

(c) whether any data has come up suggesting risky flow of water in the months ahead and/or any embankments still needing repairs; and

(d) if so, the action contemplated in the matter?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES

(SHRI VINCENT H. PALA)

(a) to (d) National Remote Sensing Agency (NRSA), under the Department of Space, Government of India is collecting remote sensed photos periodically of the critical areas including river Kosi under the national programme. There is no information which suggests risk to the existing embankments.

records.qtitle: DOCUMENTS REQUIRED FOR OBTAINING DRIVING LICENCE .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government has issued a notification listing documents that are necessary for obtaining a driving licence;

(b) if so, the details of documents required to be furnished for obtaining a driving licence;

(c) whether the documents like voter ID cards have not been considered as sufficient ID proof;

(d) if so, the reasons therefor;

(e) whether the PAN card is must for applying for a driving licence

(f) if so, the reasons therefor; and (g) whether Government proposes to review the notification and if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS

(SHRI MAHADEO SINGH KHANDELA)

(a)&(b) Government has prescribed certain documents out of which anyone could be submitted by the applicant as proof of deemed citizen or citizen by birth. These documents are listed below:-

(i) Proof of birth in India from municipality or Registrar of Births and Deaths;

(ii) School leaving certificate/Secondary School certificate showing nationality/place of birth;

(iii) Passport showing place of birth/citizenship/nationality;

(iv) Certificate of Nationality/citizenship issued by District Magistrate or any other Administrative officer;

(v) Residency Permit/domicile certificate issued by the State Government;

(vi) Grant of patta/lease of property by the Central/State Government;

(vii)Refugee Registration Card pertaining to the period 1947-1950;

(viii) Certificate of SC/ST/OBC.

(c)&(d) Voter ID has not been included in the list. Since the requirement of proof of citizenship has been made to prevent illegal migrants from obtaining a statutory document like driving licence, the list would be further expanded on the advice of Ministry of Home Affairs.

(e)&(f) PAN Card is not required for applying for driving licence.

(g) Review of rules and notifications issued there under is a continuous process.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that admission to some courses in Universities e.g. Delhi University is conducted on the basis of the Combined Entrance Test;

(b) if so , the details of the courses admission to which is so conducted;

(c) whether it is also a fact that this negates the importance of the performance in the qualifying examination; and

(d) if so, what is the justification of the entrance test?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SMT. D. PURANDESWARI)

(a) & (b) According to the information furnished by University of Delhi, admission to most of the courses of the University is made on the basis of the performance of candidates in the qualifying examination. However, Entrance Tests are conducted for some of the courses e.g. MBBS, BDS, B.E., M.D., M.S., D.M., M.Ch., M.A., M.Sc. M.Com., M.Tech., L.L.B., B.Ed., MBA etc.

(c) & (d) No Sir. In order to become eligible to appear in the Entrance Test a candidate is required to have the prescribed percentage of marks in the qualifying examination.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that pension of pay scales of S-28, S-29 and S-30 is less than what the Pay Commission had recommended;

(b) whether the pre-revised pay scales of S-24 to S-27 were upgraded from pay band 3 to 4 and S-31 and S-32 were given a separate higher pay scale but S-28, S-29 and S-30 not only did not get any proportionate increase but actually got downgraded from Rs. 39200—67000 to Rs. 37400—67000;

(c) if so, the reasons therefor; and

(d) the steps proposed to undo the harm to the affected categories?
records.ans_text:
(Shri Namo Narain Meena)

(Minister of State in the Ministry of Finance)

(a), (b), (c) & (d): Pay Commission is a recommendatory body. Due to demands from middle level officers of Defence Forces and Group ‘A’ Services, Government placed S-24 to S-27 scales in Pay Band 4 and enhanced grade pays. So as to ensure that offices in PB-4 do not stagnate, the beginning of PB-4 was modified by the Government from Rs.39200 to Rs. 37400. Only in the case of some stages in the S-28 scale, the pension of those who retired from this scale may be less than that recommended by Sixth Pay Commission. As the pay recommended by the Sixth Pay Commission was neither approved by the Government nor drawn by the employees in S-28, the question of any harm being caused does not arise.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that a number of people serving on regulatory boards of the Ministry are also directors of companies whose projects the boards, they are serving on, have appraised;

(b) if so, the details in this regard; and

(c) what action Government has contemplated against them?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS

(SHRI JAIRAM RAMESH)

(a) & (b) No, Sir.

(c) Does not arise, in view of reply to parts (a) & (b) above.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government has taken stock of the projects which are either unfinished or yet to take off for the Commonwealth Games and the time now left;

(b) if so, the details of these projects and steps taken to complete them timely;

(c) whether it is a fact that in totality Delhi still presents a bad picture so far as hygiene, road conditions and traffic jams are concerned; and

(d) the steps being taken to address all these problems?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS

(Dr. M.S.GILL)

(a) & (b) : Yes, Sir. Construction work of Competition venues and most of the Training venues is continuing apace. In addition to above, the work at the Games Village is also progressing apace, which will accommodate around 8000 athletes and officials. Infrastructure of Delhi is also being upgraded. Time Lines, against monitorable parameters are being monitored, on a web-based monitoring system developed by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.

(c) No, Sir.

(d) To further improve the civic infrastructure of Delhi the Government of NCT of Delhi has prepared plans for giving an aesthetic look to Delhi before the Commonwealth Games, 2010 and related works have commenced. The plan includes street scaping of roads leading to various Sports Venues/ Stadia ; improvement of roads by strengthening, widening & resurfacing ; change of street lights; signages etc. Comprehensive transport plans for each venue is being finalized to streamline flow of traffic on the roads of Delhi.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government has made any assessment of the waste generated by urban India, annually;

(b) whether it is a fact that there is no systematic disposal of urban waste as pointed out by a CAG Audit Report recently;

(c) whether Government is considering steps towards scientific management of waste in urban areas of the country; and

(d) if so, the details in this regard?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS

(SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA)

(a) The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) has made an assessment on Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) generation in 59 cities (35 metros and 24 State Capitals) in the country. They have also collected information on the quantity of waste generation in 28 cities in 2007-08.

(b) to (d) CAG has given a report entitled “Management of Wastes in India”. The steps taken for scientific management of urban wastes in the country include the following:

(i) Government has notified the Municipal Solid Wastes (Management and Handling) Rules, 2000. According to these Rules, Urban Local Bodies are required to take necessary steps for proper management of municipal solid wastes.

(ii) Ministry of Urban Development has formulated the Jawahar Lal Nehru Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) scheme for providing assistance to the Urban Local Bodies for various works including solid waste management.

(iii) CPCB and the Ministry of Environment and Forests (MoEF) have sanctioned 12 demonstration projects for Municipal Solid Waste Management. The cities/towns are Ahmedabad, Agartala, Chandigarh, Itanagar- Naharlagun, Jalna, Kohima, Kozhikode, Mandi, North Dum Dum & New Barrackpore, Suryapet, South Sikkim Districts and Udumalpet,

(iv) Ministry of Environment and Forests and Central Pollution Control Board have asked all the State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs)/Pollution Control Committees (PCCs) to issue directions to the Urban Local Bodies in the States/UTs for preparing time bound action plans for management of municipal solid wastes.

(v) Government has constituted a Committee to evolve a road map for management of wastes in the country.

records.qtitle: INADEQUATE CONNECTIVITY IN BORDER AREAS IN GUJARAT .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is inadequate connectivity at Veghokot, Koteshwar and nearby areas near the Pakistan border in Gujarat; and

(b) the action Government proposes to take to provide the enhanced telecom connectivity there?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY

(SHRI JYOTIRADITYA M. SCINDIA)

(a) All the telecom service providers do not have adequate coverage at Veghokot, Koteshwer and nearby areas near the Pakistan border in Gujarat.

(b) The choice of District Headquarters/towns to be covered and further expansion beyond 50% District Headquarters/towns lie with the Licensee depending on their business decision.

records.qtitle: STOCK OF COTTON IN THE COUNTRY .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) the size of current stock of cotton available in the country in relation to the corresponding stock last year;

(b) the current size of requirements;

(c) whether it is a fact that the Cotton Corporation of India is hoarding the stock of cotton;

(d) if so, the reasons therefor;

(e) whether Government is considering a proposal to regulate the activities of the Corporation; and

(f) if so, the details in this regard?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF TEXTILES

(SHRI E.V.K.S. ELANGOVAN)

(a): Current stock of cotton in the country is estimated at 54 lakh bales (170 kgs. each) as against 43 lakh bales (170 kgs. each) during the previous year.

(b): Current size of requirement of cotton is 241 lakh bales.

(c) & (d): There is no hoarding of the stock of cotton by the Cotton Corporation of India Ltd. (CCI). CCI is a nominated government agency for procurement of cotton under Minimum Support Price operations. Whenever the market price of kapas falls below / touches the Minimum support Price (MSP), CCI is mandated to undertake support price operation and purchases kapas at MSP without any quantitative limit to safeguard the interest of the cotton farmers in the country.

(e): There is no necessity to regulate the activities of the Corporation.

(f): Does not arise in view of (e) above.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government has increased the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for the cotton this year;

(b) if so, the details in this regard and the quantum of cotton procured so far this year;

(c) whether it is also a fact that the steep increase in MSP did not take into account the global downturn, thus creating perpetual problems for the textile industry and the Cotton Corporation of India (CCI) as the prices are not likely to firm up soon; and

(d) how does Government proposes to resolve this problem?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF TEXTILES

(SHRI E.V.K.S. ELANGOVAN)

(a): Yes sir.

(b): Government of India has fixed MSP for two basic varieties (medium staple variety (F-414/H-777/J-34) and Long staple variety (H-4) for the cotton season 2008-09. MSP for long staple cotton and medium staple varieties of cotton are fixed at Rs.3000/- and Rs.2500/- per quintal leading to the hike of 48% and 39% respectively per quintal over support price fixed for 2007-08. As on 18.2.2009, Cotton Corporation of India (CCI) has purchased 75.23 lakh bales of cotton.

(c): The MSP is fixed by the Government of India every year on the recommendation of Commission on Agricultural Costs & Prices (CACP) which takes into account all the various relevant factors like cost of production of cotton including global production, consumption and domestic as well as international market price differential

(d): Does not arise.

records.qtitle: STEPS FOR SPEEDY IMPLEMENTATION OF COASTAL SECURITY PLAN .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that a plan for coastal security was initiated in 2005;

(b) if so, the details thereof including that of infrastructure sought to be provided and amount allocated for the plan;

(c) what are the details of the amount released so far, year-wise and the infrastructure created till date;

(d) whether it is also a fact that progress continues to be tardy under the plan thus neglecting coastal security of the country; and

(e) the steps contemplated for speedy implementation of the plan?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRIMATI V. RADHIKA SELVI)

(a) to (e): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether there is any proposal to revive Hindustan Machine Tools (HMT) by shifting its production activities in the field of mobile phones and compact fluorescent light (CFL) bulbs etc.; and

(b) if so, the details in this regard?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEAVY INDUSTRIES AND PUBLIC ENTERPRISES

(SHRI RAGHUNATH JHA)

(a) No, Sir.

(b) Does not arise.

records.qtitle: INDIGENISATION OF SPARE PARTS USED IN INDIAN CARS .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) what is the percentage of indigenous content of spare parts used in Indian cars at present; and

(b) by when the stage of cent per cent indigenization likely to be achieved?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEAVY INDUSTRIES AND PUBLIC ENTERPRISES

(SHRI RAGHUNATH JHA)

(a) As per statistics compiled by the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturer (SIAM), the percentage of indigenous content in vehicles in India is quite high and varies from model to model. In some models it is as high as 95%.

(b) The automobile industry world over follows integrated manufacturing process with components and systems being sourced from various places and consolidated in assembly plants. Since some of the spare parts/items are not manufactured in India, the requirement is met by import. The indigenization of the same would be possible only when the industry attains economy of scale and the domestic manufacturing of these items becomes economically viable.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government is considering a proposal to formulate national conservation policy; and

(b) if so, the details in this regard?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF TOURISM AND CULTURE

(SMT. AMBIKA SONI)

(a) & (b) There is no specific proposal to formulate a national conservation policy for historical monuments. However, as per the existing practice, the monuments declared protected under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958 are maintained and conserved by the Archaeological Survey of India depending upon the availability of resources and the needs of intervention.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) the current status of environmental pollution in the Yamuna river;

(b) whether it is a fact that Yamuna river got much dirtier recently when water plants had to be closed due to non-availability of power resulting in considerable increase of ammonia in its water;

(c) whether any action has been taken against power supply companies in this regard; and

(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT & FORESTS

(SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA)

(a) As per the water quality monitoring undertaken through independent institutions, the water quality in the stretch of the river Yamuna from Tajewala to Palla in Haryana is found to be within the prescribed limits. However, the stretch of the river in the vicinity of Delhi (downstream of Wazirabad barrage to upstream of Okhla barrage) and parts of Uttar Pradesh exceeds the standards in terms of Bio-chemical Oxygen Demand of 3.0 miligram per litre (mg/l) mainly due to enormous increase in pollution load and lack of fresh water in the river during lean period.

(b) to (d) As per information provided by Delhi Jal Board, the water treatment plants at Wazirabad and Chandrawal in Delhi, were shut down recently, due to high ammonia levels in Yamuna water. The problem of increase of ammonia in river water of Yamuna is not perennial. It occurs only due to sudden release of fresh water from Haryana (to meet the raw water demand for Delhi), that results in mixing of settled sludge in the river bed.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government has enquired into Guwahati Blasts that took place on the new year`s day this year;

(b) if so, what are the findings;

(c) whether Government has taken up the matter with Bangladesh Government; and

(d) if so, the results thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRIMATI RADHIKA V. SELVI)

(a) to (d): Government of Assam has informed that three bomb blasts took place on 1st January 2009 in different parts of Guwahati City, resulting in death of 7 persons and injuries to 69 persons. In this connection three cases have been registered and are under investigation. Preliminary investigations have revealed involvement of United Liberation Front of Asom (ULFA) militants in these incidents so far. Although during investigations, involvement of Bangladesh nationals in these incidents have not come out so far, the use of Bangladesh territory by leaders of ULFA to carry out anti-Indian activities have been taken up with Bangladesh Government at various fora.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the science behind Narco-Analysis is outdated, its practicality unproven, ethics dubious and findings not maintainable in courts;

(b) whether it is also a fact that the method of conducting the test is far from satisfactory and is liable to have side effects that ultimately may prove dangerous, if not fatal; and

(c) if so, the reasons that this is not discontinued in the country when such tests are not conducted else where in any lab of the world?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD)

(a) to (c) : The constitutionality of the NARCO Analysis test in its totality as a tool of investigation in criminal cases has been challenged through Criminal Appeal No. 1267 of 2004 in the matter of Selvi and others vs. State of Karnataka before the Supreme Court of India. The Supreme Court of India has not pronounced a verdict.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that imports from China have exceeded Rs.40,000 crores during 2008- 09;

(b) if so, whether Government is contemplating making out a case of dumping and considering steps against dumping; and

(c) if so, the details in this regard?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY

(SHRI JAIRAM RAMESH)

a) to (c) Yes, Sir. As per the statistics of DGCI&S the imports from China from April 2008 to August 2008 were of the volume of Rs 59 699 Crore. b&c) Directorate General of Anti-dumping and Allied Duties (DGAD) initiates anti-dumping investigation on receiving a fully documented petition from the domestic industry with prima-facie evidence of dumping in the country, injury to domestic industry and causal link between the dumped goods and injury. Such petitions submitted by domestic industry are processed as per the procedures and within the time limits specified under the Customs tariff act, 1975 as amended in 1995 and the rules made thereunder. These laws are in consonance with WTO’s agreement on implementation of Article VI of the GATT 1994 (commonly known as the Agreement on Anti-Dumping). After investigation, the DGAD submits its Preliminary/Final findings to the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance recommending, wherever appropriate, the amount of anti-dumping duty to be levied. Acting upon such recommendations of the DGAD, the Department of Revenue may impose the provisional or definitive duties. In 2008-09, DGAD has so far initiated fourteen (14) anti-dumping cases involving China PR. In two of these cases, Preliminary findings have been issued.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that a ship ‘SS Oceanic’ carrying 250 tonnes of asbestos, a toxic material, was headed for Alang in Saurashtra coast;

(b) whether it is a fact that Alang Ship Breaking Yard has earned infamy because of its poor handling of toxic waste from dismantled ships; and

(c) if so, the steps Government has taken on both the counts?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF CHEMICALS & FERTILSERS AND MINSITER OF STEEL

(SHRI RAM VILAS PASWAN)
(a)to(c): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN THE REPLY TO PARTS (A) TO (C) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.263 TO BE ANSWERED ON 19/12/2008 TABLED BY SHRIMATI JAYA BACHCHAN, MEMBER OF PARLIAMENT REGARDING SHIP BREAKING AT ALANG


(a) The concerned agencies have reported that they have no information about the possible arrival of the ship ‘SS Oceanic’ at Alang on the Saurashtra coast.

(b)&(c): A series of measures have been taken for attenuating the hazards of ship breaking and for improving the working conditions at shipbreaking yards at Alang. The Hon’ble Supreme Court of India has also issued comprehensive directives in this matter. Consequently, detailed protocols and procedures have been put in place for scrutinizing ships arriving for breaking and for handling and disposing of hazardous materials and wastes. The concerned nodal agency, the Gujarat Maritime Board has also developed a Treatment, Storage and Disposal Facility, (TSDF) for treatment and disposal of hazardous wastes generated from ship breaking activities at Alang. Moreover, the Gujarat State Pollution Control Board also monitors the handling of hazardous waste.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.min_name: CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is large scale smuggling of foodgrains, predominantly rice to food deficient Nepal; and

(b) if so, the steps taken by Government to curb this?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD & PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION

(DR. AKHILESH PRASAD SINGH)

(a)&(b): To check smuggling activities through international borders, Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance and Ministry of Home Affairs have their field units stationed at border check posts. Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB), which is deployed on Indo-Nepal Border, has reported that during the current year, SSB has seized food articles valued at Rs.34.638 lakh on Indo-Nepal Border. SSB has also reported that to prevent smuggling of food articles and other items from India to Nepal, vigil is maintained and required preventive action is taken.
Further, Department of Revenue, Anti Smuggling Unit (CBEC) has reported that food articles valued at Rs.355.80 lakhs have been seized on Indo-Bangladesh and Indo-Nepal Borders during the current year. They have also reported that their field formations maintain strict vigil on the Indo-Nepal and Indo-Bangladesh borders to prevent smuggling activities.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) the total area covered in the country by agriculture;

(b) whether there has been any decline in the area covered under agriculture in the last three years, year-wise;

(c) whether Government has considered increasing the area under agriculture and raising more crops than at present keeping in view of the size of population and environmental dangers ahead; and

(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI KANTI LAL BHURIA)


(a): The total agricultural land in the country in 2005-06 was 182.57 million hectares.

(b): Yes, Sir. The total agricultural land in the country in the years 2003-04, 2004-05 and 2005- 06 was 182.99 million hectares, 182.82 million hectares and 182.57 million hectares respectively, indicating a marginal decline.

(c) & (d): The Government of India has been implementing `Integrated Wastelands Development Project (IWDP) Scheme` since 1989-90. The thrust of the scheme is on development of wastelands based on village / micro watershed plans and thereby increasing the area under agriculture. The Government has also launched several major initiatives including the National Horticulture Mission, Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana and National Food Security Mission to increase agricultural production.

records.qtitle: CONTRIBUTION GIVEN TO INTERNATIONAL RICE RESEARCH INSTITUTE PHILIPPINE .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether India contributes to the budget in respect of the International Rice Research Institute, in Philippine;

(b) if so, the details of the country`s contribution to the institute for the last three years, year-wise;

(c) whether it is a fact that the Institute is facing cuts in its budget at a time when the damage to rice crops, food scarcity and high prices threaten the overall food security; and

(d) whether Government proposes to provide additional help to the Institute?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI KANTILAL BHURIA)

(a) Yes, Sir. India contributes to IRRI under both restricted funding and unrestricted funding.

(b) India is a donor member of CGIAR contributing US $ 0.75 million annually out of which contribution to IRRI is US $ 150,000 under unrestricted funding.
Besides this, India also contributes under restricted funding, the details of amount contributed in last three years are at Annexure-I.

(c) The institute is not directly under the Government of India.

(d) Government provides financial contribution to the institute commensurate with its task and our priorities.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
:-

(a) whether it is a fact that European countries are becoming major threat to Indian software companies in the near future, for example the booming software market being developed by Bulgaria; and

(b) the step being taken to counter the move?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE FOR COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY

(SHRI JYOTIRADITYA M. SCINDIA)

(a): No, Sir. As per National Association of Software and Services Companies (NASSCOM), European countries are not seen as a major threat to Indian IT-BPO companies. Europe is viewed as a growing market opportunity by the industry with share of revenues earned from the region steadily increasing.

(b): Does not arise.

records.qtitle: SUPREME COURT S STAY ON FINES FOR TRAFFIC VIOLATION .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Supreme Court has imposed an interim stay on the increase in the fines for violation of traffic rules, earlier ordered by Delhi High Court;

(b) if so, when was this order given;

(c) when was the copy of the order collected by the Traffic Police and the date when it was implemented;

(d) the total amount collected at enhanced rate after the date of order and before implementation of order; and

(e) what is the mode of disposal of enhanced fines collected after the date of order and before implementation of order?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRIMATI RADHIKA V. SELVI)

(a) to (c): The Hon’ble Supreme Court of India, in its order dated 02.05.2008, had imposed an interim stay on the direction No.1, as contained in para 55 of the impugned judgment of Hon’ble High Court of Delhi in which it was directed that “whenever any driver of any vehicle including a two wheeler is challenged by the traffic police and / or any other competent authority, he shall be liable to pay costs to Rs.500/- for each offence committed by him in addition to the composition fee payable in terms of section 200 of Motor Vehicle Act or any other enabling provision of law to that effect”. The said order was received by Delhi Traffic Police on 6.5.2008 and was implemented by Delhi Police with effect from 6/7.5.2008.

(d) & (e): Rs. 91,67,500. This was deposited in Government Treasury.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) what is the amount collected by way of taxes from Gujarat in the last 3 years, year-wise;

(b) what was the amount of Central funds provided to the State during that period, year-wise;

(c) what percentage did the Central funds constitute of the tax collection, year-wise; and

(d) whether the percentage nearly holds good for all the States?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM)


(a) to (d): The information is being collected and will be laid on the Table of the House.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that scores of child marriages took place unhindered in the country, particularly in places like Rajasthan’s interior reaches on the occasion of Akha Teej, in keeping with the past tradition;

(b) if so, what are the details in this regard; and

(c) the action Government has taken to probe and prosecute the culprits?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT

(SHRIMATI RENUKA CHOWDHURY)

(a) & (b) : Yes, Sir. The problem of child marriage still exists in some parts of the country. As reported by National Crime Record Bureau, 99, 96 and 78 cases were registered under Child Marriage Restraint Act, 1929 during 2006, 2007 and 2008 respectively in the country. As per information received from the State Government of Rajasthan, the number of cases registered relating to child marriage were 1, 3 and 3 during the year 2006, 2007 and 2008 respectively.

(c) : In order to prohibit child marriages and to make the provisions of the Act more effective and punishment more stringment for offenders, a new legislation “The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006” (No. 6 of 2007) has been notified in the Gazettee of India on 11the January, 2007 and the said Act has been enforced w.e.f. 1.11.2007. The Act provides appointment of Child Marriage Prohibition Officers in each State/UT. Also, awareness generation and advocacy measures which are continuously being undertaken by the Ministry of Women and Child Development will help in prohibiting child marriages.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that rice crop in East Asia is being damaged by an insect known as the Brown Plant Hopper, which is multiplying by the billions and chewing rice paddy thus threatening diets of poor people;

(b) whether Government has examined the possibility of the insect reaching India and damaging the rice crops in the country; and

(c) if so, the steps being taken to address the problem?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI KANTI LAL BHURIA)

(a)&(b): The Brown Plant Hopper is an insect pest of paddy in the rice growing countries of East Asia. As per survey reports received from State Departments of Agriculture and the Central Integrated Pest Management Centres (CIPMCs), trace to moderate incidence of Brown Plant Hopper has been reported from isolated fields of Kerala State and moderate to severe incidence of Brown Plant Hopper has been reported from Haryana State.

(c): Experts from Government of India have already visited the affected areas in Haryana. Presently, the insect is under control. The Government of India has adopted Integrated Pest Management (IPM) as the main strategy for plant protection, including paddy crop. Awareness for pest control through IPM approach is spread among the farmers under the scheme “Strengthening and Modernization of Pest Management Approach in India” through Farmers’ Field Schools organized by 31 CIPMs across the country.

records.qtitle: RETRIEVING OF HERITAGE FILMS LOST FROM ARCHIVE .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) Whether it is fact that chunk of heritage films have been lost forever;

(b) whether it is also a fact that a majority of films that have vanished without a trace, dating back to 1930s and 1940s;

(c) The reasons for which the Film Board of India did not act in the matter;

(d) Whether Government proposes to enlist public cooperation in retrieving prints of those films, to the extent possible; and

(e) If not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR EXTERNAL AFFAIRS AND INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING

(SHRI ANAND SHARMA)


(a) & (b) : No, Sir. Out of 5095 reels (607 films) on nitrate base lost in the fire accident on 08.01.2003 at Film & Television Institute of India (FTII), Pune, content of 544 reels was lost. The other reels had been copied on safety base and are stored at NFAI. The lost reels (544) consisted of incomplete films and/or single reels. The nitrate base has generally not been used by the industry after 1950s.

(c) : The National Film Archive of India (NFAI), Pune was established in 1964. NFAI has acquired films depending on both the availability of films and the allocated funds. NFAI has a large collection of films from silent era to the recent ones including about 400 films (Indian and foreign) produced in the years until the 1940s.

(d) & (e): Since its inception, NFAI has enlisted public co-operation by appealing to the public and film industry for help in retrieving films.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that calls made from Delhi to NCR towns and vice vers are still not treated as local calls and don not materialize without a STD code particularly to places like Palwal, Sonepat, Meerut, Alwar, gurgaon etc.;

(b) if so, the reasons thereof;

(c) whether it is a fact that the city code does not enable many land line and mobile phones to access these cities due to poor technology or other reasons;

(d) whether this defeats the concept of NCR; and

(e) whether Government proposes to address the matter?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY

(SHRI JYOTIRADITYA M. SCINDIA)

(a) & (b) Yes, Sir. The calls made from MTNL Delhi network to NCR towns and vice-versa are materialized by dialing 95 followed by city code and subscriber number as these places are not part Delhi short Distance Charging Area (SDCA). This facility is available to all subscribers irrespective of whether they are having STD facility or not.

(c) No, Sir.

(d) & (e) Does not arise in view of (c ) above.

records.qtitle: EFFECT OF NREGS ON MIGRANT LABOUR IN PUNJAB .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that as a result of implementation of NREGA East-West corridor, the number of migrants from Bihar and UP has gone down considerably;

(b) whether this has affected paddy cultivation in States like Punjab which is experiencing severe labour crunch and is set to bring down the area under paddy cultivation; and

(c) the steps taken by Government to address the problem?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI CHANDRA SEKHAR SAHU)

(a) There is no programme by the name `NREGA East-West corridor` being implemented by the Ministry. However, Government had enacted National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005 in September, 2005. The Act provides for a legal guarantee for 100 days of wage employment to adult members of every rural household in a financial year for doing unskilled manual work on demand. The workers are free to avail any other employment opportunity available to them in their State or elsewhere. NREGA has been extended to the rural areas in the country in a phased manner. 200 districts were covered in the first phase with effect from 2.2.2006. 130 additional districts were covered in the second phase during the year 2007-08 and all the remaining rural areas have been covered under the Act from 1.4.2008.

(b) This Ministry has not received any report from the Governemnt of Punjab regarding paddy cultivation being affected in the State due to labour crunch on account of launch of NREGA.

(c) Does not arise.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that country`s iron-ore experts have advised on restricting or stopping altogether the export of iron-ore as it is considered worse than selling family silver;

(b) the factors that prevent us from selling it at best prices in the world than dumping it at cheapest prices;

(c) if so, whether Government has taken any decision on export of iron-ore; and

(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY

(SHRI JAIRAM RAMESH)

(a) An expert Committee, constituted by the Central Government, examined the issue of restrictions on iron ore export. The Committee consulted the various stakeholders including State Governments and submitted its report which was considered by the Government. Government agreed to the recommendation of the expert Committee that restrictions on export of iron ore are not required, while holding that even though conservation of iron ore resources of the country is of paramount importance, the same may not be achieved by banning or capping the export of iron ore but by taking recourse to appropriate fiscal measures.

(b) Indian ore in the export market till very recently was very competitively priced. For instance, in the month of April, 2008 the spot price of Indian iron ore was US$ 145 per metric tonne on FOB basis as compared to approximately US$ 134 per metric tonne which was the price of iron ore being exported by other countries on long term agreement basis. However, the spot price of Indian ore has come down to US$ 51 per metric tonne on FOB basis in November, 2008 and the iron ore exports have also come down from 52.65 million tonnes for the period from 1st April to 15th November, 2007 to 45.20 million tonnes for the same period during the current financial year.

(c)&(d) In view of (a) & (b) above, there is no change in the policy of Government on export of iron ore.

records.qtitle: RADIATION FROM MINERALS AT KANYAKUMARI BEACH
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that extreme parts of coastal areas of southern India, particularly the sea beaches of Kanyakumari have high levels of natural radiation that emanates from the minerals found on beaches;

(b) whether it is a fact that a new study has revealed that radiation figures in some places near Kanyakumari are 50 times more than the world average and this could be a cause for cancer; and

(c) if so, whether Government has taken any steps to address the problem and warn visitors to the area, and if not, the reasons therefore?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

(SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)

(a) to (c): The Ministry of Health & Family Welfare including Indian Council of Medical Research has neither conducted nor supported any study for the purpose.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is shortage of fertilizers in different parts of the country;

(b) if so, the details in this regard;

(c) whether it is also a fact that production of fertilizers in the country has gone down following closure of some plants; and

(d) the steps Government has taken to address the problem?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS & FERTILIZERS AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF MINES

(SHRI B.K. HANDIQUE)

(a) & (b) : The availability of major fertilizers viz., Urea, DAP and MOP in the country during Kharif 2008 has been over and above the assessed requirement / sales as under: 
 

(Qty. in LMT)
Fertilizer	Requirement			Availability		Sales		
DAP		42.75				53.19			52.85
MOP		17.19				22.79			21.55
UREA		137.11				134.66		       127.92
/pre>


	About 10.4 L.MT of Urea was available in the field godowns at the start 
of the Kharif 2008 season which has not been included. As such there is no 
scarcity of fertilizers.


Urea is the only fertilizer under partial movement and distribution control of 
the Government. Union Government ensures availability of urea at State level 
and . the State governments are responsible for its distribution within the 
State.     However, the Department of Fertilizers monitors the availability of 
fertilizers up to district level



	All other fertilizer ( Phosphatic and Potassic ) viz., DAP, MOP, SSP and 
NPK etc. ate decontrolled / de- canalized since 1992 The availability of 
Phosphatic and Potassic fertilizers is decided by the market forces of demand 
and supply.


(c) & (d) :During 2007-08, production of Phosphatic fertilizers has 
declined on account of steep increase in price of raw materials. This decline 
cannot be attributed to closure of Units.

records.qtitle: UNTAPPED RESERVES  OF URANIUM IN INDIA
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that nuclear plants are presently starved because of non- of uranium;

(b) if so, whether it is a fact that there are massive untapped reserves of uranium, estimated at over 1 lakh tonnes, in the States of Jharkhand, Meghalaya, Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan and Tamilnadu; and

(e) the reasons for these reserves having remained untapped, whereas we have been pursuing foreign resources ?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE PRIME MINISTER`S OFFICE AND MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS

(SHRI PRITHVIRAJ CHAVAN)

(a) to (c) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO RAJYA SABHA QUESTION NO. 83 BY SMT. JAYA BACHCHAN; SHRI N.K. SINGH REGARDING UNTAPPED RESERVES OF URNAIUM IN INDIA FOR ANSWER ON 23.10.2008.

(a) Fuel demand-Supply mismatch has led to operation of nuclear power plants at reduced capacity factors

(b) Atomic Minerals Directorate for Exploration& Research. (AMD) has identified just above 1 lakh tonnes reserves of uranium in the States of Jharkhand, Meghalaya, Andhra Pradesh and Rajasthan Mines are either in production or in development covering all viable deposits in which accounts for nearly half of this resource. Concerned efforts had been made to develop mines in other states over last several years and are expected to produce positive results in spite of difficulties such as land acquisition, mining lease, rehabilitation/resettlement of affected persons, environmental and forest clearances, public consensus.etc...

(c) While there is no slackening of efforts to fully tap all potentially viable uranium resources, efforts to access foreign resources should be seen as efforts to bring in additionality to domestic resources

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the concept of National Capital Region (NCR) has still not translated into a reality;

(b) if not, the reasons for there being no integrated and harmonious approach towards problems facing the region like transport, law and order, water sharing, etc., even now; and

(c) the reasons for the towns under NCR not being well connected by transport, metro operations and private means of transport thus adding to the woes of commuters?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT

( SHRI AJAY MAKEN )

(a)&(b): No, Sir. The National Capital Region Planning Board Act, 1985 has enabled creation of the NCR Planning Board to prepare, coordinate and monitor implementation of Regional(s) Plan for the NCR. The Board has undertaken various planning exercises and has played an important role in bringing about harmonious development of the Region. The Regional Plan of the National Capital Region deals with various aspects like transport, power, water, sewerage, solid waste management, institutional mechanism to control and monitor criminal activities, police modernization in NCR etc.

(c): NCR towns are fairly well connected by transport through road and rail network Presently, five National Highways radiate from Delhi viz. NH-1, NH-2, NH-8, NH-10 and NH-24. Apart from these five, other National Highways also strengthen the road network of NCR viz. NH-91, NH-58, NH-71, NH-71A and NH-71B. Two peripheral Expressways around Delhi are under
CONTD....2 .PA - 2 -

implementation. The State Highways are also spread all over NCR viz. SH-10 (Gohana-Jind), SH-11 (Muzaffarnagar-Panipat-Jind), SH-13 (Alwar-Jaipur), SH-14 (Alwar-Mathura), SH-16

(Rohtak-Bhiwadi), SH-18 (Bulandshahar-Moradabad), SH-20

(Jhajjar-Charkhi Dadri), SH-22 (Jhajjar-Mahendragarh), SH-24

(Rewari-Mahendragarh), SH-25 (Alwar-Narnaul), SH-39

(Anupshahar-Aligarh), SH-47 (Meerut-Bijnor), SH-57

(Baghpat-Shamli). In addition to the above, the NCR is well knitted with District Roads. It has also been decided to extend Delhi Metro Rail to other towns, namely, Noida and Gurgaon.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) the number of projects currently in progress in Arunachal Pradesh and the total length of roads proposed to be built there;

(b) whether any time-frame has been fixed for the purpose; and

(c) if so, the details in this regard?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS

(SHRI K.H. MUNIYAPPA)



(a) to (c): This Ministry is concerned with the improvement and up keep of National Highways and improvement of identified State Roads, General Staff Roads , Strategic Roads and roads under Special Accelerated Road Development Programme in the North Eastern (SARDP-NE) and Centrally Sponsored Scheme viz. Central Road Fund(CRF), Inter-state Connectivity(ISC) & Economic Importance(EI). The number of projects currently in progress and the time frame for their completion under National Highway (Original), SARDP-NE and the project of ISC/EI is given in the Annexure. In respect of the work of State roads funded under CRF, 21 works aggregating to about 170 km length of State roads are in progress. Ministry does not stipulate completion date for CRF works and it is decided by the State Government, depending upon the availability of funds.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that different types of crime has registered increase in the National Capital Region (NCR) in the last one year or so;

(b) whether it is also a fact that in the lost 5 months alone 180 cases of snatching took place in Delhi;

(c) whether the number of murders, rapes, robberies, incidents of road rage and fatal accidents involving police personnel and other in Delhi, Noida, Gurgaon, Greater Noida, etc. have considerably increased; and

(d) if so, the reasons therefor and the step taken to curb the crime?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRIMATI V. RADHIKA SELVI)

(a) According to National Crime Records Bureau(NCRB), which collects data on crimes in the country, while some kinds of crime have increased slightly, some other kinds of crime have decreased in the NCR during 2007 as compared to 2006.

(b) According to Delhi Police, 621 cases of snatching have been registered in the last 5 months i.e 1.5.2008 to 30.9.2008 in Delhi.

(c) NCRB does not maintain information on incidents of road rage. The information on victims of road accident without breakup into fatal and non-fatal accident is available only for Delhi out of the 14 NCR Districts. The cases of road accidents in Delhi have increased from 9699 in 2006 to 10528 in 2007, while the number of persons killed and number of persons injured have gone down from 2167 and 8764 in the year 2006 to 2112 and 8480 in the year 2007 respectively.
As compared to the year 2007 to the year 2006, the cases of rape in Delhi have decreased while those of robberies and murder have increased; In Gurgaon the cases of murder remained static while the cases of rape and robberies have increased; In Gautam Budh Nagar(including Noida & Greater Noida) the cases of rape & murder have decreased while those of robberies have increased.

(d) As per the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India, “Police” and “Public Order” are State subject and, as such, the primary responsibility of prevention, detection, registration, investigation and prosecution of Crime lies with the concerned State Government. The Union Government, however, attaches highest importance to the matter of prevention of crime and therefore, impresses upon the State Governments and UT Administrations from time to time, to give more focused attention to the prevention and control of crimes within their jurisdiction.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that a devastating dust storm hit Kanpur city on 14th May, 2008;

(b) whether it is also a fact that a large number of villages in the area were gutted in fire stoked by winds; and

(c) if so, the details of the loss of life and property and extent of relief provided to the victims?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRIMATI V. RADHIKA SELVI)

(a): As per the information received from the government of Uttar Pradesh, a high speed cyclonic dust storm hit Kanpur city leading to accidental fire at different places.

(b): A few villages were also reported gutted by high speed cyclonic dust storm leading to accidental fire.

(c): The State Government has reported loss of 6 human lives, 13 cattle heads and private properties worth Rs. 30,96,895.00. The Government of Uttar Pradesh extended relief of Rs. 1,22,800.oo to the victims.

records.qtitle: OPENING OF ANDAMAN NICOBAR ISLANDS FOR TOURISM .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether there is any fresh proposal under consideration to open a large number of Andaman & Nicobar Islands for tourism;

(b) if so, the details in this regard; and

(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM AND CULTURE

(SMT. AMBIKA SONI)

(a) to (c) : Tourism is being developed and promoted in a phased manner taking into account security, forest regulations and restrictions as per provisions of Andaman and Nicobar Islands (Protection of Aboriginal Tribes) Regulation, 1956.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government has recently imposed export duty on rice;

(b) if so, the details in this regard;

(c) whether it is a fact that as a result of imposition of export duty, domestic exporters have been faltering on commitments;
