records.qtitle: SALE OF LPG CYLINDERS THROUGH PETROL PUMPS .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that LPG dealers in the Northern part of the country have created an artificial shortage of LPG cylinders;

(b) if so, the steps Government has taken against the erring dealers;

(c) whether Government is considering any proposal to start the sale of LPG cylinders through petrol pumps in a convenient packing; and

(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS

(SHRI DINSHA PATEL)


(a) : Public Sector Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) have reported that at present, there is no overall shortage of LPG in the country and LPG supplies to distributors are being made by the OMCs through indigenous production and imports in accordance with the genuine demand of customers registered with the LPG distributors.

However, OMCs had reported backlog in LPG supplies in certain States in the country due to a combination of factors viz., reduction in supply of bulk LPG compared to the target by Reliance Industries Limited (RIL) & Essar Oil Limited in January-February, 2008, delay in movement of bulk LPG by rail from Jamnagar to the Northern Region, increased demand in the States due to severe cold which resulted in panic booking by the customers, strikes by contract labour, agitational activities, delays in berthing of vessels at Haldia Port due to reduced draft, bandhs etc.

Government had advised OMCs to liquidate the backlog in the country by operating the bottling plants on holidays and during extended hours. Increased bottling was also done during the working days for early clearance of backlog.

At present, OMCs have not reported any backlog in supply of LPG in the country. OMCs are monitoring the situation on a day-to-day basis and corrective action is being taken wherever required.

(b) : The possibility of blackmarketing/diversion of subsidized domestic LPG cylinders by some unscrupulous elements cannot be ruled out due to the wide gap between the retail price of LPG for domestic use and the market price for commercial LPG.

In order to stop blackmarketing/diversion of domestic LPG cylinders, the Government has enacted “Liquefied Petroleum Gas (Regulation of Supply and Distribution) Order, 2000” and formulated “Marketing Discipline Guidelines, 2001” which provides for penal action against LPG distributors indulging in diversion/ blackmarketing of LPG.

Whenever OMCs receive complaints, these are investigated and if the complaint is established, suitable action is taken against the LPG distributor(s) in accordance with the provisions of the Marketing Discipline Guidelines (MDG). MDG provides for following action against the distributor:-

- Fine of Rs. 20,000 plus the price of LPG diverted at commercial rates for 1st offence.
- Fine of Rs. 50,000 plus the price of LPG diverted at commercial rates for 2nd offence.
- Termination of the distributorship for 3rd offence.

In addition to the action taken by the OMCs, State Governments are empowered under the LPG (Regulation of Supply & Distribution) Order, 2000 promulgated under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 to take action against blackmarketing/diversion of domestic LPG. Similarly, the Weights and Measures Departments of the States / UTs initiate legal action against those LPG distributors found blackmarketing/diversion of LPG cylinders. The State Governments have been alerted from time to time to take steps against the blackmarketing/diversion of domestic cylinders for unauthorized usage.

(c) to (d) : No, Sir. Government is not considering any proposal for selling LPG cylinders through petrol pumps, as the present regulations do not permit sale of LPG cylinders at petrol pumps.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that drugs banned in a number of countries continues to be on sale in the country;

(b) if so, what are the reasons therefor;

(c) whether it is also a fact that the list of banned drugs includes medicines like Nimesulide, banned in over 170 countries, and at least 11 drugs, used for common cures continue to be sold freely in the country;

(d) whether it is a fact that this poor State of affairs is due to absence of poor monitoring mechanism; and

(e) if so, the steps Government have taken in this regard?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

(SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)

(a) to (c): A drug, banned in a specific country, may not call for its withdrawal in other countries. Every country has its own regulatory system for approving or banning drugs after examining overall benefit risk ratio of the drug and its requirement in the country. Drugs, for which harmful effects or inadequate therapeutic justification is reported in the context of current medical evidence, are examined by Drugs Technical Advisory Board (DTAB) on a continuous basis. Based on the recommendations of DTAB, so far, 78 drugs/drug formulations have been prohibited for marketing in the country. Sale of banned drugs in the country is a punishable offence under Section 28B of Drugs and Cosmetics Act. Nimesulide is not banned in over 170 countries. Due to its withdrawal/suspension in some countries, Nimesulide is currently under focused surveillance in the National Pharmacovigilance Programme.

(d) No, Sir.

(e) Question does not arise.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan

THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

(SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)

(a) to (d): Grievance Redressal Committee/Cells do already exist in Central Government Hospitals under the Chairmanship of Addl. Medical Superintendents. To enable the public to lodge written complaints/suggestions/grievances, various complaint boxes have been installed at different locations in the hospital premises. These boxes are opened periodically and then all complaints/suggestions/grievances received from patients/visitors are put up before the grievance committee. The Grievance Committee meets every week/month to examine the same on the basis of action taken note received from concerned departments/sections on the complaints/suggestions/grievances and accordingly decision/recommendation of the Grievance Committee is communicated to the administration for their redressal.

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI KANTI LAL BHURIA)


(a): As per the 3rd Advance Estimates released on 22nd April 2008, production of cotton in the country is estimated at 23.19 million bales of 170 kg each ( 3.94 milltion tonnes) during 2007-08.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government is contemplating to set up pollution free townships like the Masdar township established in 7 Km desert adjoining Abu Dhabi in United Arab Emirates; and

(b) if so, the details in the regard?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT & FORESTS

(SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA)

(a)&(b): Steps are informed to have been undertaken for setting up a Masdar township at a huge investment adjoining Abu Dhabi in United Arab Emirates based on power generated from solar energy. The Government of India at present has no scheme for setting up a township like the Masdar township.

To abate and control air and water pollution in cities, various steps have been initiated including the following:

Emission and effluent standards have been notified for various categories of industries under the provisions of the Environment (Protection) Rules, 1986.

The air quality is monitored at 339 locations in 126 cities/towns across 25 States and 4 UTs in the country.

Action plans for improvement of Air quality have been prepared and implemented for 16 cities.

Cleaner fuels have been introduced for: control of vehicular pollution as per Auto Fuel Policy.

Source Apportionment Studies for suspended particulate matter (SPM) and respirable suspended particulate matter (RSPM) have been initiated for ascertaining contribution from various sources in six cities, namely, Delhi, Kanpur, Mumbai, Pune, Bangalore and Chennai through various institutions.

For controlling water pollution emanating from Small Scale Industries units, a centrally sponsored scheme for establishment of Common Effluent Treatment Plant (CETP) is under implementation.

records.qtitle: BLACK CARBON CLOUD OVER THE COUNTRY .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that scientists have warned that Black Carbon cloud over the country rings alarm bells; and

(b) if so, the steps Government has taken to end continued dependence on coal based power plants and growing vehicular pollution, which has pushed the country towards an inevitable climatic catastrophe?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS

(SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA)

(a) The Atmospheric Brown Cloud (ABC) refers to the high loading of pollutants in the atmosphere consisting of mixture of anthropogenic sulphate, nitrate, organics, black carbon, dust and fly ash particles and natural aerosols such as sea salt and mineral dust.
The exact impacts of pollutant loading over monsoon rain and agriculture are still under study and the International program on Atmospheric Brown Cloud has been initiated by the world community to understand such impacts.

(b) Considering the fact that coal is to remain mainstay for generation of electricity in India in short to medium term perspective, new plants are being encouraged to adopt more efficient and clean coal technologies. Besides, 1,50,000 MW hydro initiative has been launched to achieve the objective of full hydro potential. Non Conventional Energy sources are also being encouraged and 11,125 MW out of total installed capacity of 1,43,061 MW in the country is contributed by renewables. Measures have also been taken to improve the air quality and reduce the pollutant loading e.g. introduction of tightened emission norms for vehicle, improvement in fuel quality in transport sector, use of cleaner fuels, introduction of electrostatic precipitators in thermal power plants, introduction of biogas plants and improved cookers in rural sector etc.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Indian Meteorological Department has studied the extreme changes reflected in the weather patterns in the northern and other parts of the country this year;

(b) whether any observations have been made on the causes of extreme weather or the trends to come; and

(c) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY AND MINISTER OF EARTH SCIENCES

(SHRI KAPIL SIBAL)

(a) to (c) : A Statement is laid on the Table of the House
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 428 FOR ANSWER ON 23rd April, 2008.

(a,b&c) India Meteorological Department (IMD) has been studying the trends of the important weather parameters and also constantly monitoring the occurrence of extreme weather events over various parts of the country. Data pertaining to the period 1901-2005 suggests that annual mean temperature for the country as a whole has risen to 0.51oC over the period. A study, which focuses on monsoon season, clearly shows that though mean monsoon rainfall remained stable (without any increasing or decreasing trend) over the Indian sub-continent, the frequency of occurrence of extreme rain events has increased about 1% per year during past 50 years.
These trends may be explained in the backdrop of global warming and increasing trend in the mean temperature of earth over the past 50 years. Increase in air temperature increases the moisture holding capacity through the amplification of instability arising from small local disturbances. In the coming decades, increasing trends of extreme weather events are likely to increase for most of the parts of India. Some of the important weather events of this year are attached as Annexure.
The excess rainfall during March 2008 over South Peninsula was due to enhanced activity of the easterly waves over the equatorial Indian Ocean. The sea surface temperature and wind anomalies over the equatorial Indian Ocean observed during the month were favourable for such excess rainfall activity over South peninsula. This kind of rainfall activity has been observed in the past also. However, the amount of rainfall received over South peninsula during the month of March 2008 was unprecedented.
Determining whether a specific, single extreme event is due to a specific cause is difficult as i) Extreme events are usually caused by a combination of weather factors and ii) A wide range of extreme events is a normal occurrence even in an unchanging climate (Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change –4th Assessment Report)

records.qtitle: EMPLOYMENT IN URBAN AND RURAL AREAS .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that booming economy has failed to check unemployment in the country;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and

(c) what steps Government propose to take to increase the pace of employment in urban as well as rural areas?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT

(SHRI OSCAR FERNANDES)

(a) to (c): As per two most recent quinquennial rounds of National Sample Survey Organisation (NSSO) on employment and unemployment, unemployment rate on Current Daily Status basis has been estimated at 7.31% in 1999-2000 (55th round) and 8.28% in 2004-05. The employment opportunities were estimated at 338.19 million in 1999-2000 (55th round) and 384.91 million in 2004-05 (61st round). The 11th Five Year Plan provides a framework to restructure policies to achieve a new vision based on faster, more broad-based and inclusive growth. It aims at making employment generation an integral part of the growth process and devise strategies to accelerate not only growth of employment but also of wages of the poorly paid. The 11th Plan document approved by National Development Council has projected that 58 million job opportunities on Current Daily Status are likely to be created during the 11th Plan period. Besides, Government of India is implementing various employment generation and poverty alleviation programmes in both rural and urban areas to increase employment opportunities. Some of the important ones are- Swarana Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana (SJSRY); Prime Minister’s Rozgar Yojana (PMRY); Swarnjayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY); Rural Employment Generation Programme (REGP); Sampoorna Grameen Rozgar Yojana (SGRY) and National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (NREGA), 2005. Steps have been initiated to identify and implement systematic reforms in administration of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) so as to facilitate closer interaction with the industry in order to improve quality of training, make the graduates better employable and help them earn

(c) if so, the details in this regard;

THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR YOUTH AFFAIRS & SPORTS

(DR. M.S. GILL)

(a) For almost all the major sports/civic infrastructure projects, related to Commonwealth Games 2010, the detailed designs and estimates have been approved, tender process has been completed, and construction work has commenced. All stakeholders, have indicated specific time-lines with reference to key milestones of each project, up to its targetted date of completion of the work, and the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports, has set up a web-based monitoring system, to monitor and review progress of projects. The construction work on most of the projects is progressing satisfactorily and would be completed well before the CWG 2010.

(b) & (c): No structure is being constructed on the river bed. However, the Games Village, is being constructed farther side of the river on land which has been reclaimed, from the flood plains of river Yamuna. This is a Delhi Development Authority Project for which they have obtained mandatory clearance from the concerned agency.

(d) & (e): Yes, Sir. Some Non-Government Organizations have filed a writ petition in the High Court of Delhi, titled `Rajender Singh & Others Versus Government of NCT of Delhi & Others`, The Hon`ble Court has heard the arguments of both the parties, and the final decision has been kept reserved.

records.qtitle: DE SEALING OF UNAUTHORISED PROPERTIES NO.
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government has decided to de-seal the unauthorised properties recently sealed under court orders;

(b) if so, the reasons for the proposed action at this point of time after causing much inconvenience and harassment to the citizens of Delhi; and

(c) the reasons that this course of action was not considered earlier which could have saved lakhs of traders of the losses and displacement caused to them?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT

( SHRI AJAY MAKEN )

(a)to(c): The National Capital Territory of Delhi Laws (Special Provisions) Act, 2007 was published for general information on 5.12.2007. The Act provided for maintaining status quo in respect of unauthorized development in the form of encroachment by slum dwellers and jhuggi-jhompri clusters, hawkers and urban street vendors, unauthorized colonies, village abadi area and its extension, existing farm houses involving construction beyond permissible building limits and schools, dispensaries, religious institutions, cultural institutions, storages, warehouses and godowns used for agricultural inputs or produce (including dairy and poultry) in rural areas built on agricultural land. The Act empowered Central Government to issue such directions to the local authorities as it may deem fit for giving effect to the provisions of the Act. Accordingly, Central Government issued directions (including the direction to deseal the properties protected under the above mentioned law) to the local bodies by issue of Notification dated 30.1.2008. The directions were issued after appropriate consideration of a reference received from Municipal Corporation of Delhi on the matter on 1.1.2008.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the country’s space programme is concluding shortly;

(b) what have been the achievements of the programme in brief;

(c) whether any activities are proposed to be taken up shortly based on the experience of developed countries; and

(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE PRIME MINISTER’S OFFICE AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES & PENSIONS

(SHRI PRITHVIRAJ CHAVAN):

(a) No, Sir.

(b) India has achieved self reliance in the areas of

(i) building state-of-the-art remote sensing and communication satellites and
(ii) launch capability through Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV) for launching of remote sensing satellites and Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV) for launching communication satellites. Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) has used these space systems for developmental applications such as tele-education, telemedicine, Village Resource Centers, natural resources management, etc.

(c) ISRO has long term plans to develop Communication and Navigation Satellites; Remote Sensing Satellites; efficient space transportation systems; space exploration; atmospheric sciences and inter-planetary missions. These plans are inline with the plans of developed countries

(d) Does not arise.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that an interceptor and diversion scheme has been cleared with a view to cleanse Yamuna of its pollution;

(b) if so, the details in this regard including details of expenditure, the level of cleanliness likely to be achieved and the amount already spent so far and the results achieved;

(c) the manner in which the current scheme is different from the ones implemented in the past; and

(d) whether there is any similar scheme for rest of the rivers in the country ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS

(SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA)

(a) to (c) According to the information provided by the Government of NCT of Delhi, Delhi Jal Board (DJB) has evolved the concept of laying interceptor sewers along the three major drains namely, Najafgarh, Supplementary and Shahdara in Delhi to prevent the flow of untreated sewage and its treatment before discharge to river Yamuna. The salient features of DJB’s proposal include laying of interceptor sewers, augmentation of existing capacity of sewage treatment plants (STPs) and construction of additional sewage treatment plants after full utilization of existing STPs. The proposal takes care of the untreated sewage from unsewered areas and allows only discharge of treated effluent into river Yamuna. The tentative cost of the project is about Rs. 1300 crore. So far no expenditure has been incurred on the project. This concept is similar to the works implemented under Yamuna Action Plan, launched by Government of India in a phased manner.

(d) Under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of National River Conservation Plan (NRCP), pollution abatement works are implemented to improve the water quality in the identified polluted stretches of major rivers in the Country. These works include interception and diversion of raw sewage flowing into the rivers, setting up of Sewage Treatment Plants for treating the diverted sewage, creation of low cost sanitation facilities, setting up of electric/improved wood crematoria and River Front Development among others. Presently, NRCP covers pollution abatement works in 164 towns along polluted stretches of 35 rivers spread over 20 States at an approved cost of Rs. 4863.75 crore.

records.qtitle: ACTION TO CHECK ROAD RAGE ACCIDENTS IN THE METROS .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that road rage has considerably increased in the metros of the country;

(b) the number of persons killed in the road rage accidents in Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata in the last one year; and

(c) the action being contemplated to check road rage accidents in the metros?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD)

(a): The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) does not maintain data on `road rage` accidents. However, Delhi Police has provided the following data relating to `road rage’ accidents in Delhi: 
Year	Cases registered
2005	18
2006	27
2007	27
2008(upto 31.3.2008)	12
 


(b):	  According to Delhi Police, one person was killed in `road rage` accident in Delhi during 2007. Such data in respect of Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata is not available. 


(c):	  `Road rage` is basically an attitudinal problem.  Delhi Police has taken the following measures to control `road rage`:


(i)  	proper regulation and control of traffic, particularly during the peak hours to ensure hassle free movement of traffic and reduction in journey time;


(ii)  	enforcement of traffic laws & rules and regulations to check traffic violations and to bring road discipline amongst drivers;


(iii)  	education of motorists and other road users to observe road safety norms and to give due regard and respect to other road users;


(iv)  	vigilance on roads by Traffic Police, Police Control Room (PCR) and Mobile Teams; and 


(v)  	strict legal action against the aggressors involved in road rage.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that industrial production in the country has slowed down to 5.3 per cent since last November;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and

(c) the action taken to speed up the tempo of production?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY

(SHRI ASHWANI KUMAR)

(a): The industrial growth, measured in terms of Index of Industrial Production (IIP), was 5.1% during November 2007. For the first 10 months of current financial year (April-January, 2007-08), the industrial growth was 8.7% compared to 11.2% during corresponding period of last year.

(b) & (c): In a market driven economy, the growth of various industries is influenced by market-forces of supply and demand. The deceleration of the industrial growth is due to a combination of factors such as rise in interest rates, rupee appreciation etc.
The Government has put in place various policies to promote broad based industrial growth. This includes, inter-alia, delicensing of industrial capacity, liberalization of foreign trade regime to provide better access to inputs at competitive prices, rationalization and reduction in duty rates of customs and central excise, better infrastructure support, and liberal FDI regime, etc. In the Budget 2008-09, the Government has proposed reduction in excise duty across the board from 16% to 14% to boost the domestic demand for the manufacturing industry. In addition, the Government has also proposed reduction in excise duty from 16% to 12% in the Budget 2008-09 for Small Cars, Motorcycles, and Scooters etc. to give boost to the domestic consumer durable manufacturing industry. Government has announced several relief measures for export oriented industries, which includes enhancement of the Duty Entitlement Pass Book (DEPB), reduction in Export Credit Guarantee Corporation (ECGC) premium by 10%, enhancement of the rates of duty drawback, interest subvention of pre-shipment and post-shipment credit, refund of service tax, raising the revenue ceiling for Vishesh Krishi and Gram Udyog Yojana.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government had warned cement industry of being taken over in case the price of cement was not lowered;

(b) if so, whether the cement industry has heeded the warning and reduced the price of cement, if so, the details thereof; and

(c) if not, the action Government are contemplating against the industry?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY

(SHRI ASHWANI KUMAR)

(a) to (c) : No, Sir. The prices of cement increased sharply between December, 2005 and March, 2007 due to mismatch between demand and supply. The Government has taken a number of measures to increase the supply of cement in the market to cater to increased demand. These include facilitating import by reducing the import duty on cement to ‘Nil’, removal of countervailing duty and special additional customs duty. Further, MMTC Ltd, a Government of India enterprises, TANCEM, a State Government enterprises of Tamil Nadu and M/s. Puducherry Agro Services Industries Corporation (PASIC) have been given a special dispensation to import cement under the provisions of Cement (Quality Control) Order, 2003 to enable availability of significant quantities of imported cement in the market. With these measures, the average price of cement has stabilized to a large extent showing an increase of only 4.44% between March, 2007 and March, 2008. Government have also made it clear that it shall not condone cartelization and profiteering by cement companies.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government has drawn any projections for the tourist inflow in the country in the next financial year in view of the current turmoil in the global markets;

(b) if so, what are the details in this regard; and

(c) the details of the strategy planned to meet and at the same time encourage the tourist inflow?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM AND CULTURE

(SMT. AMBIKA SONI)

(a) to (c): The number of foreign tourist arrivals (FTAs) in 2008 is expected to be 5.57 million presuming that the growth rate in FTAs observed in 2007 over 2006 remains same in 2008 also.
The important efforts being made by the Government to encourage tourist inflow include integrated development of tourist infrastructure at tourist circuits and destinations, growth of hotel infrastructure particularly budget hotels, augmentation of air capacity, enhancing availability of skilled manpower, according greater focus in emerging markets particularly in the regions of China, North-East Asia and South-East Asia, and international publicity campaigns through the electronic and print media.

records.qtitle: PROVISIONS FOR TAXING INCOMES EARNED FROM STOCK MARKET
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) the current provisions for taxing the incomes from the stock market;

(b) whether it is a fact that investors are exempted from payment of income tax if they have held a particular scrips for more than a year;

(c) if so, whether Government is considering a proposal to further reduce this period, in view of major slides that took place on the bourses recently; and

(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE:

(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM)

(a) The income arising from transactions in the stock market may either be taxed as capital gains or as business income; depending upon the facts of a particular case.

(b) Yes, Sir. Such exemption from payment of income tax is applicable only to capital gains arising from the transfer of an asset held for more than one year, being an equity share in a company or a unit of an equity oriented fund, and where such transactions have been charged to securities transaction tax.

(c) No, Sir.

(d) A reduction in the holding period, as suggested, will encourage investors to sell their shares which could cause further slide in the market. Therefore, the proposal to reduce the period of holding is not acceptable.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government has taken note of the current turmoil in Sri Lanka;

(b) if so, whether Government has received any request for intervention in the turmoil;

(c) whether Government has otherwise analysed the scenario with its repercussions, if any, on the country; and

(d) the steps, if any, Government is contemplating?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE)

(a)-(d) India is closely monitoring developments in Sri Lanka and is concerned about the recent upsurge in the violence and conflict in that country. Our policy towards Sri Lanka is based on the conviction that there is no military solution to the conflict. The way forward lies in a peacefully negotiated political settlement within the framework of a united Sri Lanka, acceptable to all communities in Sri Lanka, including the Tamils. It is with this in mind that we have welcomed as a first step the intention of the Government of Sri Lanka to fully implement the 13th Amendment.

records.qtitle: GANGA ACTION PLAN PHASE I AND II .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) the amount spent on cleansing of Ganga after Ganga Action Plan Phase I;

(b) the details of works done in Ganga Action Plan Phase II;

(c) the remaining works and by when these are likely to be completed;

(d) the present quality of Ganga water with technical details and the minimum prescribed standards; and

(e) whether further improvements are likely in the quality of water?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS

(SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA)

(a) & (b) An expenditure of Rs.312.67 crore has been incurred as on 31st December, 2007 for undertaking various pollution abatement measures for the river Ganga under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of National River Conservation Plan after Ganga Action Plan(GAP), Phase-I. A total of 163 works of pollution abatement have been completed under the GAP, Phase-II so far resulting in creation of 101 million litres per day of sewage treatment capacity. These works include interception and diversion of raw sewage, setting up of Sewage Treatment Plants for treating the diverted sewage, creation of low cost sanitation facilities, setting up of electric/improved wood crematoria and River Front Development among others.

(c) As river conservation is a continuous/dynamic activity, additional projects of pollution abatement are sanctioned by the Government from time to time under the GAP-II taking into account the pollution hotspots, proposals received from the State Government and availability of financial resources. In this regard, all the concerned State Governments have been advised to complete the 117 ongoing sanctioned works by the Financial Year 2009-10.

(d) & (e) The values of Dissolved Oxygen (DO) & Bio-chemical Oxygen Demand (BOD), key indicators of water quality, at major locations along the river Ganga in 1986 and 2007, vis-à-vis prescribed standards are indicated in the Table at Annexure. This shows that there has been a discernible improvement in the water quality of the river over its pre-GAP quality. However, besides pollution abatement initiatives, the water quality of the river is also impacted by a host of factors which include minimum flows in the river, proper Operation & Maintenance of the assets like Sewage Treatment Plants, Crematoria etc., development of sewerage/civic infrastructure within the cities/towns, among others.

records.qtitle: HARDSHIP AND COUNTER INSURGENCY ALLOWANCE TO CRPF AND BSF .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that CRPF and BSF have requested for hardship and counter insurgency allowance at par with armed forces; and

(b) what action Government has taken on the request?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI SRIPARAKASH JAISWAL)

(a) & (b): After the appointment of 6th Central Pay Commission on 5th October, 2006, the demands of the Central Police Forces for allowances commensurate to the risks and hardships to which they are exposed, have come within its purview.

records.qtitle: TROOPS DEPLOYED IN UN PEACE KEEPING FORCE .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) the countries where Indian troops are at present deployed as part of the UN peace keeping force;

(b) what is the number of troops so deployed and the terms and conditions of deployment; and

(b) by when the term of deployment is likely to be over?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF DEFENCE

(SHRI A.K. ANTONY)

(a) The Indian Armed Forces personnel are deployed in six UN Peace Keeping Missions viz., Congo, Lebanon, Ethiopia-Eritrea, Sudan, Golan Heights and Ivory Coast, at present.

(b) A total of 8887 Indian Armed Forces’ personnel are presently deployed in UN Peacekeeping operations and UN Headquarters, New York. The terms and conditions of the personnel deployed in these missions are governed by the orders/instructions issued by the UN and Government of India including Memorandum of Understanding / Letter of Assist signed between UN and Government of India.

(c) Each peacekeeping mission is governed by UN mandate which is reviewed from time to time.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) the names of countries with which India has conducted joint defence exercises in the last two years; and

(b) how India has benefited from these exercises?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF DEFENCE

(SHRI A.K. ANTONY)

(a) The names of countries with which India has conducted joint defence exercises in the last two years are USA, France, UK, Oman, Russia, Singapore, Thailand, China, Maldives and Mongolia.

(b) These exercises have helped in enhancing interoperability with defence forces of friendly foreign countries and in increasing military to military cooperation.

records.qtitle: DECLINE IN INTEREST RATE ON HOME LOANS
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that interest rate on home loans has declined;

(b) if so, the number of occasions on which it has declined during the last one year;

(c) whether it is also a fact that the benefit of declined rate of interest is not being passed on to the existing borrowers; and

(d) if so, what are the reasons for differential rate of interest for existing as well as new borrowers?
records.ans_text:
(FINANCE MINISTER) (SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM)

(a), (b), (e) & (d) : A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.

records.qtitle: INTEREST RATE CHARGED ON EDUCATION LOANS
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) the rate of interest charged on education loans by Government: and other banks;

(c) whether there is any proposal to bring down this rate of interest in order to reduce mental pressure on students and in a bid `Io reduce the cost of education; and

(c) if not, what arc the reasons therefor ?
records.ans_text:
(MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTKY OF FINANCE)

(SHRI PAWAN KUMAR BANSAL)

(a) : As per extant guidelines, the interest rate on education loans upto Rs.4 lakh should not exceed the Benchmark Prime Lending ]Rate (BPLR) of the banks and for loans above Rs.4 lakh it should not exceed BPLR+I per cent.

(b) & (c) : Certain features have been built into the education loan scheme to reduce the burden of interest on the student. There is a repayment holiday/moratorium., during the period of the course plus one year one year or six months after getting a job, whichever is earlier. Furthermore, the interest is to be debited quarterly/half/early on simple basis, during the. repayment holiday/moratorium period to further ease the interest burden on the student.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that a number of Airlines including Indian often offload passenger holding confirmed tickets at the last moment without assigning any reason;

(b) whether it is also a fact that this deprives passengers of important engagements and in some cases commitment of offered jobs, resumption of duties etc.; and

(c) the steps Government is taking to avoid such unpleasant situation and to discourage passengers seeking legal remedies in such situations?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION

( SHRI PRAFUL PATEL )

(a),(b)&(c): As per international industry practice, airlines over book their flights to optimize utilization of capacity, as all passengers booked on a flight do not turn up at the airport. However, at times more passengers than expected do turn up and the airline has no option but to resort to offloading. Air India does have a policy of making alternate arrangements for their travel. They are either accepted on the next available Air India flight or transferred on other airlines, subject to space availability. They are also provided hotel accommodation with meals, transport and telephone facility. Occasionally, letters are given to passengers on request confirming that they have been offloaded, which they can present to their company.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that gender identification kits are available for sale by a US based company through a website; and

(b) if so, the steps Government is contemplating either to ban the website in the country or regulate its sale in the country?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE

(DR. ANBUMANI RAMADOSS)

(a)&(b): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 228 FOR 14TH MARCH, 2008.

The declining sex ratio is a matter of great concern and calls for concerted action from all quarters. In order to contain the menace of female foeticide and ushering in a healthy sex ratio in the Country, the Central Government enacted the Pre-Conception & Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques Act, 1994. The Act, inter alia, provides for stringent action against individuals and genetic laboratories/clinics offering sex determination services. Similar penalty provision also exists for those who seek such services.

2. Various mechanisms have been evolved at the national, State and district levels to ensure strict compliance of the provisions of the Act by all stake holders through periodic inspection and monitoring.

3. The advent of internet e-communication has emerged as a new threat in this regard. It has been reported that some of the overseas agencies are freely posting advertisements pertaining to sex determination services and wares. For instance, web sites like the `www.GenSelect.com; www.4-gender-selection.com, www.pregnancystore.com, etc., are offering sex determination kits called the `baby Gender Mentor Home DNA Test Kit`, that help the buyer determine the sex of the foetus through DNA analysis at home.

4. The matter was referred to the Ministry of Communications & IT to block the offending websites. But, that Ministry expressed the view that such an action did not render the promoters of such sites completely ineffective as they could re-emerge and be available for the viewers again under a new nomenclature and in a new avatar,

5. To identify the people involved, the issue was then taken up with the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, to trap the people importing the sex determination kits pandered by the offending overseas websites into the Country.

6. The Ministry of Health requested the Customs Department for details of the individuals or organisations who have imported the sex determination (Gender Testing) kits from abroad to facilitate the Government to proceed further against such people under Section 23 (3) of the PC & PNDT Act and also to intercept and not release such articles under Sub-Section (2) (k), (u) & (v) of Section 11 under Chapter IV of the Customs Act, 1962 (52 of 1962), vide the Government`s letter dated 29.11.2007 and 5.1.2008.

7 In response to the Government`s above request, the Customs Department have suitably alerted their field formations not to release the imported Gender Testing Kits and to take appropriate action under the Customs Act.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) the present level of productivity of cotton per hectare and how does it compare with other cotton producing countries;

(b) whether there has been any increase in the productivity as a result of recommendations; if any, made by the task force appointed in mid-nineties; and

(c) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI KANTI LAL BHURIA)

(a): As per information available on FAO`s internet site `faostat` productivity of cotton in India was 400 Kg./ha as against 1243kg./ha in China, 1007Kg./ha in Egypt and 805Kg./ha USA in the year 2006.

(b) & (c): Since launch of `Technology Mission on Cotton` in February, 2000 significant achievement has been made in increasing the yield of cotton in the country. The yield per hectare which was at 191 Kg./ha in 2002-03 has increased to 416Kg./ha in 2007-08.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government has studied the effects of the organic manure;

(b) if so, what are the findings; and

(c) whether there is any mechanism to monitor its quality and if so, what are the details in this regard?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI KANTI LAL BHURIA)

(a) & (b): Under All India Coordinated Research Project (AICRP) on `long term fertilizer experiments` over the last few decades, Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has concluded that only integrated use of optimal dose of Nitrogen, Phosphorous & Potash (NPK) and organic manure can maintain soil health and give higher sustainable yields. Organic manure, besides supplying essential plant nutrients, improves soil physical conditions and stimulates biological activities of soils through supply of energy to soil microbes.

(c): Organic manures are mostly produced on farm and used by the farmers. However, with commercialization of few type of organic manures, three organic manures have been brought under Fertilizer Control Order (FCO) namely

(i) City waste compost
(ii) Vermi-compost and
(iii) Press- mud. The quality of the above organic manure is monitored as per the specifications/provisions of FCO.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) the present strength of rare species of animals like lions, tigers and leopards etc., giving details, Sanctuary-wise;

(b) the species of animals that have faced extinction over the last one decade;

(c) whether Government has focused its attention to save the species on the verge of extinction; and

(d) if so, with what results?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS

(SHRI S. REGUPATHY)

(a) Sanctuary wise population details of wild animals are not collated at Central Government level. The All India Estimation of Tiger, co-predators and its prey was carried out recently in the tiger range states of the country using a modified and integrated methodology as recommended by the Tiger Task Force. The details are at Annexure I. Similarly, the all India enumeration of wild population of elephants in the country was carried out in 2007, except the North Eastern States. The details are at Annexure II. Further, as per the estimation carried out in 2006, there are 359 + 10 Lions in Gir Protected Area and adjacent areas.

(b) Fluctuation in population of wild animals is a natural phenomenon. However, there are no specific reports available with this Ministry to indicate that any particular species has faced extinction during the last one decade.

(c) & (d) Government of India, under the various Centrally Sponsored Schemes – Development of National Parks and Sanctuaries, Project Tiger and Project Elephant provides financial and technical assistance to the State /UT Governments for the conservation and management of wildlife including rare and endangered species. These Schemes have helped in the conservation of wildlife and its habitat in the country.

records.qtitle: MISSING DATE OF BIRTH RECORDS OF SENIOR ARMY OFFICERS .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there are some senior most officers waiting for promotion for top slots in the army who have no record of their date of birth;

(b) if so, the details in this regard and the number of such officers in the army;

(c) how did this lapse occur; and

(d) how this is proposed to be resolved?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF DEFENCE

(SHRI A.K. ANTONY)

(a) All officers of the Indian Army have a recorded date of birth which is maintained by Military Secretary’s Branch of Army Headquarters. Hence, there are no such officers who have no record of their date of birth.

(b) to (d): Do not arise.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) the details of vacancies at present in the armed forces;

(b) since when these vacancies have been in existence;

(c) whether these vacancies have been advertised and given wide publicity;

(d) if so, what has been the response;

(e) whether it is a fact that the response to advertisements, opinion polls and the process of admission in defence establishments reveals that the youth are not inclined to come forward to take army as a carrier; and

(f) the steps Government is contemplating to address the problem?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF DEFENCE

(SHRI A.K. ANTONY)


(a) to (f): A Statement is attached.



STATEMENT IN RESPECT OF PARTS (a) TO (f) OF RAJYA SABHA UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.1274 FOR 12.3.2008 REGARDING VACANCIES IN THE ARMED FORCES.

There is a shortage of 11,153, 1403 and 1368 officers in Army, Navy and Air Force respectively. This deficiency has been continuing since very long time in varying degree. There is no shortage of Personnel Below Officer Ranks (PBOR) in the Armed Forces.

The Armed Forces have undertaken sustained image projection and publicity campaign to create awareness among the youth on the advantages of taking up a challenging and satisfying career. Candidate-friendly recruitment procedures to attract more number of candidates and a focused publicity drive in various institutions to attract potential candidates have been undertaken. Awareness campaigns, participation in career fairs and exhibitions, advertisements in print and electronic media, counselling and motivational talks in schools, colleges and NCC camps are also some of the other measures in this direction. In addition, the commitment and bravery of the Armed Forces is consistently projected through the electronic and print media.

There has been adequate response to the advertisements for joining the Armed Forces. Although a good number of candidates pass through the written part of the examination, many fail to make the grade at the stage of Service Selection Board (SSB) interviews, which is mandatory for selection of officers, as they are not able to meet the requisite selection and medical criterion.

The shortfall in recruitment of officers in the Defence Services are largely due to change in the socio-economic environment and the resultant changes in career preferences, better employment opportunities in other sectors, tough selection procedures and service conditions required for the Defence Forces.

Several steps have been taken by the three Services to attract more talented youth to join the Defence Forces. All officers including those in Short Service Commission (SSC) have been made eligible to hold substantive rank of Captain, Major and Lieutenant Colonel after 2, 6 and 13 years of reckonable service respectively. In addition to the above, 750 posts of Lieutenant Colonels have been upgraded to Colonel’s rank. The tenure of SSC officers has also been extended from 10 years to 14 years.

The Government has also appointed VI Central Pay Commission to go into the question of revision of pay and allowances etc. of all the Government servants including the Armed Forces. The three Services have presented a joint memorandum to the Pay Commission suggesting revision of pay and allowances and other service conditions. The matter has also been discussed with the Pay Commission by the three Service Chiefs and officers in the Ministry of Defence.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) what is the estimated percentage of population covered by finance agencies for grant of housing loans;

(b) whether it is a fact that these finance agencies do not provide housing loans for rural areas;

(c) if so, what are the reasons therefor; and

(d) whether Government has considered the feasibility of authorizing panchayats for completion of formalities to facilitate grant of housing loans in rural areas?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

( SHRI PAWAN KUMAR BANSAL )

(a): No estimates have been made by the Government on the percentage of population covered by financial agencies for grant of housing loans.

(b): According to information reported by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in the Basic Statistical Returns of Scheduled Commercial Banks (SCBs) the share of rural areas in total number of accounts for housing loans of SCBs was 16 per cent as on 31st March, 2006.

(c): One of the reasons for lower share of housing loans in rural areas as compared to other areas is that housing requirements in rural areas are also met through Government schemes like the Indira Awaas Yojana where assistance is given in the form of subsidy for dwelling units without necessarily involving financial agencies. Further, there is also a relatively larger dependence in rural areas on informal credit channels.

(d): No such proposal is under the consideration of the Government at present.

records.qtitle: WASTAGE OF FUEL DUE TO DELAY LANDING OF AIRCRAFTS .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) the amount of fuel that is currently being wasted annually as a result of delayed landings on airports in the country;

(b) whether any steps have been taken to eliminate or reduce these wastages;

(c) if so, the details thereof; and

(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION

( SHRI PRAFUL PATEL )

(a), (b), (c) & (d) The unprecedented growth in civil aviation has raised various challenges, specially at Delhi and Mumbai airports. Some of the important initiatives taken to improve the position and reduce delays are as under: 1.At Delhi and Mumbai airports various steps have been taken up for checking delay in landing/ taking off of aircraft viz. construction of new high speed exit taxiways, simultaneous use of both runways have started during the traffic congestion period, establishment of clearance delivery position, ban on general aviation aircraft during peak period, upgradation of ATC Automation system etc. 2.AAI has already taken up the project of upgradation of 35 non-metro airports which will enable them to handle the increased air traffic at those airports. 3.Improved ATC procedures have been framed. 4.At the time of slot allocation schedule arrival and departure time are spread in such a manner that bunching should not take place resulting into delays. 5.The number of hourly movements of flights are being freezed at Mumbai and Delhi airport at par with available runway/ terminal building capacity etc. However, as some airlines do not maintain details related to delays due to `landing restrictions` or late clearance for take off which lead to additional fuel burn, it is not possible to work out the fuel loss on this count.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that, according to a Government report on elementary education released on 22nd January, 2008, only 43 per cent of students in Government schools pass with more than 60 per cent marks, with girls doing slightly better than boys;

(b) whether, at upper primary level, only 39 per cent students pass with a first class ; and

(c) if so, what are the reasons for the flaws in the quality of education that the learning abilities of students do not improve much while going for elementary education?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI M. A. A. FATMI)

(a) to (c) National University of Educational Planning and Administration (NUEPA) collects elementary school statistics annually through the District Information System for Education (DISE) from all districts in the country. According to DISE data 2006-07, 45.04 % students passed with 60% and above marks, at the exit classes of the primary stage. Girls have performed slightly better than boys, and the percentage of girls and boys passing with 60% and above marks is 45.12% and 44.96 % respectively. At the upper primary level, 39.40% students passed with 60% and above marks.

Under Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, several activities have been undertaken to improve the quality of elementary education. This includes recruitment of 8.32 lakh additional teachers to improve the pupil teacher ratio, in-service training of teachers for a period of 20 days every year, free distribution of textbooks for primary and upper primary classes to about 6.5 crore Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and girl students, academic support to primary and upper primary schools through 6395 Block Resource Centres and 68352 Cluster Resource Centres and regular evaluation of students.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) the different varieties of fertilizers being produced in the country and the details of the plants alongwith their locations producing a kind of fertilizers ;

(b) whether there are any varieties for which there is a demand but is not being produced in the country and if so, the details in this regard ; and

(c) by when the country is likely to achieve self sufficiency in the production of requisite varieties of fertilizers ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS & FERTILIZERS AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS

(SHRI B.K.HANDIQUE)


(a) Major fertilizers being produced in the country include urea, Di-Ammonium Phosphate (DAP), complex grade fertilizers and Single Super Phosphate (SSP). Details regarding location of the plants producing these fertilizers are indicated in the statement at Annexure.

(b) For requirement of Muriate of Potash (MOP) for which there is demand, the country is totally dependent on imports as there are no economically exploitable reserves of Potash in the country.


(c ) While no definite time frame can be prescribed for increasing production of fertilizers to attain self-sufficiency, Government is working towards increasing the production capacity of chemical fertilizers, chiefly urea. This is sought to be done through revival of the currently closed units of Fertilizer Corporation of India Ltd.(FCIL) and Hindustan Fertilizer Corporation Ltd. (HFCL) as well as through establishment of new plants. These companies are in discussions with gas companies for pipeline connectivity and availability of natural gas.
The Government is in the process of developing a new pricing policy for investment in urea sector in order to promote investment in urea sector and consequently to increase the indigenous production.
Production of phosphatic fertilizers in the country is dependent upon availability of raw materials/intermediates in the international market. Hence, additional capacity creation for production of DAP and complex grade fertilizers can not be anticipated definitely.

records.qtitle: SUICIDES OF FARMERS IN UTTAR PRADESH .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there are reports of drought in some parts of Uttar Pradesh with farmers committing suicide;

(b) if so, what are the details in this regard;

(c) whether it is a fact that relief provided so far is meagre and has not ameliorated the conditions of farmers there;

(d) the steps Government is contemplating to provide further relief particularly in areas like Bundelkhand; and

(e) whether there are any plans to introduce crop insurance in such areas?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI KANTI LAL BHURIA)

(a) & (b): This year, the Government of Uttar Pradesh have reported drought in parts of the State. However, no report on suicides by farmers in the context of drought has been received from the State Government.

(c): It is primarily the responsibility of the State Government to take necessary measures in the wake of natural calamities including drought. There is ready availability of funds with the State Government in the Calamity Relief Fund (CRF) for taking such measures. No Memorandum has so far been received from the State Government for assistance from the National Calamity Contingency Fund (NCCF) etc. for the current drought.

(d): An Inter-Ministerial Central Team visited the Bundelkhand areas and some tehsils in Allahabad district of Uttar Pradesh in the 4th week of January, 2008, to study the drought like situation in these areas with a view to assessing the ground situation and the scale of implementation of various medium-term and long-term drought mitigation programmes/schemes and to recommend strategy and various measures that are required for agriculture development suitable for the areas to ameliorate the current situation. Further action would be taken after receipt of the Team`s report.

(e): National Agricultural Insurance Scheme is applicable in Uttar Pradesh, including Bundelkhand areas. However, crops/areas to be covered are notified by the State Government.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that medical tourism is opening new vistas of foreign earnings;

(b) whether it is also a fact that countries like USA are seriously considering to avail of cheaper medical facilities;

(c) whether it is also a fact that the medical facilities available to citizens at home would become more costlier;

(d) if so, the steps being taken to address the situation; and

(e) whether there is any proposal to ensure investment of fixed part of these foreign earnings for creating more health infrastructure and if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE

(DR. ANBUMANI RAMADOSS)


(a) Yes sir.

(b) Government is not aware of any such development in USA or in any other country.

(c) No sir.

(d) Does not arise.

(e) No sir, Government does not collect separate information in respect of foreign exchange earned through visits of medical tourists. The hospitals in private sector are providing treatment under medical tourism and they are further strengthening health infrastructure.

 No memorandum for Central assistance has been received from any State

records.qtitle: EARNINGS OF METRO IN DELHI NO.
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) the present earnings per day from Metro operations of Delhi Metro Rail Corporation in Delhi;

(b) whether any part of the earnings is being utilized for repayment of loans, R&D and welfare of commuters;

(c) if so, the details thereof;

(d) whether any more amenities are proposed to be provided by way of concessional fares for senior citizens physically challenged people and other vulnerable sections of the community; and

(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT

( SHRI AJAY MAKEN )

(a): Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) Ltd. has reported that the present earnings per day from Metro operation is Rs. 70 lakh approximately.

(b)&(c): The income generated from the operation is utilized for the repayment of loan also. DMRC has fulfilled all its loan repayment commitments till date aggregating to Rs.268.72 crore. Drinking water, toilet facilities etc. have been provided at stations for the welfare of the commuters. Recently, feeder buses have been introduced to carry passengers to and from Metro stations. Under the over all programme of indigenization, efforts are being made to substitute some items of sophisticated equipment like automatic fare control system, signaling & telecommunication.
CONTD....2 .PA - 2 -


(d)&(e): There is no proposal for introduction of concessional fares. The metro fares are decided by a Regulatory Authority. DMRC has no independent role in this regard. However, for the senior citizens and physically challenged persons, DMRC is providing many additional amenities like: 
-     Reserved seats in trains @ 4 seats in each coach.


-     Perforated benches at platform.


-     Arrangement of wheel chair at every Metro station.


-     Provision  of  wide gates in the paid area for  convenient
entry.


-     Tactile  tiles  and  self   operated  lifts  with  Braille
transcription for the blind.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that under the schemes such as speed post, delivery of letters sent by ordinary mail from one city to another is being considerably delayed;

(b) if not, the time taken in the delivery of letters sent from Mumbai to Rameshwaram, Delhi to Chennai and Delhi to Trivandrum;

(c) whether it is also a fact that earlier these letters were delivered next day depending upon the time they were put in the letter boxes; and

(d) if so, the reasons for decline in the efficiency of the post offices?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY

(DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD)

(a) No, Sir. However, the incidents of occasional delay in delivery of mail could be due to cancellation/late running of trains and state transport buses carrying mails, missending of mails, incomplete and illegible address of the addressee, non-use of PIN Code, non-availability of addressee and change in the residence of the addressee without intimation to the concerned Postmaster etc.

(b) & (c) Department of Post has fixed norms for delivery of mail across the country and has widely circulated them for information of the public. First class ordinary mail between Metro cities has norms of delivery within 48 to 72 hours after the day of posting. Mails for States other than in which they are posted have norms of delivery within 3 to 5 days depending on the distance involved and transport links.

(d) No instances of decline in the efficiency of the post offices have been noticed with respect to (b) & (c) above.

records.qtitle: INTRODUCTION OF NREG THROUGHOUT THE COUNTRY .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI CHANDRA SEKHAR SAHU)

(a)&(b): Yes, Sir. Government has decided to extend NREGA to all the remaining rural districts in the country with effect from 1.4.2008. The Programme is already being implemented in 330 districts in the country. Remaining 266 districts have been covered in the third phase of implementation. A notification to this effect was issued on 28.9.2007.

(c)&(d): The NREG Act requires it to be made applicable to the whole of the territory to which it extends within a period of five years. The Scheme has been extended in accordance with the provisions of the Act.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan

records.qtitle: RECOGNITION OF KOL TRIBE AS SCHEDULED TRIBE .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI P. R. KYNDIAH)


(a) to (c) : A statement is laid on the table of the House.

…..
Statement in respect of Parts (a) to (c) of the Rajya Sabha Starred Question Number 260 for 3-12-07 regarding ‘Recognition of Kol tribe as Scheduled Tribe’ raised by Shrimati Jaya Bachchan.


(a) & (b): The Kol tribe has been recognized as a Scheduled Tribe in the States of Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Orissa and are eligible for the same benefits as available to the other Scheduled Tribes.

records.qn_text:

(e) if so, whether Government has given a thought for overhauling PDS and, if so, with what result?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD & PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION

(DR. AKHILESH PRASAD SINGH)

(a): The stock of foodgrains (rice & wheat) as on 1.11.2007 is as under:-
(in lakh tons) Rice 106.51 Wheat 90.25 Total 196.76

(b) & (c): The Department of Food & Public Distribution got Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS) evaluated by PEO, Planning Commission and ORG MARG. The report of ORG Marg received in 2005 mentioned that there was diversion of 53% wheat and 39% rice respectively, under TPDS at the all India level.

The Programme Evaluation Organization report mentioned 36.35% diversion of subsidized foodgrains. These reports pointed out the diversion/leakages of foodgrains under TPDS is due to inclusion and exclusion errors in identifying targeted beneficiaries and non-viability of Fair Price Shops (FPS).

(d): Yes, Sir.

(e): Strengthening of the Targeted Public Distribution System to improve its efficiency, accountability and effectiveness is an ongoing process. Based on findings of earlier studies of TPDS, a Nine-Point Action Plan is already under implementation by States and UT Governments. Its implementation is monitored by the Central Government. Action Plan for strengthening of TPDS is at

Annexure-I.

Additionally, a revised Citizens` Charter has been issued recently for adoption and implementation by State/UT Governments for facilitating use by citizens of provisions of Right to Information (RTI) Act, 2005 in relation to functioning of TPDS.

ANNEXURE-I

ANNEXURE REFFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PART (e) OF THE UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1218 DUE FOR ANSWER ON 30.11.2007 IN THE RAJYA SABHA
ACTION PLAN FOR STRENGTHENING OF TPDS 
 


(i) 	Continuous review of the BPL and AAY lists to eliminate bogus 
ration cards and to ensure coverage of only eligible 	BPL and Antyodaya 
families.


(ii) 	Ensuring leakages-free and diversion-free distribution of PDS 
commodities, regular inspection by different levels of functionaries, strict 
action against guilty persons/agencies.


(iii) 	Involvement of Panchayati Raj Institutions in PDS 
operations -PRI representatives on Advisory Committees, running of fair price 
shops by Panchayats and effective representation of  Panchayati Raj 
representatives on 	Vigilance Committees.


(iv) 	Ensuring transparency in working of PDS, display of BPL and AAY 
lists by fair price shops, observance of notified timings by fair price shops.


(v) 	Use of Information Technology, Computerization of TPDS operations,
 display of fair price shops-wise and district 	wise allocations of PDS 
commodities on web-sites for public scrutiny.


(vi) 	Carryout door-step delivery of PDS commodities to fair price 
shops.


(vii) 	Ensuring timely availability of and issuance of foodgrains
 by fair price shops.


(viii) 	Creating awareness among public about PDS operations, 
training Vigilance Committees of intricacies of PDS 	operations.


(ix) 	Making fair price shops financially viable entities - allowing 
them to sell non PDS items etc.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) Whether it is a fact that Government propose to invest Rs.4,000 to Rs.10,000 crores in the Petroleum, Chemical and Petrochemical Investment Regions (PCPIR) and if so, the details in this regard; and

(b) Whether it is also a fact that some States have set their proposals, for investment in this regard, and if so, the name of these States, the amount proposed to be invested by them and the decision taken on the proposals? ANSW ER
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS & FERTILIZERS AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS

(SHRI B.K.HANDIQUE )

(a) to (b): The Cabinet has recently approved the Policy for setting up of Petroleum, Chemical and Petrochemical Investment Regions (PCPIRs), and the same has been published in the Gazette of India (Extraordinary, Part I, Section 1 dated 4th April, 2007) and is also placed on the web site of the Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals viz: www.chemicals.nic.in. The State Government would play a lead role in setting up of the PCPIR and prepare a project proposal for an identified site. The Central Government will consider and approve applications from the State Governments for establishment of PCPIRs in terms of this policy and also facilitate availability of external physical infrastructure linkages including rail, road, ports, and airports. Similarly, the State Government, applying for a PCPIR, will ensure that all physical infrastructure and utilities linkages under its jurisdiction are provided to the site.
The following four proposals have been received for hosting PCPIRs.

(i) Proposal from the Government of Andhra Pradesh for hosting a PCPIR at Vishakhapattnam.-Kakinada-Rajamundry within the Vishakhapattnam and East Godavari Districts.
(ii) Proposal from the Government of Karnataka for hosting a PCPIR within the coastal districts of Dakshina Kannada and Udupi of Karnataka.
(iii) Proposal from the Government of Gujarat for hosting a PCPIR at Dahej spread over` the blocks of Vagra and Bharuch of South Gujarat.
(iv) Proposal from the Government of West Bengal for hosting a PCPIR at Haidia spread over the Haidia Municipal Corporation and Nayachar islands in Purba Medinipur.
The investment requirements of a PCPIR will depend on its location and other factors which will include the availability of existing infrastructure and the details in the project proposal. The investment details will vary from place to place and are to be concurred to by the concerned departments of the Government of India and the State Government. Exact quantification of investment would depend on the proposed specific details.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
:-

(a) whether it is a fact that about 80 percent of all e-mail origination in India is spam;

(b) whether it is also a fact that Government is working on India`s first formal anti- spam law in order to enable net users to get rid of net nuisance; and

(c) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER FOR COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY

(ANDIMUTHU RAJA)


(a) to (c): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 220 FOR 29.11.2007 REGARDING ANTI-SPAM LAW


(a) As per the study conducted on Internet Security by one of the International industry leader, 76% of e-mail messages originating in India amounts to spam. However, this is only 1% of total spam e-mail messages generated worldwide.


(b) & (c) Section 43 & 66 of the Information Technology Act, 2000 provides a legal framework to check spam and unsolicited e-mail in the country. Further a bill to amend Information Technology Act, 2000 was introduced in the Parliament on 15 December, 2006 to strengthen the legal framework and provisions pertaining to cyber crimes including spam in the principle Act.

records.qtitle: CONSTRUCTION OF BUNKERS AND INSPECTION POSTS ON IB BY PAKISTAN .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan

(b) what are the reasons that his Ministry is unaware of this development while the Ministry of Home Affairs has confirmed reports; and

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF DEFENCE

(SHRI A.K. ANTONY)


(a) to (c): Pakistan has constructed several bunkers and inspection posts (observation posts) on the International Border in Jammu and Kashmir taking advantage of ceasefire in the last 3 ½ years. records.qtitle: DECLINE IN PRODUCTION DUE TO HARDENING OF RUPEE .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that production has declined in export oriented industries like metal products, textile, garments, leather and leather products from 28 per cent last year to 18 per cent this year in April-July as a result of hardening of rupee against dollar;

(b) whether it has also affected industrial growth by 1.3 per cent compared to last year; and

(c) what steps Government has taken to address the situation?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY

(SHRI JAIRAM RAMESH)

(a) & (b) In terms of Index of Industrial Production at 2-digit level compiled by Central Statistical Organisation (CSO), the production of only two industrial groups, namely, Metal Products & Parts (with a weightage of 2.81%) and Paper & Paper Products (with a weightage of 2.65%) registered negative growth rates of -1.5% and -0.2% respectively during April-July 2007 implying that their production decreased as compared to corresponding period of the previous year. The overall Index of Industrial Production, however, recorded a growth of 9.6 per cent in April-July 2007 as compared to 11.1 per cent in the corresponding period of the previous year.

Performance of individual industries in a market driven economy, apart from exchange rate movement, depends on a number of factors, such as demand and supply conditions, relative prices of inputs, competition and other macroeconomic factors. Besides, demand conditions in major importing countries and trade environment also impact the performance of industries in which exports constitute a significant proportion of production.

(c) Government has put in place various policies to promote broad based industrial growth. This includes, inter-alia, delicensing of industrial capacity, liberalization of foreign trade regime to provide better access to inputs at competitive prices, rationalization and reduction in duty rates of customs and central excise, better infrastructure support, and liberal FDI regime, etc.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan

MINISTER OF HEAVY INDUSTRIES AND PUBLIC ENTERPRISES

(SHRI SONTOSH MOHAN DEV)

(a) to (d): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.167 FOR ANSWER ON 27.11.2007 REGARDING “PRODUCTION OF CARS” BY SMT. JAYA BACHCHAN.

(a) to (d): As per Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM), the total number of vehicles including passenger cars produced during current year and during the last three years by the Indian Automobile Industry is as under:-

Year		2004-05	2005-06	2006-07	April-October, 2007

Utility Vehicles182018	196506	222111	137874
MPVs		67371	66661	84707	54106

(Passenger Vehicles)


	The following new tie-ups have been announced:-


(i)	Ashok Leyland with Nissan 

(ii)	Mahindra & Mahindra with Renault 

(iii)	Mahindra & Mahindra with Nissan 

(iv)	Skoda Auto with Volkswagen 

(v)	Swaraj Mazda with Isuzu Motors
