	According to the data available, India has a large road network of 3.31 
Million Km comprising of 66590 Kilometer of National Highways and Expressways, 
128000 kilometer of State Highways and 3.12 million kilometer of district and 
rural roads.  The vehicle density in India is estimated to be 3.2 motor 
vehicles per kilometer which is very low.  In countries like Germany and 
Taiwan, this figure is much higher i.e. 209.6 and 159.2 respectively.  The 
passenger vehicle penetration in India is only 7 cars per thousand people 
whereas in Malaysia, South Korea and Brazil it is 253, 219 and 96 respectively.  
The vehicle penetration in major Indian cities is also very low for example; 
the vehicle penetration for Delhi, Chennai, Mumbai, Kolkata and Bangalore is 
only 85, 51, 23, 23 and 41 cars per thousand population respectively.  The low 
vehicle penetration in India is also true for two wheelers.  Although, India is 
the second largest producer of two wheelers yet the penetration is 43 two 
wheelers per thousand population as against 258 and 286 in Malaysia and 
Thailand.  Therefore, India is hugely under motorized as compared to global 
levels.  Inspite of very low vehicle penetration levels in India as compared to 
global levels, the congestion problem in Metro-cities arises due to factors 
like driving conditions, driver behaviour, enforcement of rules and 
regulations, traffic management, lack of town planning etc.  However, there is 
continued effort for improvement of road infrastructure in the country.




	Currently, the automotive sector in India accounts for 5 % of GDP.  The 
sector provides direct and indirect employment to 13.1 million people and also 
facilitates economic growth.  Therefore, Government is not considering freezing 
production of more cars.  Instead, there is continuous effort to improve 
driving conditions and mass transit systems for decongestions.

records.qtitle: REQUEST TO OPEC FOR RAISING CRUDE OIL OUTPUT .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS

(SHRI DINSHA PATEL)

(a) & (b) No, Sir. However, while addressing the OPEC international Seminar held in September, 2006 at Vienna, Austria, Union Minister of P&NG had raised the soaring oil price issue. The Minister pointed out that “Oil security is not just oil supply security. Even with the secure oil supply source, a developing country may not be in a position to procure adequate oil unless price is affordable. So the price stability has become an important constituent of oil security. Given the vital role of energy prices in the economic and social well being of the common man, it is imperative to provide oil at affordable prices and this is becoming increasingly difficult given the present oil price scenario.”

(c) & (d) Yes, Sir. Various measures are being taken on a continuous basis to find crude oil substitute in the country, which are as follows : 



i. Carving out more and more areas of natural gas for exploration for offer 
under various rounds of New Exploration Licensing Policy (NELP).
ii. Quicker development of discovered gas reserves for enabling commencement of 
production.
iii. Use of stimulation techniques for increasing production from existing 
fields of natural gas.
iv. Application of Enhanced Oil Recovery (EOR)/ Improved Oil Recovery (IOR) 
techniques for increasing recovery factor from existing fields.
v. Exploration and production of Coal Bed Methane Gas.
vi. Exploration of sites of underground coal gasification.	
vii. Participating in gas hydrates programmes carried out by various countries.
viii. Acquisition of exploration acreages and oil & gas producing properties 
overseas to bring in equity oil and gas.
ix. Encouraging Oil PSUs to aggressively pursue equity and oil gas opportunities
 overseas & supporting them at diplomatic level.
x. Substitution of oil through use of non-conventional source of energy such as
 bio-diesel, ethanol, etc.
xi. Setting up of Hydrogen Corpus Fund for supporting Research & Development in
 various aspects of Hydrogen which could substitute part of natural gas as 
transport fuel in future.

records.qtitle: RATE OF INTEREST CHARGED ON USAGE OF CREDIT CARDS
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) what is the rate of interest being charged by banks on the purchases and the cash advances given to credit card holder;

(b) whether it is a fact that the interest rate is exorbitant and in case of some banks, it ranges from 42 to 48 per cent;

(c) if so, what are the reasons that Government has not so far given any thought of taming the banks on the interest rate to save customers from being fleeced; and

(d) whether Government is considering a proposal to bring a law on the subject?
records.ans_text:
The Minister of State in the Ministry of Finance

(Shri Pawan Kumar Bansal)

(a) to (c) : As per Master Circular on Credit Card operation dated 2nd July, 2007 issued by Reserve Bank of India (RBI), credit card dues are in the nature of non-priority sector personal loans and as such banks are free to determine the rate of interest on credit card dues without reference to their Benchmark Prime Lending Rate (BPLR) and regardless of the size. However, RBI has advised the banks that the annualized percentage rate (APR), the method of calculation of APR, late payment charges including the method of calculation, the manner in which the outstanding unpaid amount is to be included for calculation of interest, etc. on credit card dues should be indicated by card issuing banks in the `Welcome Kit` and monthly statement. Banks have also been advised not to levy any charge that was not explicitly indicated to the cardholder at the time of issue of card and getting his / her consent. Further, credit card scenario is being constantly monitored and instructions to banks on their credit card operations are issued by the RBI, on an ongoing basis.

(d) : No, Sir.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether any steps are being taken to encourage Minority focused Banks by the al whether Government has reviewed the interest rate scenario;

(b) if so the dermis thereof:

(c) what is the demand indicated by the economy;

(d) whether any correctives are warranted by the economic conditions; and

(e) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE: MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI PAWAN KUMAR BANSAL)

(a) & (b): Yes, Sir. Effective flora October 18,1994, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has deregulated the interest rates on advances above Rs.2 lakhs,, including the housing loans and these interest rate are determined by the banks themselves with the approval of their Boards of Directors subject to benchmark Prime Lending Rates (BPLR) spread guidelines. In order to enhance transparency in bank pricing of their loan products, banks have, been advised to fix their BPLR after taking into account
(i) actual cost of funds,
(ii) operating expense; and
(iii) a minimum margin to cover regulatory requirement of provisioning/capital charge mid profit margin arid ensure that the BPLR truly reflects the actual cost, Individual banks, therefore, determine interest rates to be charged to a particular borrower subject to BPLR arid spread guidelines. Given the prevailing credit market in India and the need` to continue with concessionality for small borrowers, the practice of treating BPLR as the. ceiling for loans upto Rs. two lakhs continues. However, Banks are flee to determine the rates of interest without reference to BPLR and regardless of the size in respect of loans of purchase of consume,` durables, loans to individuals against shares and debentures/bonds, other non-priority sector personal loans;, etc.

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has given freedom to commercial banks with effect form 22nd October, 1997 to fix their own interest rate on domestic term deposits of various maturities with the prior approval of their respective Board of Directors/Asset Liability Management Committee (ALCO). As such, the rates of interest o n deposits are determined by the banks themselves.

(c) to (e): RBI had stated that the outcome for interest rates depends mainly on the outlook for inflation, growth prospects and investment demand and it is not possible to predict short.-run movements in interest rates.

records.qtitle: ISSUE OF ELECTORS PHOTO IDENTITY CARDS .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Government had decided to issue electors` photo identity cards to all the citizens of the country;

(b) if so, the number of voters covered so far and supplied with the identity cards, State-wise; and

(c) by when the remaining citizens are likely to be covered?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF LAW AND JUSTICE

(SHRI H.R. BHARDWAJ)

(a): As per the provisions of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 and the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, only Indian citizens who attains the age of 18 are eligible for inclusion into electoral roll and only persons registered as such can obtain an Elector`s Photo Identity Card.

(b): A Statement showing the status of number of electors issued with Voter Identity Cards and also the percentage of electors provided with the Identity Cards, as intimated by the Election Commission of India is laid on the Table of the House.

(c): The Election Commission of India has intimated that it has been the endeavour of the Commission to achieve 100% coverage under the Elector Photo Identity Cards (EPIC) scheme, and even though the efforts have been constantly made to cover all the electors under the EPIC scheme, various reasons such as natural calamities, which also attend to works other than election work, apathy of voters themselves are some of the reasons why progress has been uneven.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that 10 member ASEAN countries, who attended the East Asia Summit, have agreed to strengthen and promote energy cooperation, while showing concern over the negative impact of high oil prices on economic growth and development in the region; and

(b) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER

( SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE )

(a) & (b) : At the 2nd East Asia Summit (EAS), held on 15th January 2007 in Cebu, Philippines, a special session of energy, to achieve the shared goal of ensuring affordable energy sources for development in the region, was held. Discussion among the 16 Heads of State/Governments of the member countries of ASEAN, Australia, China, India, Japan, republic of Korea and New Zealand covered issues relating to energy security, renewable and alternative energy sources, energy efficiency and conservation and climate change.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government had decided to issue electors’ identity cards to all the citizens of the country;

(b) if so, the number of voters covered so far and supplied with the identity cards, State-wise; and

(c) by when the remaining citizens are likely to be covered? A N S W E R
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF LAW AND JUSTICE

(SHRI K. VENKATAPATHY)

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) A Statement showing the number of Elector’s Photo Identity Cards (EPIC) issued in various States/Union Territories provided by the Election Commission of India is laid on the Table of the House.

(c) It has been the endeavor of the Election Commission to achieve 100% coverage under the EPIC scheme, as far as practicable, in a time bound manner. Even though efforts have been constantly made to cover all the electors under the EPIC scheme, various reasons such as natural calamities, engagement of administrative machinery to works other than election work and apathy of voters themselves are some of the reasons why the progress has been uneven.

records.qtitle: JHUGGI JHONPRI CLUSTERS IN METRO CITIES
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that a large number of JJ clusters have come up in the four metro cities of the country;

(b) whether it is also a fact that some of these, like the one in Mumbai are described to be one of the biggest slums in whole of Asia;

(c) whether it is also a fact that these clusters/slums point to stark reality of poverty in the country and lower our image;

(d) whether Government propose to evolve a unified approach for their development and ensure steps to provide certain basic amenities including housing to them; and

(e) if not, reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING & URBAN POVERTY ALLEVIATION

( KUMARI SELJA )

(a)to(c): Yes, Sir.

(d)to(e): The Government has launched the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) to assist cities and towns in taking up housing and infrastructural facilities for the urban poor in 63 cities in the country under the Basic Services to the Urban Poor (BSUP) Programme. For other cities, for taking up housing and slum upgradation programmes, the Integrated Housing and Slum Development Programme (IHSDP) has been launched with the objective to strive for holistic slum development, with a healthy and enabling environment by providing adequate shelter and basic infrastructure facilities to the slum dwellers. Both BSUP and IHSDP are under implementation since December-2005. The duration of JNNURM would be seven years beginning from the year 2005-06.

records.qtitle: SAVING MT. EVEREST FROM ENVIRONMENTAL EROSION .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(b) whether Government are aware that six world heritage sites including Mount Everest could be at risk from the impact of climate change;

(c) whether it is a fact that a group of experts has urged the United Nations to list these locations as being in danger;

(d) whether Government have considered any steps as its contribution to save the Mount Everest from environmental erosion; and

(e) if so, the details in this regard?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS

(SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA)

(a) & (b) There have been media reports, mostly in the international media, regarding impacts of climate change on world heritage sites. Some references to Mount Everest have been made following a meeting of United Nations Educational Scientific and Cultutral Organistions’s (UNESCO’s) World Heritage Committee in July 2005. Mount Everest is not located in India but is situated on the border of Nepal and China.

(c) & (d) The World Heritage Centre and the International Union of Conservation of Nature and Natural Resources (IUCN) have not recommended inclusion of Mount Everest as a heritage site in danger.

records.qtitle: FUND FOR BENEFIT OF TELEPHONE SUBSCRIBERS .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that TRAI has constituted a fund for the benefit of Telephone subscribers;

(b) if so, the details in this regard;

(c) the sources of finance for the fund;

(d) whether Government have made any initial contribution to the fund; and

(e) if not, the reasons for the same?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY

(DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD)

(a) Yes, Sir. Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has established the Telecommunication Consumers Education and Protection Fund.

(b) The Fund has been established through issue of a Regulation, viz., “Telecommunication Consumers Education and Protection Fund Regulations, 2007” (6 of 2007) dated 15th June, 2007 in Gazette of India.

(c) Any amount charged from the subscriber in excess of the rates of telecommunication services determined under any regulation or order or direction made under the TRAI Act or amount in excess of the rates announced by the service providers, where the rates have been notified under market forbearance and which could not be refunded to the concerned subscribers and thus lying as unclaimed with the service providers, shall constitute the corpus of the Telecommunication Consumers Education and Protection Fund.

(d) No, Sir.

(e) The Telecommunication Consumers Education and Protection Fund Regulations, 2007 do not provide for Government funding.

records.qtitle: STEPS TAKEN TO RESTORE NORMALCY AFTER RIOTS .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) the details of States/places where riots took place in the last six months of the country;

(b) the reasons for these riots; and

(c) the steps taken by Government or State Governments to restore normalcy?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL)

(a): During the last six months, no communal riot is reported to have taken place in the country.

(b) to (c): Do not arise.

records.qtitle: REASONS FOR DEATH OF PRISONERS IN TIHAR JAIL .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) the measures taken by Government to ascertain the reasons of seven deaths of prisoners which took place in Tihar Jail within 10 days in the month of June of the current year which is an important incident itself;

(b) whether the food/meals provided to prisoners is one of the main reasons for the same; and

(c) if so, whether Government are going to take any action against the officers/staff to avoid recurrence of such incidents?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRIMATI V. RADHIKA SELVI)

(a): In every case of death, mandatory inquest by area Sub Divisional Magistrate/Metropolitan Magistrate under Section 176 Cr.P.C. is carried out. Necessary action is taken on the basis of SDM’s/Metropolitan Magistrates report in case the report indicts any foul play by Jail staff.

(b): No, Sir.

(c): Does not arise in view of (b) above.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that discontent in Arunachal Pradesh has reached such a level that people there are thinking in terms of aligning with China;

(b) whether it is also a fact that China is not issuing visas to the residents there on the ground that it considers Arunachal Pradesh and its residents as part of China; and

(c) the steps Government have taken to address the situation?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE)

(a) No.

(b)-(c) China illegally claims approximately 90,000 square kilometres of Indian territory in the State of Arunachal Pradesh. China did not give a visa to an officer of the Arunachal Pradesh cadre of the Indian Administrative Service to visit China in May 2007 on a study tour organised by the Department of Personnel and Training. Government of India have conveyed its regret and disappointment to the Chinese side on this occasion through the Chinese Embassy in New Delhi and the Indian Embassy in Beijing. Government have also reiterated their position that Arunachal Pradesh is an integral part of India.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that several hundred tonnes of plastic and other kind of waste is generated by hill stations in the country throughout the year particularly during tourists seasons;

(b) whether any regular arrangements exist there for disposal of the waste;

(c) if so, the details in this regard;

(d) whether any campaign is carried out at these hill stations to guide and educate tourists for proper disposal of this waste; and

(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS

(Sh. NAMO NARAIN MEENA)

(a) to ( c) Plastic waste form 5 to 10% of the total municipal solid waste generated in cities and towns of the country including hill stations. Hill stations in particular face increasing quantity of garbage and plastic waste generation during the tourist season. As per the manual of the Ministry of Urban Development, it is estimated that 100,000 tonnes of garbage is generated per day in the country.

Concerned local bodies of hill stations collect plastic waste alongwith municipal solid wastes and dispose them off in landfills or send it for recycling. However, due to lack of facilities for complete collection of municipal solid waste, plastics are sometimes found littered on the hill stations.

(d) to (e) The Ministry of Environment & Forests has notified the Plastic, Manufacture and Usage Rules, 1999 amended 2000 and 2003 banning the manufacture, stocking, distribution and selling of carry bags made of virgin/recycle plastic which are below 18 to 12 inches in size and 20 microns in thickness. Some hill stations have also notified stricter norms to control use and disposal of non bio-degradable garbage in private and public places. The concerned local authorities from time to time undertake mass awareness campaign including involving local voluntary groups exhorting tourists to dispose solid waste in designated places/dustbins.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that NRIs have complained against the misuse of Section 498A of the Dowry Prevention law by Police, to the Prime Minister and the President of India;

(b) if so, the details in this regard;

(c) whether it is also a fact that out of 58000 cases filed under the provisions of the Dowry Prevention law 25000 were found fake;

(d) whether it is also a fact that a website 498.org. has also been established to make a case against the provision; and

(e) what steps Government are contemplating to make the law more balanced and effective?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI MANIKRAO H. GAVIT)

(a) & (b): Section 498A is a section of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and not the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961. Government has received a couple of representations from the Indians residing in foreign countries against alleged misuse of Section 498A of IPC by their wives etc. However, information in respect of complaints received from NRIs is not compiled separately.

(c): As per statistics compiled by the National Crime Records Bureau, the number of cases reported under the Dowry Prohibition Act during the year 2005 were 3204, whereas, 3592 cases were reported during 2004. However, no separate information is available about the cases found fake out of the above.

(d): As per information provided by the Ministry of Overseas Indian Affairs, there is an NGO in San Francisco named ‘Rakshak’ which has established a website http://www.498.org. and http://rakshak.info. for highlighting the problems of NRIs.

(e): The Government has been receiving representations from various quarters for amending Section 498A of the IPC. The Criminal Law (Amendment) Bill, 2003 had, inter alia, a proposal to make Section 498A of the IPC compoundable, but the same was dropped by the Government on the request of women’s organizations, to retain the effectiveness of this legal provision.

records.qtitle: . RISE IN TYRE PRICES DESPITE REDUCTION IN DUTIES .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that despite reduction in the duties, prices of tyres have been going up, if so, what are the reasons therefor; and

(b) what steps Government have taken to address this situation?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY

(SHRI ASHWANI KUMAR)

(a) : Tyre is a de-licensed and de-reserved item. Tyre prices are determined by market forces. Tyre prices have increased primarily due to increase in input-prices and increased demand for tyres.

(b): Government has reduced customs duty from 12.5% to 10% to make imports of tyres cheaper and augment the supply of tyres. Under Regional Trade Agreements, tyres can also be imported at preferential rates of customs duty which would be lower than 10%.

records.qtitle: VISIT OF RELATIVES OF POWS IN PAKISTAN .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that a delegation of kith and kins of 1971 war prisoners, reportedly lodged in Pakistani jails visited Pakistan recently on an invitation extended by Government of Pakistan;

(b) if so, the details in this regard;

(c) whether it is a fact that on reaching Pakistan, they were not allowed to visit the jails;

(d) whether Government took up the matter with the Government of Pakistan; and

(e) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE)

(a)&(b) Yes, Sir. A group comprising members of the families of missing defence personnel visited Pakistan from June 1-14, 2007. They visited 10 jails in Pakistan. Indian prisoners were presented before the relatives. The visiting family members did not come across missing defence personnel in the jails they visited. However, it was confirmed that one of the missing personnel had been killed in action and not taken Prisoner of War.

(c) No, Sir.

(d)&(e) Do not arise.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) the present extent of green cover in the country, in terms of percentage;

(b) whether it is a fact that the green cover has not inched forward beyond 19 per cent;

(c) whether it is also a fact that in terms of the forest policy of 1950s, the green cover was envisaged as 25 per cent and in terms of this, we have not added to our forest cover and the danger of global warming is looming over our head; and

(d) the steps Government are considering to address the situation?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS

(SHRI S.REGUPATHY)

(a) The present Forest and Tree Cover (FTC) in the country is 23.68%.

(b) No, Sir. There is marginal increase in the forest cover. The status of forest cover in the country is as under: 


Assessment year		1997	1999	2001	2003
% of geographical area	19.27	19.39	20.55	20.64




(c)	No, Sir. The National Forest Policy, 1952 aimed at maintaining 
1/3rd of land area under forests. In spite of making all efforts, we are able 
to maintain 23.57 forest land, 20.64 forest cover and 23.68% Forest and tree 
cover.


(d)	The government of India has taken following steps to achieve 33% 
Forest and Tree Cover (FTC) in the country:




·Guidelines have been issued by Government of India on 15-12-2004 to the States 
for rationalization of regulatory provision about felling and transport of 
trees grown on private lands;



·The Ministry has mooted a Multi-Stake Holder Partnership (MSP) framework for 
forestation.



·States have been advised to constitute State-level coordination committee 
under chairmanship of Chief Secretaries for eliciting cooperation of all land-
owning Departments for contributing towards increase in FTC.



·Under National Afforestation Plan (NAP) Scheme Rs 1180.72 crores were released 
to support 729 FDA projects through 24,215 JFMCs for treating a total project 
area of 9.36 lakh ha.



·A restructured scheme for Grants-in-Aid for Greening India was launched in 
2005-06 to promote production and use of quality planting material in tree 
planning.



·As a follow-up of the Mid-Term Appraisal of 10th Five Year Plan, a new scheme 
for afforestation involving Panchayati Raj Institution for tree planning on 
non-forest lands is mooted.



·Establishment of two new Eco-Task Force (ETF) battalions for eco-restoration 
of degraded areas was mooted by the Ministry, in addition to supporting the 
existing four ETF battalions.



·State Government and Union Territories Administrations have been requested to 
formulate and implement a comprehensive Media Plan to create awareness about 
tree planting.

records.qtitle: MONITORING THE COURSE OF RIVER CHANNELS .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that it is an engineering necessity to monitor regularly the course of river channels upstream/downstream of all bridges, dams, weirs, etc. which affect the natural flow of the rivers so that likely damages to pucca structures across the rivers are remedied in time; and

(b) the names of rivers in respect of which this is not being done and the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS

(SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA)

(a) & (b) According to the information received from the Ministry of Water Resources, the Central Water Commission (CWC) carries out gauge, discharge, sediment study and observes pre and post monsoon cross section on important rivers on regular basis at selected location. These information are used for specific study and in carrying out design of important structures on river course. While monitoring specially for the course of river channels, upstream/downstream of all Bridges, Dams and Weirs are not carried out by CWC, morphological study of rivers Gandak, Ghaghara and Sutlaj, using remote sensing technique, is done. This includes performance evaluation of major flood control/hydraulic structures such as embankment, spurs and bridges executed so far from morphological point of view as well as their effect on river behavior.

records.qtitle: SRAVANA SAKA EMPOWERING CENTRAL GOVERNMENT TO DEPLOY MILITARY TROOPS .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government are considering a proposal to empower the Central Government to deploy military troops in any part of the country;

(b) if so, the considerations that have necessitated this empowerment; and

(c) what are the existing provisions in this regard?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI MANIKRAO HODLYA GAVIT)

(a) to (c): The information is being collected and will be laid on the Table of the House.

records.qtitle: CONSTRUCTION OF ROAD UPTO BASE CAMP OF MOUNT EVEREST BY CHINESE GOVERNMENT .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Chinese Government are constructing a 105 km. long road up to the base camp of Mount Everest;

(b) if so, whether Government have examined the implications of the Chinese proposal from the point of view of country’s defence as also the environmental angle; and

(c) if so, with what results?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF DEFENCE

(SHRI A.K. ANTONY)

(a) to (c): Xinhua (official Chinese news agency) reported on 19th June 2007 that China would begin building a `highway` on Mount Everest in Tibet Autonomous Region so as to ease the path of those bearing the Olympic torch. Construction of the road will kick off at Everest Base Camp. The project aims to turn a 108-km rough road linking Tingri County of Xigaze prefecture at the foot of the mountain to the Base Camp into a blacktop highway fenced by undulating guardrails. On completion, the highway will become a major route for tourists and mountaineers. The Government keeps a constant watch on all developments having a bearing on India`s security and takes all necessary measures to safeguard it.

records.qtitle: BUILDING STRATEGIC RESERVES BASED ON CHEAP OIL .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware that China imported 12.4 million barrels of crude for its strategic storage tanks in December, which was more than 50 percent higher than its November intake, taking advantage of cheaper oil; and

(b) if so, what are the reasons that Government does not consider such courses for building up reserves based on cheap crude price?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS

(SHRI DINSHA PATEL)

(a) As per the FACTS Global Energy Report Issue of March 2007, 12.4 million barrels of crude were offloaded to the Chinese storage sites of its Strategic Petroleum Reserves (SPRs) at Zhenhai, Zhejiang Province in December, 2006. This was in addition to the 3 and 4 million barrels of injections in November, 2006.

(b) In order to enhance the energy security of the country and to safeguard against short term supply disruptions, Government have approved setting up of 5 Million Metric Tonnes (MMT) strategic storage of crude oil at three locations, viz. Vizag (1.0 MMT), Mangalore (1.5 MMT) and Padur, Udipi (2.5 MMT). This project is likely to be completed by the end of 11th Five Year Plan. The Government is planning to further enhance its strategic reserve capacity to 15 MMT in the next phase.

records.qtitle: PRICE OF LNG TO BE IMPORTED FROM IRAN
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan

(a) whether it is a fact that Iran has demanded price hike for supply of Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) to India;

(b) if so, what are the details in this regard including likely total impact; and

(c) whether India has accepted the price hike proposal?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS

(SHRI DINSHA PATEL)

(a): No formal proposal has been received from Iran regarding price revision of LNG.

(b) & (c): In view of (a) above, do not arise.

records.qtitle: . TRAINING TO JUDGES ON DISPOSAL OF CYBER CRIME CASES. .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are considering a proposal to set up specialized training centres in cyber crime for judges in order to speed up disposal of cases related to such offences; and

(b) if so, the details thereof?.
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF LAW & JUSTICE

(SHRI K. VENKATAPATHY)

(a) & (b) :The Government, at present, has no specific proposal to set up specialized training centers for providing training in the area of cyber crimes to judges. However, the Government conducts regular awareness and training programmes on cyber laws and cyber crimes for Judicial Officers. National Judicial Academy at Bhopal also conducts programmes to train judges in cyber laws and cyber crimes. 43 judges participated in each of the workshop conducted by the Academy in 2004 and 2006.

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF LAW AND JUSTICE

(SHRI K. VENKATAPATHY)

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:

(b) what has been the number of beneficiaries and amount of benefit given in the last one year, alongwith the details thereof, State-wise; and

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI SHARAD PAWAR)

(a) to (c): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT IN RESPECT OF PARTS (a) TO (c) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 93 FOR 17/08/2007 REGARDING COVERAGE UNDER CROP INSURANCE SCHEME.

(a) & (b): The details of coverage of States, farmers, claims amount paid and farmers benefited during 2005-06 under National Agricultural Insurance Scheme (NAIS) are given in the Annexure.

(c): The NAIS is open to all States and Union Territories for coverage. At present 23 States and 2 Union Territories are implementing the scheme. The Government of India and the Implementing Agency i.e. Agriculture Insurance Company of India Ltd. (AIC), from time to time, keep on persuading the non-implementing States/UTs for participation in the scheme.

records.qtitle: DOUBLING OF TRACK BETWEEN VARANASI ALLAHABAD AND ALLAHABAD RAI BARELI .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is a single track between Varanasi to Allahabad and Allahabad to Rai Bareli;

(b) whether there is any proposal to convert it to double track;

(c) if so, the details of the proposal; and

(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

(SHRI R.VELU)

(a): Yes, Sir.

(b): No, Sir.

(c): Does not arise.

(d): The traffic on the suggested Varanasi-Allahabad and Allahabad-Rai Bareli sections have not reached the level to justify doubling as the doubling of single line section/providing multiple lines on double sections is taken up when their carrying capacity become saturated.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that River Ganga at Allahabad has been depositing heavy silt along the bank on Allahabad side;

(b) whether it is also a fact that the main channel has swung away towards the low lands on Phaphamau side;

(c) whether it is also a fact that the main channel, as a result of tangential flow towards the left bank, is liable to cause colossal loss of property, cut off rail and road communication from across Ganga and cause long term damage; and

(d) if so, the steps Government have taken to address the situation?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS

(SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA)

(a) to (d) A statement is laid on the Table of the House.

Statement referred to in reply to parts (a) to (d) of Rajya Sabha Starred Question No.76 to be answered on Thursday, the 16th August, 2007 on “Silt along Ganga at Allahabad”.

(a) to (d) As per the report of Ministry of Water Resources, a Technical Team comprising officers from Government of Uttar Pradesh, Ganga Flood Control Commission (Patna), Ministry of Railways and the Central Water Commission was constituted and visited Allahabad in May, 2007 to study the matter relating to river Ganga changing its course in the town. The Technical Team observed that river Ganga was shifting towards the Phaphamau side during the last 3-4 years. The river has formed a meandering loop and it was observed that about 1.5-2.0 kms. upstream of the bridges, some erosion has taken place. However, the extent of erosion could not be found out.

The Team also observed that the approach to the road and railway bridges is quite protected and stacked boulders placed there will also dampen the river flow. The river flow is still 600 to 700 metres away from the existing road and the Phaphamau town is protected by the road itself. Some protection works have also been carried out by the Government of Uttar Pradesh earlier at the junction of straight and curved portions of guide bund of upstream of the railway bridge. Thus, no immediate danger to the guide bund, road and railway bridges or Phaphamau town from floods is anticipated.

The Team has recommended the need for
(i) close monitoring of the flow pattern of the river during the current monsoon season,
(ii) conducting a model study on the behavior of the river in the vicinity of the bridges, and
(iii) carrying out morphological studies with remote sensing techniques in the 20 kms. reach of the river (10 kms. upstream and downstream of the bridges) by the State Government. The Ministry of Water Resources has already suggested to the Government of Uttar Pradesh to undertake the required studies and remedial measures.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government have regularized a large number of unauthorized colonies in Delhi;

(b) if so, the details in this regard and the total number of colonies regularized so far;

(c) whether any infrastructural development including sanitation, sewer lines, electricity, roads, etc. have been provided in all these colonies;

(d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; and

(e) the steps Government have taken to avoid mushrooming growth of Delhi?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT

( SHRI AJAY MAKEN )

(a): No colony has been regularized in the recent past. But guidelines and modalities are being prepared for regularisation of unauthorised colonies which have come up before July, 2002.

(b): Does not arise in view of (a) above.

(c)&(d): Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi (GNCTD) has reported that at present roads/drains exist in about 500 unauthorized colonies which are located on private land. Electricity and water supply are also being provided by DISCOMs and Delhi Jal Board.

(e): Municipal Corporation of Delhi has reported that it has revamped its infrastructure for detection and control of unauthorized construction in Delhi. In this context, a number of measures have been taken which includes restructuring and strengthening of existing Central Control Room, Zonal Control Rooms, Central Demolition Squad and formation of Special Task Force.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government had decided to send a lunar mission;

(b) if so, the status of the proposal; and

(c) by when the proposal is expected to materialize?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE PRIME MINISTER’S OFFICE
(SHRI PRITHVIRAJ CHAVAN):

(a) Yes, Sir. An unmanned Indian Mission to Moon, called Chandrayaan-1, has been approved by the Government.

(b) The Critical Design Reviews of Chandrayaan-1 Space Craft and payload systems have been completed. The flight units of space systems and scientific instruments are in advanced stage of realization. Commissioning the Indian Deep Space Network (IDSN), required to track the Chandrayaan-1 is progressing satisfactorily. The 18m antenna has successfully undergone testing and evaluation and is ready for use. The critical design review for the 32m antenna was completed.

(c) The Chandrayaan-1 Mission is presently scheduled for launch in the first half of 2008.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) the number of Central schemes currently in operation in various States for poverty alleviation;

(b) whether there is any monitoring mechanism available for watching the performance of these schemes; and

(c) whether these schemes have been reviewed recently; and

(d) if so, the results thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING & URBAN POVERTY ALLEVIATION

( KUMARI SELJA )

(a): With a view to ameliorate the living conditions of the urban poor and to reduce the urban poverty in the country, Ministry of Housing & Urban Poverty Alleviation is implementing a centrally sponsored urban poverty alleviation scheme named Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana (SJSRY) on all India basis, since 1.12.1997.

(b): The scheme of Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana (SJSRY) is being implemented in the country through State/Union Territory Governments. The scheme is monitored through Quarterly Progress Reports (QPRs), review meetings and field visits by the senior officers of the Ministry of Housing & Urban Poverty Alleviation. In addition to these, a High Level Monitoring Committee (HLMC), headed by Secretary in the Ministry of Housing & Urban Poverty Alleviation, with representatives from different sectoral departments as well as other stakeholders such as Reserve Bank of India, State Governments, also monitors the scheme on a half yearly basis.

(c)&(d): The scheme of Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana (SJSRY) has been evaluated recently through M/s Access Development Services Limited, New Delhi, in 9 representative States/UTs. The major suggestions of the evaluation study include: focus on supporting urban self-employment, marketing and credit linkages to the beneficiaries, proper market assessment before setting up of micro-enterprises, training needs assessment etc.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that China is considering a proposal to link Kigaje with capital Lhasa by 280 Km. rail link by 2010; and

(b) if so, whether it would pose a security risk to India and if so, the steps being considered to address the situation?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE)

(a) Government have seen Chinese media reports stating that the Qinghai-Tibet railway is expected to be further extended from Lhasa to Xigaze. These reports also state that the construction of this 254-kilometres long rail section is expected to be completed by 2010.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether he is aware that there is at present acute shortage of small coins in a number of city markets and commuters/consumers are facing acute shortage of coins at the hands of bus conductors, taxi and scooter drivers and vendors of daily necessities;

(b) whether the shortage is very sudden; and

(c) if so, the steps being taken to address the problem?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF FINANCE ( SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM)

( a ) to ( c ) : A Statement is laid on the Table of the House 

A Statement referred to with regard to reply to para (a) to (c) Rajya. Sabha 
Starred Question No. 45 for answer on 14.8.2007 by Shrimati Java Bachchan on 
acute shortage of coins


(a)  to (c) : There have been some reports as well as complaints from 
public/trade bodies regarding shortage of coins in certain markets. The Reserve
 Bank of India has reported that the shortage is being felt for the last one 
year. The following steps have been taken to address the problem:


(i)	The Government has been minting Rs.2 coins in Ferritic Stainless
	Steel (FSS) instead of cupro-nickel since 2005 and has also
	decided to mint Rs.5 coin in Ferritic Stainless Steel instead of
	curpro-nickel.


(ii)	Minting of Re.l, Rs.2 and Rs.5 coins has been placed on fast track.
	Several issue offices of Reserve Bank of India held coin melas,
	distributed coins through mobile banks at market place etc.
	Reserve Bank of India has also advised select currency chest
	branches to do the same.


(iii)	To cater to the large demand of hotels, restaurants, retail shops
	etc., distribution arrangements have been made through registered
	Association/Trade bodies wherever they have come forward for the
	purpose.


(iv)	In Mumbai, arrangements have been made for distribution of coins
	through five post offices and similar arrangement is being put in
	place in other States.


(v)	All the Banks have been advised to ensure distribution of coins
 through their currency chest branches proactively and they have also been 
advised to identify some branches in each district for the specific purpose of 
coin distribution


(vi)	Banks have been advised to consider installation of coin vending
	machines

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 24 FOR 13.08.2007 BY SHRIMATI JAYA BACHCHAN REGARDING ISO-9000 CERTIFICATE TO SCHOOLS

records.qtitle: JAMPACKED RUNNING OF LOCAL TRAINS IN MUMBAI .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that local trains in Mumbai have been running jampacked for last several years so much that commuters find it difficult to move in a compartment or get down over a station particularly physically challenged and commuters who are casual visitors to Mumbai;

(b) whether it is also a fact that often there are long queues over ticket counters as a result of which commuters often miss their scheduled trains; and

(c) what are the improvements Government have carried out all these years to address the woes of the commuters?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

(SHRI R.VELU)

(a) Yes, Sir. During the peak hours in morning and evening, there is heavy rush. However, special coaches have been earmarked in these trains for the convenience of handicapped persons and lady passengers.

(b) & (c) Booking counters are also crowded during peak rush hours. To address this problem, a number of steps have been taken/ are being taken by Railways, which include provision of additional booking counters, provision of Coupon Validating Machines, provision of computerised Unreserved Ticketing System. Instructions have also been issued to extend Jansadharan Ticket Booking Sevak (JTBS) scheme to Western Railway. Provision of Contactless Smart Card based ticketing system and Automatic Ticket Vending Machines (ATVMs) is also on hand. Improvement in ticketing system is a continuous and ongoing process.

(b) & (c): The doubling of Jalandhar - Jammu Tawi line, part of which falls in Jammu & Kashmir, is already in progress and complete double line on this route will be available by 2008-09.

(b)

(d)

(e)

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government propose to conduct a survey shortly first of its kind in the country to ascertain the languages of various parts of the country; if so, the details in this regard;

(b) if so, the objectives thereof;

(c) whether it is a fact that according to earlier findings 220 languages are spoken in the country;

(d) whether there has been an~ increase over this figure; and

(e) the department entrusted with the responsibility to conduct the survey?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (SMT. D. PURANDESWARI)

(a) Yes, Sir. There is a proposal to conduct a Linguistic Survey of the country, the report of which will be available after 10 years of its commissioning.. The total budgetary requirement during 11th Plan period for this project has been estimated at Rs.280 crores. During the 12~a Plaza period estimated expenditure is Rs.308 crores.

(b) The Survey aims at providing a systematic and comprehensive account of the status of Indian languages diversity and multilingualism, inter lingual relationships and dynamics of languages. To do so, it will exploit advances in technology to document prepare databases of different kinds, corpora of spoken and written varieties and produce a wide range of linguistic materials in. both print and electronic form.

(c) As per Census 1991 there are 114 languages in the country. 216 mother tongues, each of which is spoken by 10,000 more people, are listed under these languages.

(d) As per provisional data for 2001 Census, the number of languages of India has gone up from 114 to 122. The number of identifiable mother tongues, which have returned 10,000 or more speakers at tile all India level, has also gone up to 234.

(e) The Survey will be conducted under the aegis of Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Human Resource Development.

records.qtitle: WITHDRAWAL OF CHETAK AND CHEETAH HELICOPTERS .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan

(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and

(c) the details of the new versions of helicopters proposed to be put in their place? ANSWER (SHRI A.K. ANTONY)

(a) & (b): Yes Sir, because the existing fleet of helicopters is of 1960s and 1970s vintage and, hence, inadequate for the present operational requirement of the Indian Army.

(c) Based on the qualitative requirements framed by the Indian Army, the acquisition process in terms of the Defence Procurement Procedure for procurement of new helicopters compliant with these qualitative requirements, is under way.

records.qtitle: UTILIZATION OF SCIENTIFIC MANPOWER BY DRDO .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that India has the third largest scientific and technical manpower in the world, including DRDO;

(b) if so, whether it is also a fact that people in India derive hardly any benefit from the size of the manpower, including DRDO;

(c) whether the technologies developed by the huge manpower are not utilized and the taxpayer’s money goes waste; and

(d) if so, what are the reasons therefor, and whether Government propose to review its unfruitful policy in this regard? ANSWER (SHRI A.K. ANTONY)
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF DEFENCE

(a) There is no authentic statistics available in this regard. However, Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) holds 6812 scientific and 10959 technical manpower.

(b) No, Sir. Science and technology has been used as an effective instrument for the socio-economic development of the country. The output of Science and Technology has benefited the society and improved the quality of life. The technologies developed by DRDO viz Missiles, Radars, Battle Tanks, Electronic Warfare System, Combat Vehicles, Armaments and Explosive, Life Support systems etc. have been used by all the three Services, other security services and spin off to the society as well.

(c) No, Sir.

(d) Does not arise.

Development of tourist spots under its various schemes of infrastructure development for tourist circuits and destinations; Focusing on growth of hotel infrastructure particularly budget hotels; Enhancing connectivity through augmentation of air capacity and improving road infrastructure to major tourist attractions;

records.qtitle: INCREASE IN LENDING AND DEPOSIT RATES BY BANKS
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) what is the scenario with regard to interest rates in the country in the months ahead;

(b) whether it is a fact that lending and deposit rates are being tweaked up by several banks:

(c) if so, whether it points to the possibility of :interest rates going up; and

(d) whether the upward rates of interest would help mop up excess liquidity in the system?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI PAWAN KUMAR BANSAL)

(a),(b),(c) & (d): The Annual Policy Statement for the year 2005-06 issued by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), had stated that `the outcome for interest rates depends mainly on the outlook for inflation, growth prospects and investment demand and it is not possible to predict short-run movements in interest rates`. RBI has deregulated the interest rates on advances above Rs.2 lakh with effect from October 18, 1994. Interest rates are determined[ by the banks themselves with the approval of their Board of` Directors subject to Benchmark Prime Lending Rate (BPLR) and Spread guidelines. In order to enhance transparency in pricing of their loan products, banks have been advised by the RBI to fix their BPLR after taking into account

(i) actual cost of funds,
(ii) operating ,expenses and

(iii) a minimum margin to cover regulatory requirement of provisioning/capital charge and profit margin and ensure that the BPLR truly reflects the actual cost. Individual banks, therefore, determine interest rates to be charged from a particular borrower subject to their BPLR and spread guidelines. However, loans up to Rs.2 lakh carry the prescription of not exceeding the BPLR.

RBI has also given freedom to commercial banks to fix the, ir own interest rates on domestic term deposits of various maturities with the prior approval of their respective Board of Directors with effect from October 22, 1997. As such, the rates of interest on deposits are being determined by the banks themselves. However, RBI regulates interest rates on savings bank accounts. As stated in the Third/Quarter Review of Annual Statement on Monetary Policy for 2006-07, issued on January 31,2007, the Reserve Bank will ensure that appropriate liquidity is maintained in tlhe system so that all legitimate requirements of credit are met, particularly for productive purposes, consistent with the objective of price and financial stability. Towards this end, the Reserve Bank will continue its policy of active demand management of liquidity through open market operations (OMO) including the Market Stabilisation Scheme (MSS), Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF} and Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) and using all the policy instruments at i~ disposal flexibly as and when the situation warrants.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) what is the status in respect of track renewal programme;

(b) whether it is a fact that almost all the railway tracks need to be renewed; and

(c) what is the outlay involve in the programme? ANSWER
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS


(SHRI R.VELU)

(a): Every year planning is made to include track renewal works which becomes due for renewal in that year. For the year 2007-08 works costing Rs.4663.5 crore have been identified and included in works programme 2007-08.

(b): No, Sir. Track renewal are carried out on age-cum condition basis criteria laid down in Indian Railways Permanent Way Manual and as per traffic needs. Nearly 3000 km. tracks become due for renewal on annual basis as per present level of traffic.

(c): Outlay involved in track renewal works included in works programme 2007-08 is Rs.4663.5 crore (Gross).

(c) whether the tracks are fit enough to bear the increased speed?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Chairman of Policy Determination Committee has recently observed that DDA is most corrupt agency in Delhi;

(b) whether it is also a fact that even the topmost officers of DDA are aware of the extent of corruption but find themselves helpless in the matter; and

(c) whether Government have ever made an assessment of areas of functioning by DDA where its officers and staff indulge in corruption & the possibility of time bound computerized work & fixation of responsibility without the personal contact of applicants?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT

( SHRI AJAY MAKEN )


(a): No such observation has come to the notice of the Ministry.

(b): Delhi Development Authority (DDA) has reported that corruption cases in DDA are dealt with firmly and criminal cases and disciplinary proceedings are instituted wherever found necessary. A number of measures have also been taken for improving transparency in the functioning of DDA and preventing corruption.

(c): Various measures have been taken from time to time to increase the transparency and reduce scope for irregularities or corruption in DDA. Facilitation counters have been established for helping citizens in their work with DDA; senior officers of DDA are accessible to the public through public hearing for attending to their grievances; schemes, rules, procedures, application forms, etc. have been put on the web site; draw of lots for allotment of houses has been computerized; posting of tender notice on the web site has been introduced, disposal of commercial plots is done through well publicised public auction and various other measures taken to eliminate discretionary power and bring in objectivity and transparency in functioning of DDA. Review of various measures taken for quality investigation, quick disposal of vigilance cases and improving transparency in various functions is also undertaken.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that a vibrant summit took place in Gujarat in January, 2007 where investors across the globe took part; and

(b) if so, the outcome of the summit including tile issues discussed and the projects cleared for investment and the MoUs, if any, signed there?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF OVERSEAS INDIAN AFFAIRS

(SHRI VAYALAR RAVI)

(a) Yes Sir. The State Government organized the vibrant Gujarat global investors meet at Ahmedabad on January 12-13, 2007.

(b) As reported by the State government, during the summit, seminars were held in 9 sectors-Oil and Gas, Chemicals and Petrochemicals, Special Economic Zone and port-led Development, agro and food processing, engineering, auto and ceramics, bio-technology, textiles and apparels, gems and jewellery and pharmaceuticals. 343 Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) were signed and 20 announcements were made for investments in the state of Gujarat with a total investment of Rs. 4,61,835/- crore.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) the approximate monthly charges an individual has to pay for viewing cable TV through CAS/Dish TV and other such systems introduced through MTNL etc. including the initial expenditure;

(b) what is the similar monthly expenditure an individual has to pay under the conventional cable TV without CAS; and

(c) whether it is a fact that entertainment through CAS regime is much costlier and is liable to deprive millions of poor families of their right to entertainment and information and if so, the steps proposed to be taken to address the situation?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING AND PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS

(SHRI P. R. DASMUNSI)



(a): Total monthly charges will be dependant on the individual choice and scheme of STB and number of pay channels chosen by consumer for viewing. The charges to be paid in the CAS notified areas for receiving TV channels through Cable Network have been prescribed in Telecom Regulatory Authority of India’s (TRAI) Tariff Order dated 31.08.2006. The Tariff Orders are available on the TRAI website www.trai.gov.in.

(b): For cable TV in non CAS areas, provisions of Tariff order dated 01.10.2004 as amended from time to time are applicable. The main feature of this tariff order is that price payable by a subscriber is as prevailing on 26.12.2003, with a subsequent enhancement of 7%. If there are any additional pay channels being provided by the service providers after 26.12.2003, then there is a provision for increase in subscription charges.

(c): Whether the subscribers’ monthly bill will go up or go down after implementation of CAS will depend on the present monthly bill, on the number of pay channels one desires to watch and the scheme of Set Top Box which the consumer opts for after introduction of CAS. It is not true that millions of poor families would be deprived of entertainment as a result of CAS implementation.

records.name: KAMAL AKHTAR
records.qn_text:
(a) what are the details of the progress in regard to the proposal to interlink rivers in the country;

(b) whether the proposal has finally been abandoned; and

(c) if so, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES

( SHRI JAI PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV)  

(a) The Ministry of Water Resources(MOWR) (erstwhile Ministry of Irrigation) and Central Water Commission(CWC) formulated a National Perspective Plan(NPP) for Water Resources Development in 1980 envisaging inter-basin transfer of water from surplus basins to deficit basins/areas for optimum utilization of water resources. The NPP comprises two components, namely, Himalayan Rivers Development Component and Peninsular Rivers Development Component. National Water Development Agency (NWDA) was set up under the MOWR in 1982 for carrying out various technical studies to establish the feasibility of the proposals of NPP. Based on various studies conducted, NWDA has identified 30 links (16 under Peninsular Component & 14 under Himalayan Component) for preparation of Feasibility Report (FRs). Out of these, FRs of 14 links under Peninsular Component and 2 links (Indian Portion) under Himalayan Component have already been completed.   Further, a Memorandum of Understanding for preparation of Detailed Project Report (DPR) of one of the link in Peninsular Component Namely Ken-Betwa link was signed among the Central Government and State Governments of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh on 25th August, 2005. Subsequently, the Central Government entrusted the preparation of the DPR of the aforesaid link to NWDA, which is planned to be completed by June, 2008.  

(b) No, Sir.

(c) Does not arise.

records.qtitle: CO OPERATION WITH USA IN THE HYDROCARBON SECTOR .

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan

(a) what is the number of technologies that have been developed by DRDO so far;

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF DEFENCE

(a) Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) has developed numerous technologies related to various systems realized for Users. These include missiles; composite materials; electronic warfare systems; avionics, radars and sonars, communication systems; signal processing; armament and explosives; combat vehicles; nuclear, biological and chemical decontamination suites; parachutes, etc.

(b) There have been more than hundred number of technologies transferred from DRDO to private industry for commercialization. Many of these technologies are dual-use technologies for defence purposes and also for civil applications.

(c) No, Sir. There is no non-utilisation of DRDO technologies. Even in the very few cases when the technology does not mature and transform into a viable product, the efforts of development of such technology in itself gives an added knowledge base to the scientific community and adds to the knowledge bank of the laboratories for use in other developmental projects.

records.qtitle: DIFFERENT ELECTRICITY RATES IN NDMC AND MCD AREAS .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there are two sets of rates of electricity in Delhi-one for consumers living in NDMC areas and the other for rest of Delhi, if so, the reasons for the discriminatory rates; and

(b) whether Government propose to do away with the discriminatory rates, if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER

( SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE )

(a) & (b) : A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) & (b) OF STARRED QUESTION NO. 92 TO BE ANSWERED IN THE RAJYA SABHA ON 05.03.2007 REGARDING DIFFERENT ELECTRICITY RATES IN NDMC AND MCD AREAS.

(a) & (b) : Yes, Sir. The tariff for consumers living in Distribution Companies

(Discoms) areas under Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) is different from the tariff for New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) area.

Tariffs for various categories of consumers of a distribution licensee are determined by the State Regulatory Commissions in accordance with the provisions of the Electricity Act, 2003. The State Government has powers under the Act to give policy directions in public interest to the SERC. The tariff rate for various categories of consumers for a DISCOM in Delhi is determined by the Delhi Electricity Regulatory Commission (DERC).

The tariff of electricity depends on the overall power purchase cost as well as the operational and financial performance of the Distribution Companies (DISCOMs), that is, Aggregate Technical and Commercial (AT&C) losses, operational expenses, capital investment for system upgradation/augmentation etc.

The tariff of National Capital Territory of Delhi for the geographical areas which are serviced by the North Delhi Power Limited (NDPL), BSES Yamuna Power Limited (BYPL) and BSES Rajdhani Power Limited (BRPL) are governed by the policy directions issued by the Government of NCT of Delhi in relation to the restructuring of the erstwhile Delhi Vidyut Board. As a matter of Policy, the Government of NCT of Delhi had decided that retail tariff for the three Distribution Licensees shall be identical till the end of 2006-07 i.e. consumers of a particular category shall pay the same retail tariffs irrespective of their geographical location. These policy directives are not applicable to the New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) and the retail tariff in the NDMC.

As the NDMC is having a revenue surplus due to low Aggregate Technical & Commercial (AT&C) loss, DERC in its order has stated that there is no need to increase tariff in the area served by NDMC. Though the privatised distribution companies have brought down the AT&C losses below the levels targeted at the time of privatisation, these losses are still higher than those in NDMC area.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) the extent to which the power sector in the country has been tapped currently; and

(b) the estimated potential of the power sector in the country at present along with the details of plans aimed at exploitation of power sector?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER
( SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE )

(a) : The installed capacity in the country as on 31st January 2007 was 128182.5 MW comprising of 33941.8 MW Hydro, 84149.9 MW Thermal and 3900 MW Nuclear and 6190.9 MW Wind.

(b) : According to the data available in the Integrated Energy Policy report, the estimated proven reserves of coal in the country is over 38100 Million tons of oil equivalent

(Mtoe), Lignite reserve is 1220 Mtoe, Oil reserve is 786 million tons, gas reserve is 1101 Mtoe and coal bed methane is 765 Mtoe. The report further indicates substantial availability of thorium reserves. The re-assessment studies of hydro-electric potential of the country, completed by the Central Electricity Authority in 1987, have placed the exploitable hydro power potential at 84,044 MW at 60% load factor which will result in an install capacity of about 1,50,000 MW on the basis of probable average load factor. In addition, currently the estimated renewable energy potential is reported to be over 84,700 MW. For optimum utilization of energy resources in the power sector, following actions have been taken: 
-	Coal to remain the main stay in the energy fuel mix.  Out of the projects
 aggregating to over 76400 MW identified for the 11th Plan, over 51,000 MW is
 coal based.


-	Nuclear capacity would increased from present 3900 MW to over 7200 MW.


-	Shelf of thermal projects aggregating to over 1,00,000 MW has 
beenprepared for taking up in the future.


-	50,000 MW hydro initiative has been launched for coordinated development
 of hydro potential.
-	During 11th Plan, capacity addition to the tune of 14,000 MW through 
renewable sources is proposed.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have received any complaints on its Tatkal scheme regarding charging of fare from passenger from first to last station of the train, the fixed charge passengers have to pay and the period in advance by which tickets are issued; and

(b) whether Government have examined these complaints, if so, with what results?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS
(SHRI R.VELU)

(a) & (b): Some complaints were received regarding charging of fare under Tatkal Scheme from originating to terminating point of the train with boarding facility from intermediate station. These complaints were replied on the basis of extant position at that time. However, in view of this as well as informal feedback received, the matter was re-examined and the zonal Railways were authorised to take decision to allow booking under Tatkal scheme from end to end or keeping it free or allowing it from intermediate station depending upon the demand pattern. The Advance Reservation Period (ARP) for booking tickets under Tatkal scheme is five days excluding the day of journey. This ARP has been kept with a view to enable passengers to book accommodation under this scheme through Internet also. Since the scheme has been generally appreciated, at present, no review is deemed necessary.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have any reports of inhuman treatment meted out to Indian prisoners in Pakistan;

(b) if so, the details in this regard; and

(c) the steps taken to address this situation?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE)


(a) to (c) A statement is placed on the Table of the House.
Statement referred to in reply to parts (a) to (c) of Rajya Sabha Starred Question No. 56 (Priority-XVI) for answer on 01.03.2007 regarding `Indian prisoners in Pakistan`


(a&b) Instances of inhuman treatment of Indian prisoners have come to the notice of consular officers of our mission in Islamabad from time to time. Pakistan authorities do not inform the Indian mission of the arrest of Indians and consular access is not given until their sentence is complete. In many cases, it is delayed even beyond that. According to available information, 95 Indians in Pakistani jails are yet to be given consular access. 378 fishermen and 144 civilian prisoners and 74 PoWs are still languishing in Pakistan jails. Indian prisoners released by Pakistan have reported ill-treatment during imprisonment.

(c) Government has consistently taken up the issue of the humane treatment and release of prisoners with Pakistan. During the Home Secretary-level talks on May 30-31, 2006 it was agreed to release all the remaining fishermen by 30 June 2006, exchange lists of civilian prisoners by 15 June 2006 and facilitate consular access by 31 July 2006 for subsequent release. As agreed, on 30 June 2006, India released 38 Pakistani civilian prisoners who had completed their sentence and provided consular access for the rest. Pakistan, however, released only 19 Indian civilian prisoners. During the Foreign Secretary-level talks on November 14-15, 2006 in New Delhi both sides agreed to release eligible civilian prisoners and fishermen whose nationality had been confirmed by December 25, 2006. During the visit of External Affairs Minister to Pakistan on January 13-14, 2007, both sides agreed to establish a committee on prisoners, comprising retired judges of the superior judiciary to visit j! ails in the two countries and propose steps to ensure humane treatment and expedite release of prisoners who have completed their prison terms.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) the details of satellites launched on 10th January, 2007 and functions assigned to each of them;

(b) the details in respect of data/pictures etc. transmitted by them, so far; and

(c) the details of fields where the data would be utilised or is proposed to be utilised?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE PRIME MINISTER`S OFFICE

(SHRI PRITHVIRAJ CHAVAN):

(a) Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV-C7) launched on 10th January, 2007, carried 4 satellites viz.,
(i) CARTOSAT-2 for Cartography
(ii) Space Capsule Recovery Experiment (SRE) to demonstrate our capability to recover an orbiting capsule safely back on earth and also for conducting long duration micro gravity experiments
(iii) LAPAN-TUBSAT – a 55 Kg Video Surveillance Satellite belonging to Indonesia and
(iv) NANO-PEHUENSAT-1 of Argentina meant for carrying out amateur radio experiments.

(b) & (c)India`s CARTOSAT-2, carrying a Panchromatic camera (PAN) with a resolution of better than 1m and a swath of 9.6 km has given satisfactory images over India and other parts of the Globe. CARTOSAT-2 data will be useful for detailed large scale mapping applications and will be utilized for various urban and rural infrastructure development purposes as well as for Land Information System (LIS) and Geographical Information System

(GIS).
India`s Space capsule Recovery Experiment (SRE-1), a 550 kg capsule, demonstrated the technology for performing experiments in microgravity conditions and bringing them back. SRE-1 also provided valuable data during the re-entry and recovery operations.
LAPAN-TUBSAT of Indonesia is an Earth observation satellite and a technology demonstrator for experimental message store and forward system. PEHUENSAT-1 is an Argentinean nanosatellite for amateur radio experiment between colleges and universities of Argentina.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether there are any areas in the food processing for which machinery is not available in the country;

(b) whether there has been any import of machinery from abroad for food processing industries hitherto unavailable in the country in the last two years;

(c) whether any steps have been taken for improving the quality of food processing or covering new areas in the last two years; and

(d) if so, the details thereof? ANSWER
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES

(SHRI SUBODH KANT SAHAI)

(a): The equipments used for food processing including packaging are, in general, being manufactured indigenously both in organized as well as in Small Scale Sector. Specialized and sophisticated equipments including high capacity automatic lines such as slaughter line/abattoir equipments, meat tenderizing/processing machines, Pizza base making lines are not available indigenously.

(b): There have been import of machineries for grain milling including rice and flour milling, machineries for sugar manufacturing, for bakery, confectionery and chocolate, machineries for manufacturing of meat/poultry, and parts of other food processing machinery, etc. during the last two years namely, 2004-05 and 2005-06

(c) & (d) : During the last two years, Government have finalized Vision document 2015 for the Food Processing Industries, which envisages trebling the size of the processed food sector by increasing the level of processing of perishables from 6% to 20%, value addition from 20% to 35% and share in global food trade from 1.5% to 3% by 2015. The Government has also enacted the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 which has been passed by the Parliament on 02.08.2006 and notified on 24th August, 2006. The objective of the Act is to bring about a single statute relating to food and establish Food Safety and Standards Authority. Further, Government has decided to set up National Institute of Food Technology, Entrepreneurship & Management (NIFTEM) at Kundli, Haryana as an International Centre of excellence which will work synergistically with the industry as similar institutions within India and outside to improve the quality of food processing in the country.
Government has been providing financial assistance and other incentives for technology upgradation/modernization/setting up of food processing units. Under the Plan scheme for Technology up gradation/establishment/ modernization of food processing industries financial assistance in the form of grant-in-aid is provided to all implementing agencies @ 25% of the cost of the plant and machinery and technical civil works subject to a maximum of Rs.50 lakhs in general areas and 33.33% subject to a maximum of Rs.75 lakhs in difficult areas including North–Eastern States. In addition, assistance is also given for improvement of quality of processed food through Total Quality Management, promotion of quality assurance and safety concept, adoption of Codex and other international standards, setting up of quality testing laboratories and Research & Development in the processed food sector under its 10th Plan Schemes.

records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

(SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)

(a): As per Bulletin of the WHO/November 2004,82(11), there are 3.90 Lakh Visually Impaired children (Below the age of 15 Years) in India with prevalence rate of 0.08%.
According to Dr. R.P. Centre for Ophthalmic sciences (AIIMS) , New Delhi Visual Impairment among children are constant over the last five years. The available evidences prove that the blindness among children due to infective and nutritional causes has declined over the period.

(b) & ( c): There is no authentic information on the opinion of Professor of Computational and Visual neurosciences in the Department of Brain at Cognitive Science at MIT, USA about visually impaired children in India. Hoverever, childhood Blindness is one of the focused area under the National Programme for Control of Blindness. Steps being taken under the Programme for prevention and control of Childhood blindness during the 10th five year plan are:- 
 

(i) to provide eye glasses to about 1.5 million children having significant refractive errors. 

(ii) To develop 50 Pediatric ophthalmology Units at tertiary level. 

(iii) To train at least 200 eye 
specialties in various sub-specialties of ophthalmology including pediatric 
Ophthalmology. 

(iv) To develop IEC for pediatric ophthalmology.
