(c) the steps Government are contemplating to address the situation?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT

(SHRI OSCAR FERNANDES)

(a) Reliable estimates of employment and unemployment are obtained through quinquennial National Sample Surveys carried out by the National Sample Survey Organisation (NSSO). Last such survey, for which results have been published, relates to the year 2004-05. As per these surveys, unemployment rate in India has marginally gone up from 2.2 percent in 1999-2000 to 2.3 percent during 2004-05.

(b) Yes, Madam. This is because of their engagement in low productivity jobs.

(c) The approach to Tenth Plan focuses on providing gainful high quality employment to the additions to the labour force and it is listed as one of the monitorable objectives for the 10th Plan and beyond. The growth strategy of 10th Plan has laid emphasis on rapid growth of those sectors, which are likely to create high quality employment opportunities and deal with the policy constraints, which discourage growth of employment. Particular attention has been paid to the policy environment influencing a wide range of economic activities, which have a large employment potential.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that National Crime Records Bureau has come out with a crime-clock; if so, the details thereof;

(b) whether the clock has indicated any frequency about various kinds of crime such as crimes against women, dowry deaths, rape, murder, riots, arson, dacoity and sexual harassment; if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether the data given by the clock tallies with the record of his Ministry/ Police; and

(d) if so, the steps taken to address the situation?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

( SHRI MANIKRAO HODLYA GAVIT )

(a) to (c): The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) has worked out `frequencies` of incidents of various crimes on the basis of the data furnished by the State Governments/U.T. Administrations, which it has depicted in the form of a `clock` in its annual report `Crime in India`. The `frequencies` indicated there are arrived at by dividing the total number of incidents of a particular crime reported in the country during the year by the total number of minutes in a year (365x24x60).

(d): `Police` and `Public Order` are State subjects under the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India and therefore, the State Governments/Union Territory Administrations are primarily responsible for prevention, detection, registration and investigation of crime and for prosecuting the criminals through the machinery of their law enforcement agencies. The Ministry of Home Affairs, however, supplements the efforts of the State Governments by providing them financial assistance for modernization of their Police Forces in terms of weaponry, communication, equipment, mobility, training and other infrastructure under the Scheme of Modernization of State Police Forces. Further, intelligence inputs are regularly shared by the Central Security and Intelligence Agencies with the State Law Enforcement Agencies to prevent crime and law and order related incidents. Advisories are also issued to the State Governments/Union Territory Administrations from time to time to ensure proper maintenance of law and order.

records.qtitle: ST STATUS TO KOL TRIBE PEOPLE .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that people belonging to Kol tribe have been given the status of a tribe in the States of Orissa, Chhattisgarh, Uttaranchal, Jharkhand, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh; and

(b) if so, the reasons that such recognition has not been given in Uttar Pradesh ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI P. R. KYNDIAH)


(a) & (b): Kol Tribe has been notified as Scheduled Tribe in the States of Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Orissa only.
The list of Scheduled Tribes in relation to a State or Union Territory is notified under the provisions of Article 342 of the Constitution of India. Accordingly, the list of notified Scheduled Tribes is State / Union Territory specific. Before any community can be considered for inclusion in the Scheduled Tribes list of any State / UT it must fulfill the criteria adopted by Government of India for identification of a community i.e.:
(i) Indications of primitive traits,
(ii) Distinctive culture,
(iii) Geographical isolation,
(iv) Shyness of contact with the community at large and
(v) Social and economic backwardness
The Government on 15-6-1999 has approved the modalities for determining the claims for inclusion in, exclusion from and other modifications in the list of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. According to these modalities only those proposals, which have been recommended by the concerned State Government and the Registrar General of India as well as the National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (now the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes) are to be considered and legislation amended.
The proposal for inclusion of Kol community in other States including Uttar Pradesh have been processed as per approved modalities.

(a): 2011 MW grid interactive renewable power generation installed capacity has been set up during 2005-06 through renewable energy sources, which is estimated to have fed 14 billion units of electricity to the grid.

(b): 3377 MW grid interactive power generation installed capacity has been added during the last two years, i.e., 2004-05 and 2005-06 through renewable energy sources.

(c): Apart from supplementing grid-interactive power generation, renewable energy supplements energy needs of cooking, heating, lighting and motive power throughout the country.

(d): To promote renewable energy generation in the country fiscal and financial incentives are being provided that include capital / interest subsidy, accelerated depreciation, and relief from taxes. These apart, preferential tariff for grid interactive power is being given in most potential states. Publicity and awareness on the use of renewable energy systems / devices are also being created through print, postal and electronic media and special events like the Rajiv Gandhi Akshay Urja Diwas, which are being organised. District-level Advisory Committees have been also constituted in states to facilitate effective coordination of renewable energy schemes / programmes.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION

(SHRI TASLIMUDDIN)

(a) to (c): The Super Bazar Dalit Karamchari Sangh has filed Special Leave Petition No.8398/2005 in the Supreme Court challenging the order of winding up of Super Bazar. The Supreme Court in its Order dated 28.2.2006, inter alia, observed that professional management of the Super Bazar is absolutely essential. With a view to explore the possibility of having an arrangement under which the management of the Super Bazar may be entrusted to a body of professionals, the Supreme Court constituted a Committee of Officials to consider all aspects of the matter. The Committee submitted its report on 29.3.2006 in the Supreme Court of India. On 5.5.2006, the Supreme Court directed the Committee to issue an advertisement in two National dailies for inviting bids to start Super Bazar afresh. In compliance of this Order, a notice was published on 19.05.2006 in two National daily newspapers. M/s. Reliance Industries Ltd. and Indian Labour Cooperative Society along with Indian Potash Ltd. had submitted their bids. These bids were opened by the Committee on 8.6.2006. The bids were evaluated by the Committee and a Report was submitted in the Supreme Court on 4.7.2006. The next date of hearing of the case fixed by the Supreme Court is 12.12.2006. Therefore, the matter is sub-judice.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Broadband scheme offered by MTNL is drawing poor responses as compared to similar schemes offered by other service providers like AirTel; if so, the reasons therefor;

(b) whether it is also fact that the scheme offered by MTNL is costlier to consumer and suffers from poor technology and gives poor performance in wet and cloudy season and does not even ensure customer satisfaction; and

(c) the steps Government are taking to improve technology and cost to the consumer?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY

(DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD)

(a) No, Sir. The broadband scheme offered by MTNL is very popular. The scheme was announced in January, 2005 and as on 31-10-2006, about 3.44 lakh lines are already working. MTNL is adding nearly 1000 customer per day on its broadband network. Seeing the growing demand, MTNL is procurring another 8 lakh lines on broadband equipments in the current year 2006-07.

(b) No, Sir. MTNL has got nearly 15 tariff plans for broadband customers to suite individual`s requirement. The technology used is Asymmetrical Digital Subscriber Line

(ADSL) 2+ on landline, which is the state-of-the-art technology. The service can be affected due to cable fault during monsoon but all efforts are made to rectify such faults on war footing.

(c) The following steps have been taken to improve technology and cost to the customers:
Improving its landline network by replacing paper core cable, rehabilitating the outdoor plants, decreasing loop length etc. Revision of tariff from time to time to make them customer friendly for all segments of society. It has been planned to introduce Worldwide Inter-Operatibility for Microwave Access

(WIMAX) equipments, which is a wireless system for providing broadband service to the customer in remote areas as well as 3G mobile networks.

records.qtitle: AGRAHAYANA SAKA SECURITY OF ELDERLY PEOPLE IN METRO CITIES .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that slack policing in the Capital continues to put elders at risk;

(b) whether it is a fact that incidents of crime against senior citizens witnessed a spurt over the past few months in Delhi and Mumbai, as compared to the rest of metro cities, if so, the reasons therefor; and

(c) the steps Government have taken to strengthen the programmes of police for senior citizens in all the Metros?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI S. REGUPATHY)

(a): No Sir.

(b): Information is being collected and will be laid on the Table of the House.

(c): `Police` and `public order` being the State subjects, it is the responsibility of the State Government to take steps for prevention of crimes, including those against senior citizens. However, the Government of India has issued advisory to the State Governments/UT Administrations to take measures for the safety and welfare of senior citizens. Instructions have also been issued to ensure sensitization of police officers during their training programme towards problem of older persons.
The steps taken by Delhi Police for safety and security of senior citizens include introduction of a special helpline No. 1291 to attend to distress calls pertaining to senior citizens; setting up of Senior Citizen`s Cell which functions round-the-clock; sensitising senior citizens about the importance of using safety gadgets in house with the help of Non-Government Organisations; multi-tasking Police Control Room Vans; effective supervision by senior officers by moving around in the field more often; and verification of domestic helps, drivers, chowkidars etc.
The steps taken by Mumbai Police for strengthening the programmes of Police for safety and protection of senior citizens include sensitization of beat officers/staff of all the police stations in Mumbai about the danger of attacks on elderly persons; issuing instructions to them to visit the residences of elderly persons to discuss and solve their problems; and holding meetings of elderly persons and police staff periodically at every police station.
Kolkata Police has introduced `Senior Citizens Help Line` having No. 9830088884 for the help of the senior citizens which is available round the clock at the Control Room to guide them in distress.
The steps taken by the Chennai Police for the safety of elderly people include speedy grievance redressal by the senior officers; counseling the elders by police personnel against depression; giving priority to the elders` complaints over the family dispute; and watching the administration of old age homes etc.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan

(b) whether the same has been inducted; and

(c) if not, the reasons therefor and the purpose for which the technology was developed, if it was not to be utilized? ANSWER (SHRI A.K. ANTONY)

MINISTER OF DEFENCE

records.qtitle: SERVICE TAX ON USER CHARGES FOR USE OF PUBLIC AMENITIES. .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government have decided not to levy Service Tax on the user charges for the use of public amenities;

(b) if so, the details of the facilities/services that are covered by the definition of amenities; and

(c) whether the hospital services, school education facilities and insurance etc., are covered by the definition of amenities, if not, how do Government define amenities?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM)

(a), (b) and (c): Taxable services are specified under section 65 (105) of the Finance Act, 1994. Public amenities are not specified under the above section. Use of hospital services and educational services are also not specified taxable services under section 65(105).
Service provided by an insurer, carrying on general insurance business, to a policy holder in relation to general insurance business is leviable to service tax under section 65(105)

(d). Service tax is leviable on the gross amount charged by the insurer.
Service provided by an insurer, carrying on life insurance business, to a policy holder in relation to the risk cover in life insurance is leviable to service tax under section 65(105)(zx). Service tax is leviable on the gross amount charged by the insurer for the risk cover in life insurance. However, an insurer has the option to pay one percent of the gross amount of premium charged as service tax.

records.qtitle: DELAYED CREDITING OF CHEQUES BY BANKS .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that by delaying the clearance of cheques of customers banks earned Rs. 3276 crores in the year, 2005-06;

(b) whether it is also a fact that the enrichment had been on 13000 lakh cheque worth Rs.11,33,7000 crores as estimated by the India Statistical Institute and the RBI`s Department of Statistical Analysis and Commuter Services; and

records.ans_text:
THE MINISTEROF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI PAWAN KUMAR BANSAL)

(a) & (b): RBI does not have any such instances on record that any bank has made huge earnings in cheque clearing and deliberately delaying the credit. If any specific instances of violation of RBI`s guidelines are noticed, it takes appropriate regulatory action.

(c) i Does not arise. However, any customer aggrieved by delay in clearance of cheques can move the concerned Banking Ombudsman for redressal of his grievance.

records.qtitle: CARE OF ORPHANED BOYS AND GIRLS .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Care Homes and Orphanages keep children upto the age of 18 only;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor;

(c) whether it is a fact that by the time the orphan boys and girls reach the age of 18 they do not complete education enough to enable them to get employment due to factors such as ban on under age employment etc.; and

(d) if so, whether Government propose to provide for retention of orphans for some more years, if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI RENUKA CHOWDHURY)


(a),(b),(c)&(d) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PART (a),(b),(c)&(d) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 174 FOR 4.12.2006 BY SHRIMATI JAYA BACHCHAN REGARDING CARE OF ORPHANED BOYS AND GIRLS


(a)&(b) As per Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000, a child is defined as a person who has not completed 18 years of age. Accordingly, the children homes which may be established and maintained by the State Governments/UT Administrations under the Act, either by themselves, or in association with the voluntary organizations, for children in need of care and protection keep these children upto the age of 18 years.

(c) The Children Homes are supposed to be functioning as comprehensive child care centres and are expected to provide facilities which include education to all children according to their age and ability, either inside the home or outside. The children homes are also required to facilitate vocational training to children under the guidance of trained instructors.
The ban on employment under the Child Labour [Prohibition and Regulation] Act, 1986 as well as the National Child Labour Project [NCLP] scheme being implemented by the Ministry of Labour and Employment is with the intention of providing better scope for education to these children. There may, however, be children who have not completed education at the age of 18 years.

(d) Section 44 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000 provides for establishment of recognition of After Care Organizations for children between the age of 17 to 18 years who may stay in these organizations till the age of 20 years. These organizations are expected to enable the children to prepare themselves for an honest, industrious and useful life after they leave children homes. Government of India has been impressing upon the State Governments the need for full implementation of the Act.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan

records.qtitle: REVIEW OF FUNCTIONING OF COMMODITY EXCHANGES .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) the number of commodity exchanges and multi-commodity exchanges that are in existence and functioning at present;

(b) what is the number of notified commodities being traded by them;

(c) whether it is a fact that these exchanges are instrumental for turning many businessman as paupers because of the futures trading and have also resulted in the unjustified increase in the price of pulses; and

(d) if so, whether Government propose to review their functioning, if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI PAWAN KUMAR BANSAL)

(a) There are 24 Commodity Exchanges, which are recognized for commodity futures trading. At present, 22 Exchanges are functioning, and out of these, 18 Exchanges are multi-commodity Exchanges.

(b) At present, there are 103 commodities notified for commodity futures trading, and out of these, active trading is taking place in 92 commodities.

(c) & (d): No Sir. The commodity futures market performs important functions of price discovery and price risk management. Forward Market Commission (FMC), the Regulator for commodity futures market, set up under the provisions of the Forward Contracts

(Regulation) Act, 1952, has laid down various regulatory measures for ensuring the orderly functioning of the commodity Exchanges. These regulatory measures ensure that the prices of futures contracts traded at the Exchanges reflect demand and supply situation of a particular commodity and that the Exchanges efficiently perform the function of price discovery, which benefits all the stakeholders, including the farmer. FMC is also keeping a close watch on the developments in the commodity futures market on a continuous basis.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) the action taken under chapter 8 of the Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities protection of Rights and full Participation) Act, 1995 for installation of audio signals at red lights in the public roads, creating curb cuts and slopes in pavements for easy access of wheelchair users and engraving the surface of Zebra crossing for the blind and those with low vision and similar infrastructure at ATMs etc;

(b) whether civic agencies work in reverse order and create obstacles for these persons by raising the height of footpath and central verge on the roads disproportionately; and

(c) if so, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT

(SMT. SUBBULAKSHMI JAGADEESAN)

(a) to (c) The Persons with Disabilities Act, 1995stipulates that the appropriate Government and the local authorities shall within the limits of their economic capacity and development provide for installation of auditory signals at red lights and engraving on the surface of the zebra crossing on the public roads for the benefit of persons with visual impairment & causing curb cuts and slopes to be made in pavements for the easy access to wheel chairs users. The term `appropriate governments`, has been defined in Section 2(a) of the Act to include the Central Government as well as State Governments and the local authorities. Implementation of the provision relating to barrier free access for persons with disabilities on public roads comes under the purview of the State Governments/U.T. Administrations and local authorities. The Government of India have issued instructions to all the executing agencies to make necessary arrangements for adopting barrier free features on the roads constructed/maintained by them.

records.name: Motilal Vora
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware of the fact that barrage being constructed at Sutlej in Baraj Jada Valley of China and Tibet would result in acute shortage of availability of water in India and availability of water for North India would come under control of China;

(b) whether there is any treaty or mutual understanding between India and China under which China should have taken prior consent of the Government of India;

(c) whether it is also a fact that heavy destruction were caused in Sutlej and Spiti valley of Himachal Pradesh due to breach caused in an artificial lake created at Parichhu river in Tibet itself last year;

(d) if so, whether Government have lodged its protest to Government of China in this regard; and

(e) to what extent India is capable of safeguarding its borders or it would again be occupied by China as in the past?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI E. AHAMED)


(a) Government have noted that the spokesperson of the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs, in response to a report in an Indian newspaper about China building a barrage on the River Sutlej in Tibet, has reportedly stated as follows: “In recent years, the Chinese side has constructed a small-scale hydropower station on the Langqinzangbu (Sutlej River) at Zhada County in the Tibet Autonomous Region, to satisfy the daily electricity needs of local population. Chinese Government has always adhered to the basic principle of fair and reasonable development and utilization of trans-boundary rivers. During this process of development and utilization, Chinese Government fully considers the impact on lower reaches. The Ministries of Water Resources of China and India have always maintained good cooperation. In 2005, both sides signed the Memorandum of Understanding on provision of hydrological information during the flood season on the Langqinzangbu/ Sutlej River by the Chinese side to the Indian side. This has played a positive role in flood-control safety in downstream areas”.


(b) No.


(c)&(d) In the wake of the creation of a landslide dam and barrier lake on the River Parechu in Tibet last year, Government took up the matter in a proactive manner with the Chinese side through diplomatic channels as well as through the border personnel meetings to deal with the situation. Inter-Ministerial teams were also sent to China to hold discussions with the Chinese side to mitigate the crisis. During the visit of the Chinese Premier to India in April 2005, in response to concerns expressed by the Indian side, the Chinese side agreed to take measures for controlled release of accumulated water of the landslide dam on the River Parechu, as soon as conditions permitted. Following the flash floods in the River Sutlej in June 2005, which led to loss of property in downstream areas, Government asked the Chinese side to confirm the status of the landslide dam on the River Parechu, which was suspected to have collapsed and caused the flash flood. The Chinese side confirmed that the base structure of the landslide dam had been washed away and that with the discharge of accumulated water behind the landslide dam, the artificial lake on the River Parechu no longer posed any threat to the downstream areas.

(e) Government remain vigilant in monitoring the security situation in India’s periphery and are taking all necessary steps to safeguard the security and territorial integrity of India.

records.qtitle: QUALITY OF WATER IN GANGA AT ALLAHABAD .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) what is, at present, the quality of water in Ganga and at the confluence of three rivers at Allahabad;

(b) whether any steps have been taken to monitor the quality of water regularly; and

(c) the steps Government have taken to provide clean and hygienic water to tourists who would visit Allahabad in December this year at the time of Kumbh Mela?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS

(SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA)

(a)& (b) The water quality of river Ganga is being monitored once a month by Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) through Uttar Pradesh Pollution Control Board (UPPCB) under its ongoing programme of ‘Monitoring of Indian National Aquatic Resources (MINARS)’. The Ministry of Environment & Forests is also monitoring the water quality of river Ganga for evaluating the impact of implementation of Ganga Action Plan on river water quality.
The monitoring data under Ganga Action Plan from Rishikesh (Uttranchal) to Uluberia (West Bengal) reveals that the water quality of river Ganga during the summer of 2006, is not meeting the desired bathing class standard in the stretch from Kannauj downstream to Allahabad upstream in respect of bio-chemical oxygen demand (BOD), an indicator for organic pollution. The levels of dissolved oxygen (DO) however, are found to meet the standard throughout the river length. The BOD values at the bathing ghat at Sangam and Allahabad downstream are 3.7 and 3.2 milligram per liter respectively as against the desired standard of 3.0 milligram per liter.

(c) Under the Ganga Action Plan at Allahabad, a sewage treatment capacity of 60 million liters per day has been created during Phase-I and a treatment capacity of 29 million liters per day is envisaged in Phase-II. As per the report of Uttar Pradesh Pollution Control Board, all industrial units at Allahabad have installed effluent treatment plants which are operating satisfactorily. During the Kumbh Mela, the Uttar Pradesh Pollution Control Board can issue directions under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 and the Water (Prevention & Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 to the industrial units and local bodies in case of non-compliance. Also, as per the direction of the Hon’ble Allahabad High Court, the State Irrigation Department has been asked to maintain sufficient water release from Narora Dam during this period.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan

(b) whether the Bill seeks to do away with the monopolies, impose ceilings on TV network and similar restrictions on cable and other service providers; and

(c) whether these provisions seek to control the content of the programming and its anti-monopoly measures could also entail restructuring of their share holding patterns?

THE MINISTER OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING AND PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS (SHRI P. R. DASMUNSI)

(a), (b) & (c): The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting is considering a proposed Broadcasting Services Regulation Bill in consultation with Ministries concerned. records.qtitle: MONEY WASTED FOR IMAGE BUILDING BY CIL .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Coal India Ltd. has been burning public money on an image making exercise;

(b) whether it is also a fact that it has been giving largesse to a private club in Kolkata and has also spent Rs. l0 lacs on a PR exercise; and

(c) the action Government have taken to curb the expenditure?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COAL

(DR. DASARI NARAYANA RAO)

(a) No, Sir. CIL spends only a miniscule part of its overall profit on publicity as a part of an overall corporate strategy.

(b) CIL has not been giving any amount to any private club on continuous basis. However, it made a one time contribution of Rs.10 lacs to Kolkata club as a cosponsor of an event known as `International Evening` organized by them. As reported by CIL part of the funds raised on the occasion were to be reserved for the betterment of the weaker sections of society and to be contributed to the Governor`s or Chief Minister`s Relief Fund.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) the power theft and distribution losses at present and the last two years in the country, State-wise and year-wise; and

(b) whether the burden of power theft as well as distribution losses is passed on to the consumers throughout the country; if not, the reasons that this burden is passed on to the consumers by private power companies in Delhi?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER

( SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE )


(a) : As reported by Central Electricity Authority (CEA), the details of Transmission and Distribution (T&D) losses which include theft of power also of various States during the years 2002-2003, 2003-04 and 2004-05 are at Annexure.

records.qtitle: INFRASTRUCTURE IN DELHI FOR COMMON WEALTH GAMES
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) the present state of preparedness in the Capital for the Commonwealth Games, 2010;

(b) whether it is a fact that choked drains in the Capital, long power cuts, congested and pot-holed roads with MCD and DDA being indifferent to them, water shortage generally, the creaking city infrastructure present a very bad picture;

(c) whether it is a fact that Prime Minister`s Office has also recently expressed its concern on this state of affairs; and

(d) the action that has been taken to address the situation?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT

( SHRI AJAY MAKEN )

(a)&(b): The various agencies concerned have prepared their action plans for the Commonwealth Games, 2010 including construction of Games Village, upgradation of Stadia and civic infrastructure. The Government of NCT of Delhi has informed that an Integrated Action Plan has been prepared and a Core Group of officers has been constituted to oversee the progress. The Action Plan includes construction of 1 million gallons per day (mgd) Water Treatment Plant and 1 mgd Sewerage Treatment Plant at the Commonwealth Games Village, upgradation of water supply and sewerage system at all the Games venues, construction of link road from Games Village to Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium, construction of flyovers, renovation and development of ISBTs, deployment of High Capacity Buses, extension of Metro Services and setting up of dedicated power supply stations. The various projects are at different stages of planning and preparation of estimates.
Regarding maintenance of drains and roads, Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) has informed that 1296 drains were desilted before the on set of monsoon and regular efforts are made to attend the pot holes in the road from time to time.

(c)&(d): In a meeting taken by the Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister on 5th July, 2006 a reference was made about the mechanism of coordination between various civic and construction agencies throughout the city resulting in problems of poor drainage and sanitation. It was desired at the meeting that appropriate action may be taken by the concerned agencies to avoid such problems in future.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware that Beijing–Lhasa train started running in early July, 2006;

(b) whether Government have examined the security implications arising out of operation of this train; and

(c) if so, the results thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan

THE MINISTER OF POWER

( SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE )

(a) & (b) : The overall power supply position the National Capital has improved over the years and the energy and peak shortage reduced from 1.9% and 9.2% at the beginning of the 10th Plan (2002-03) to 1.5% and 3.3% respectively in the year 2005-06. However, there have been instances of increased power shortage during certain periods in peak summer and peak winter when the demand for power increases significantly and /or availability of power gets reduced due to higher forced outage of generating units, reduced hydro availability, etc.

(c) & (d) : According to Government of NCT of Delhi Privatization of distribution sector in Delhi has shown very encouraging results. Aggregate technical and commercial (AT&C) loss reduction in first four years has been around 12 % and the distribution companies are committed to reduce losses around 17 % during the first five year period. Other parameters have also shown very encouraging trend such as response time to attend faults, etc.

(e) & (f) : No Sir, tariff for all category of consumers is determined by Delhi Electricity Regulatory Commission Under Section 62 of the Electricity Act, 2003 after examining ARR petitions submitted by Discoms, Delhi Transco Limited, Indraprashtha Generation Company Limited & Pragati Power Company Limited. According to Government of NCT of Delhi, Special Courts as per Electricity Act, 2003 have been established to expeditiously dispose the cases related to the theft of electricity.

records.qtitle: PHALGUNA SAKA CRACKS IN SUN TEMPLE AT KONARK .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a)whether it is a fact that the 12th Century Sun Temple at Konark, Orissa has developed cracks;

(b)if so, the reasons for such happening and details in this regard; and

(c)the action taken to restore/repair the Temple?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER FOR TOURISM AND CULTURE

(SMT. AMBIKA SONI)


(a) to (c) A statement is laid on the table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PART (a) TO (c) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 336 FOR 14.3.2006 REGARDING “ CRACKS IN SUN TEMPLE AT KONARK

(a) &(b)Due to inherent porous nature of the Kondalite rock used for the construction of the temple, distress is noticed at the lower most row of the Superstructure (Jagmohan) at the south-east side. The iron dowels provided to bind the architectural members have deteriorated and oxidization has resulted in cracks on the edges of the members. The exterior surface of the temple is also exposed to constant saline action due to salt laden winds from the sea which is another cause of deterioration.

(c)Steps are being taken to arrest the deterioration of exterior surface of the monument. These include removal of salt by paper pulp treatment, fungicidal treatment to contain micro-vegetational growth, consolidation of weathered stones and water repellent treatment, besides routine maintenance.
The cantilever members of the Super structure (Jagmohan) are supported with tubular scaffolding and stainless steel pins are used to consolidate the architectural members. ASI is also consulting the Central Building Research Institute for expert guidance.

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS.(SHRI SURESH PACHOURI)

(a): The Right to Information Act, 2005 has come into force only on 12th October 2005. It is too early to review the working of the Act.

(b) & (c): The Central Information Commission in its decision No. CIC/C/2006, dated 16/1/2006 had held that a public authority is not precluded from prescribing standard format for the purpose of making the application for ease of reference and response. However, this decision was reviewed by the Commission on 08/02/2006, when it was held that it is incumbent upon any public authority prescribing a format that it remains simple and comprehensible as well as accessible to common folk. The Commission has further clarified that applications for information on plain paper are also to be received and replied within the prescribed time limit.

(a): The Commissioner of Police, Delhi, made a presentation on 5th January, 2006 before the media about the work done by Delhi Police during the year, 2005. Some of the salient features of the presentation are indicated below:- 



i) There was increase  of 4.57% in  registration of IPC Crime and 3.35% 
in registration of heinous crime.
ii) There was decrease in crime under the 
Crime Heads of dacoity, murder, attempt to murder, riot and theft.
iii) 
Working out of IPC cases increased from 61.84% in 2004 to 67.54%  in 2005.

iv) Working out of heinous crime increased from 86.89% in 2004 to 89.94% in 
2005. 
v) Rate of conviction  increased from 50% in 2004 to 55% in 2005. 

vi) There was 11.67%  increase in the number of persons arrested in IPC 
offences and an increase of 4.64% in detection under Local & Spl. Laws. 

vii) Analysis of rape cases shows that about 97% of rapes  were committed by 
persons known to the victims. 
viii) 51  militants  belonging to various 
organizations were arrested which was the highest number in any single year.

ix) Progress was made in modernization of police force, traffic management and 
providing security to senior citizens.



(b):	Due to scientific investigation and better police follow up during 
trial of cases, about 55% conviction rate  has been achieved.  The detection 
rate has been 67%.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government’s attention has been drawn to a new survey published in London in the first half of January, 2006 by Lancet magazine stating inter-alia that 5 million baby girls have been murdered in the country every year since 1994; and

(b) if so, Government’s reaction thereto?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI RENUKA CHOWDHURY)

(a) As per information furnished by Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, a study on Low male-to-female sex ratio of children born in India, national survey of 1:1 million households was conducted by Lancet. The interpretation of the study states that based on conservative assumptions, pre-natal sex determination practice accounts for about 0.5 million missing female births yearly.

(b) Ministry of Health & Family Welfare has undertaken training of trainers from State Judicial Academies to train lower judiciary and public prosecutors with the objective to sensitize the judiciary on the issue. National Inspection and Monitoring Committee (NIMC) having representatives of Department of Women & Child Development, National Commission for Women, Indian Council for Medical Research as members, undertakes periodical visits to the districts with low child sex ratio (0-6 years) to oversee the implementation of the Act at ground level and monitors the prosecutions launched against unregistered bodies and bodies violating provisions of the Act/Rules and directions of the Supreme Court of India in the matter. The National Support and Monitoring Cell has been constituted as a mechanism to help Appropriate Authorities in apprehending actual wrong doer who are committing female foeticide/abetting female foeticide.
It is, nevertheless, recognized that mere legislation is not enough to deal with this problem that has roots in social behavior and prejudices. A number of activities to create awareness on the issue are being undertaken. The initiatives include meeting with the organizations working against sex selection, involvement of the medical professionals, religious leaders to spread the message, requesting police training academies and schools to include the issues in curriculum of their training, telecasting of PNDT spots on private satellite channels and Doordarshan, and involvement of elected representatives etc. A ‘Save the girl Child’ Campaign with a view to lesson son preference by highlighting achievements of young girls has been launched. District Magistrates have also been requested to regularly review the implementation of the PC&PNDT Act alongwith other programmes in their district.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is. a fact that more than 34 lakh eases were pending in various courts by the middle of 2004;

(b) if so, the current figures in this regard; and

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF LAW AND JUSTICE

(SHRI K: VENKATAPATHY)

(a) Yes, Madam.

(b) At present there are 33,635 cases in Supreme: Court, 33,41,040 cases in High Courts and 2,53,06,458 cases in Subordinate Courts reported to be pending.

(e) Time bound disposal of eases is within the exclusive domain of judiciary. However, in order to reduce pendency of eases Government has initiated a number of measures which include, timely filling the vacancies of judges, increasing the judge strength, grouping of cases, involving common question of law, constitution of specialized benches, organizing Lok Adalats at regular intervals encouraging alternative modes of dispute resolution like negotiation, mediation and arbitration, and setting up of special tribunals like Central Administrative Tribunals, State Administrative Tribunals, Income Tax Appellate Tribunals, Family Courts and Labour courts. The Government has extended the term of existing 1562 Fast Track Courts for another five years i.e. upto 31.3.2010 for clearing huge pendency of cases at District level.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that we are on the verge of losing our wetlands in the country like Europe which lost 80 per cent of its wetland in the last century ;

(b) if not, what are the details of the ongoing wetland projects receiving attention of Government for their preservation; and

(c) what are the details of the wetland projects being preserved under Ramsar Convention to which India is a signatory?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS

(SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA)

(a) No, Sir. However the wetlands in the country are facing threats due to biotic factors like over-exploitation, encroachments, siltation and discharge of industrial effluents as also abiotic factors.

(b) The Ministry of Environment & Forests implements a scheme on Conservation & Management of Wetlands under which 71 wetlands covering 22 States of the country have been identified for undertaking conservation activities to check further degradation. Assistance on 100% grant basis is given for activities like survey & demarcation, protection, siltation control, pollution abatement catchment area treatment, de-weeding, biodiversity conservation, supplementary and alternate livelihood support for people dependent on wetlands, community participation and education & awareness. An amount of Rs. 43.16 crores has been released from 1987-88 to 2005-06 for conservation and management of identified wetlands in the country for various conservation activities.

(c) So far, 25 sites have been identified from India as Ramrasr sites under Ramsar convention which include: Ashtamudi, Sasthamkotta & Vembanad-Kol ( Kerala) Chilika Lake & Bhitarkanika Mangroves ( Orissa) , Bhoj Wetland (M.P.), Deepor Beel ( Assam) Harike, Kanjli & Ropar ( Punjab), East Calcutta Wetlands ( W.B.), Keoladeo National Park & Sambhar Lake ( Rajasthan) , Kolleru Lake ( A.P.), Loktak Lake ( Manipur), Point Calimere (T.N.), Pong Dam Lake, Chandratal & Renuka ( H.P.), Tsomorari, Wular, Surinsar - Mansar, Hokarsar (J&K), Rudrasagar (Tripura) and Uppar Ganga (U.P.).

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) Whether it is a fact that a pilot nation by nation study of environmental performance named 2006 Environmental Performance Index shows inter-alia that India ranks amongst the 20 lowest scoring countries in the critical environmental goals ranging from clean drinking water, low ozone levels to sustainable fisheries and low greenhouse gas emissions;

(b) Is so, what are the details thereof and the reasons therefor; and

(c) What steps Government propose to take to improve its rankings?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS

(SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA)

(a) Yes Sir.

(b ) The Pilot 2006 Environmental Performance Index has been developed by the Center for Environmental Law & Policy at Yale University and the Center for International Earth Science Information Network (CIESIN) at Columbia University in collaboration with the World Economic Forum and the Joint Research Centre of the European Commission. Using 16 indicators, six core policy categories and the two broad objectives of Environmental Health and Eco-system Vitality, the Environmental Performance Index Framework has ranked India 118 out of a total of 133 countries.
The position of the countries at the bottom of the rankings has been attributed by the authors to several factors such as low Environmental Health scores, densely populated industrializing countries with stressed ecosystems, arid states with limited natural resource endowments, lack of capacity for aggressive pollution control or systematic natural resource management.

(c) The Government of India accords high priority to environment protection and sustainable development. These concerns are duly reflected in our planning process. The Government of India has already taken a series of steps, including establishment of a regulatory framework to address these concerns.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have drawn up a plan for production of Hydrogen energy;

(b) if so, the details in this regard; and

(c) the areas where the Hydrogen energy would be put to use?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF NON-CONVENTIONAL ENERGY SOURCES (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) (SHRI VILAS MUTTEMWAR)


(a), (b)& (c): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT
Statement referred to in the Reply to Parts (a), (b) & (c) of Rajya Sabha Starred Question No. 82 for 23.02.2006 on Production of Hydrogen Energy

(a), (b) & (c): A National Hydrogen Energy Road Map up to 2020 has been recently prepared by a Steering Group on Hydrogen Energy set up by the National Hydrogen Energy Board which has been constituted by the Ministry of Non-Conventional Energy Sources. The Steering Group consisted of high level representatives from industry, leading scientists and technologists and eminent public figures. The Road Map has considered all components of the Hydrogen Energy System, that is, production, storage, transport and delivery, applications and safety aspects. It includes production of hydrogen from indigenous sources such as coal, nuclear and renewable energy including solar, wind, biomass, micro-hydro and biological routes.
Hydrogen energy would be mainly used for transport and power generation applications. The Road Map has projected that one million hydrogen fueled vehicles will be on Indian Roads and 1000 MW hydrogen based aggregate power generation capacity will be set up in the country, by 2020.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that in order to have access to nuclear technology India has an agreement with USA;

(b) whether it is also a fact that the agreement entails splitting of the country`s civilian and military nuclear facilities and place its civilian reactors under the global scanner;

(c) whether it amounts to a compromise with our policy of non-alignment as envisaged by the first Prime Minister of the country; and

(d) if so, what were the compulsions before the Government for abandoning the path of non-alignment?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(ANAND SHARMA)


(a) India and US reached an understanding on cooperation in civil nuclear energy on 18 July 2005 during the visit of Prime Minister to US in the context of India`s quest for energy security as an essential component of our vision of our development.

(b) Under the terms of this understanding, India will be identifying and separating its civilian and military nuclear facilities and programs in a phased manner and filing a declaration regarding its civilians facilities with the International Atomic Energy Agency

(IAEA) and would place voluntarily its civilian nuclear facilities under IAEA safeguards.

(c) The understanding on cooperation in civil nuclear energy in no way compromises India`s traditional non-alignment policy that mandates decisions to be taken on the basis of our national interests and national security considerations only.

(d) Does not arise.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:

(b) if so, what is the number of MiG 21 planes that have crashed so far; and

(c) whether Government propose to review their continuance for Defence purposes?
records.ans_text:

(SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE)


(a) Due to a spate of accidents in 2002-2003, the term ‘Flying Coffin’ was coined by a section of the media.

(b) Out of a total number of seven hundred and ninety three (793) MiG-21 aircraft which have been inducted in the Indian Air Force (IAF) since 1963, the IAF has lost three hundred and thirty (330) MiG-21 aircraft in the accidents.

(c) the earlier versions of the MiG-21 aircraft (e.g. Type-77, Type-96 and Type-75 Bis) are in the process of being phased out. The latest version has been upgraded to MiG-21 Bison using the contemporary systems and is likely to continue in the service till 2020.

records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have come across any fresh evidence on uses/ application of neem tree, its formulations, and products made from the tree leaves etc., in more areas ; if so, the details thereof indicating the areas of current application as well as the fresh ones ;

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Supreme Court has recently lashed out at Delhi Government for not cleansing Yamuna, if so, what are the details in this regard;

(b) what action Government have since taken to clean and improve the surroundings of Yamuna;

(e) whether there is any representation to allow use of any space near Yamuna for housing or other construction activity; and

(d) whether Government have drawn any lesson from the Mumbai flood following use of land near Mithi River for construction activity?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS (NAMO NARAYAN MEENA)

(a) & (b) Hon`ble Supreme Court on 7th September, 2005 in the matter of PIL No. 724/1994 has issued directions for taking up the pollution abatement works in Yamuna in a time bound manner and that the progress in this regard be reviewed periodically by the Government of NCT of Delhi and in addition by an Apex Committee under the Hon`ble Court. In this context, the Delhi Jal Board has separately decided to appoint international consultants for a comprehensive study to find out a complete solution for pollution abatement in the river Yamuna at Delhi.
The matter was further heard on 12th December, 2005, when the Court made strong observations in the context of its earlier orders regarding timely submission of affidavits and status report of periodical reviews. The Court also directed the Commissioner, Municipal Corporation of Delhi and Chief Executive Officer, Delhi Jal Board to file their affidavits within 10 days and ensure their personal presence on the next date of hearing.

(c) Proposals for taking up various developmental activities in the flood plains of river Yamuna are received in Central Water Commission (CWC) for consideration by Yamuha Standing Committee (YSC) set up under the Chairmanship of Member, River Management, CWC. Since reclamation of the land in the flood plains of the river affect the river regime and result in raise in High Flood Level, proposals for construction of public utility structures in the flood plains are received in CWC for clearance from time to time. The proposals which may not cause significant adverse affects in the river regime and the flood levels are cleared by the YSC.

(d) According to the Central Water Commission, the main reason for recent flood in Mumbai was unprecedently high rain fall over a short period. The encroachment in the flood plains of Mithi River are reported to have accentuated the problem.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
he details of progress Government have
 made in talks with Pakistan over Kashmir in general and Siachen in particular during last six months?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI E. AHAMED)
Jammu and Kashmir is one of the issues being discussed with Pakistan within the framework of the India-Pakistan Composite Dialogue. Two rounds of dialogue have been successfully concluded and the third round is scheduled to begin in January 2006. In the course of these discussions and at various high level meetings, both sides have agreed to pursue measures to enhance interaction and cooperation across the LoC, including agreed meeting points for divided families, trade, pilgrimages and cultural interaction. The Srinagar-Muzaffarabad bus service has been operationalised, though it is temporarily suspended due to the earthquake. Both countries have also agreed to let trucks use this route to promote trade. Agreement has also been reached to start additional routes, including the Poonch-Rawalakot bus service and to finalize modalities for meeting points for divided families across LoC. These issues will be taken up again once the infrastructure damaged by the earthquake is restored. Following the earthquake, both sides agreed to open five crossing points across LoC to facilitate the movement of people and relief material from either side.
Two rounds of talks have been held with Pakistan on the issue of Siachen and both sides have agreed to continue with their discussions to resolve the issue in a peaceful manner. India`s consistent position on the Siachen issue is that authentication of the presently held positions has to be the first step before any redeployment of troops is considered.

records.qtitle: STRATEGY FOR CLEANSING RECLEANSING THE RIVERS .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have devised any fresh strategy to cleanse/recleanse the rivers of, the country in the light of the experience gained in this regard from the earlier programmes/projects; and

(b) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINIS`TRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS

(SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA)

(a) to (b) The objective of the National River Conservation Plan is to improve the water quality of the rivers through the implementation of the pollution abatement works like Interception and diversion works, Sewage treatment plants, low cost sanitation works, Electric crematoria and improved wood crematoria, River front development etc. In the light of the experience gained from these programs, Govt. has discussed fre`sh strategies with the State Governments for cleaning rivers in various fora. Among the points delibentted are: ,
o Urban local bodies/States laave the responsibility to create urban infrastructure so as to ensure that untreated sewa~,e is not discharged into rivers and lakes. o Additional resources may be generated for creation of such urban infrastructure by building into the external developmental costs, the cost of collection of sewage, its conveyance, treatment etc. wherever new urban centres are developed and such costs should be built into the price of developed land. o States may also consider exploring other means for raising resources for capital expenditure, such as, surcharge on property tax, stamp duty etc. o Urban local bodies/State Governments need to further consider innovative ways for raising revenue for meeting the ,operation and maintenance costs by adopting measures, such as,
Levying user charges Sale of sludge Generation of power froth bio-gas in sewage treatment plants Creation of facilities for tourism
o Public participation and awareness t~rogrammes to generate awareness among the public for keeping water bodies clean, need to be also conducted simultaneously during implementation of pollution abatement schemes.

records.qtitle: PROVIDING FREE COST OF ELECTRICITY TO SECTIONS OF THE COMMUNITY .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) what are the names of the States where the electricity continues to be provided free of cost to sections of the community;

(b) what is the total drain out of expenditure on this head, giving details State-wise;

(c) whether Government have given advice to these States for refraining from such a course; and

(d) the reasons that this benefit is not given to all consumers alike instead of choosing groups or sections of community which are considered vote banks by the political party in power in a State?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER

( SHRI P.M. SAYEED )

(a) &(b) : At present three States viz. Andhra Pradesh, Punjab and Tamil Nadu are giving free supply of power without any ceiling on consumption to certain categories of consumers like agriculture.
In some other States, free supply of electricity is available to certain category of consumers only upto a very limited level of consumption or connected load.
A statement indicating the States and expenditure involved on free supply of electricity as per available information is at annexure.

(c) & (d) : Under section 65 of the Electricity Act, 2003 , the State Government may grant subsidy from its budget to any class of consumers if it so desires in the tariff determined by the State Electricity Regulatory Commission.
The National Electricity Policy lays emphasis on ensuring recovery of cost of service from the consumers to make the power sector sustainable. The policy also provides that a minimum level of support may be required to consumers living below poverty line and consuming only up a specified level say 30 units/month. Tariff for such consumers should also be at least 50% of the cost of the average cost of supply.

records.qtitle: SPECIAL CELL FOR SECURING RELEASE OF POWS .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that family members of 54 soldiers believed to be in Pakistan jails since the 1965 and 1971 wars have demanded that Government set up a special cell to work on bringing them back; and

(b) the action Government have taken in the matter?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF DEFENCE

(SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE)


(a) & (b): The Government have been taking up the matter of the release of Indian Prisoners of Wars with Pakistan through diplomatic channels and during high level visits from time to time. The matter was taken up by our Prime Minister with the Pakistan Prime Minister during the latter’s visit to Delhi from November 23-24, 2004 and also during the visit of President Musharraf to India from April 16-18, 2005. However, Pakistan has never acknowledged the presence of any Indian Prisoners of Wars in its jails.
In pursuance of the efforts of locating Indian Prisoners of Wars, the Government took up the matter with Pakistan Government for sending a delegation of the families of the missing defence personnel on a visit to various jails in Pakistan to facilitate identification of Indian Prisoners of War but this has not been accepted by Pakistan. A similar delegation had visited Pakistan in September, 1983 but it was given limited access and could not locate any Indian Prisoners of War.
Various proposals including setting up of a special cell to look into the matters of Prisoners of Wars in Pakistan have been received, but would be useful only if Pakistan agrees to engage in further discussions on the issue.

records.qtitle: CHEQUE BOUNCE CASES IN I ELHI ANI MUMBAI .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) what is the number of cheque bounce cases pending :in Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai at present under the National Instruments Act;

(b) whether the huge pendency is causing considerable ,delay in the disposal of these cases; and

(c) the steps Government are contemplating m check the huge pendency?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI S.S. PALALANIMANICKAM)
a) Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 empowers the payee of the cheque to file a complaint under Section 141 of the Act against the drawer of the cheque in cases where cheques are dishonored for insufficient funds. As such it is left to the concerned parties to decide whether to approach the courts or not. The data base of Reserve Bank of India, therefore, does not generate information regarding cases pending in various courts relating to bouncing of cheques under th Negotiable Instrument Act. However, based ont he information received from Public Sector Banks, there are at present about 3024 cheque bounce cases pending in Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai;

(b)&(c): Yes, Sir. In order to reduce pendency, the Negotiable Instalments Act was amended in December, 2002 and a new Section 143, was inserted providing for summery trial of` cases under the Act. The Section also provides that every endeavour shall be made by the Court to conclude the trial within six month:! of :filing the cornplaint.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) wheher it is a fact that Sensex rose rapidly to cross 8500 mark during the last one year;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor;

(c) whether it is also a fact that spurt in Sensex is due to large scale investment by foreign investors;

(d) if so, the details thereof; and

(e) the initiative taken by Government to keep a watch on the situation and its impact on social aspects of economy`?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE FOR FINANCE

(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM)

(a): The stock markets have shown an upward trend over the last one year. On 1st December, 2004 the Sensex closed at 6227.83. It crossed 7000 to close at 7076.52 on 21st June 2005. It further rose to 7669.45 on l~t August, 2005. On 3rd October, 2005, it touched 8697.65 and closed at a new high 28th of 8994.94 on November, 2005. The closing figure for 1st December 2005 was 8944.78.

(b), (c) & (d) The movement of the index is a function of changes in investment arising out of perceptions about the economy and/or a sector or the stocks constituting the index. Besides economic factors, movement of stock indices also depends on various domestic and international events, market sentiments and corporate performance and likely economic growth in future, including the fundamentals of the economy. While there is no exact correlation between any of these factors and upward movement of the Sensex, a healthy growth in capital market is generally associated with increased investment in the economy including by foreign investors.

(e): The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), the market regulator, keeps a constant vigil on the markets. In view of recent market movements, SEBI has taken several measures as a part of its surveillance activities. These include, inter alia, shifting of several scrips to trade-to-trade segment to discourage day trading and speculation and imposition of circuit filters/price bands on several scrips. SEBI has advised stock exchanges to initiate expeditious demonstrative action wherever warranted so as to protect investors` interests and to ensure orderly functioning of the stock market. Additionally, from time to time, stock exchanges issue lists of do`s ~and dont`s for investors with regard to dealing in securities, through leading English and Hindi newspapers. SEBI also emphasizes this through its periodic investor education programmes and encourages investors to take informed decisions. According to SEBI, these initiatives have minimized untoward speculation in small stocks.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are considering a proposal to put an end to the age old system of deputation of officers to and from Government Departments, Ministries, Legislatures, Public Undertakings and with VIPs/Ministers etc.;

(b) whether it is a fact that the system promotes heart burning and is capable of lowering the productivity of officers belonging to regular establishment; and

(c) if the reply to

(a) above be in the negative, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS.(SHRI SURESH PACHOURI)

(a) & (b): No, Sir.

(c): Deputation enables Government, Public Sector Undertakings and other Organisations to obtain and benefit from the services of experienced officers, experts and professionals. Deputations also help organizations get over their manpower requirement especially when there is no feeder grade in a cadre or the strength of the feeder grade is not sufficient to sustain 100% promotion. Besides, in the case of isolated posts/posts created for temporary periods/ posts in temporary organizations, deputation is the most appropriate method of recruitment. Deputation also helps infuse fresh blood and talent into a cadre/organization. Often, the Recruitment Rules of such organizations or Government Departments provide for a complement of deputation as one of the modes of recruitment on terms which may vary from fixed term deputation to permanent absorption.
