records.qtitle: SCARCITY OF DRINKING WATER IN GUJARAT .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is acute crisis in North and Central Gujarat and several districts of Saurashtra because of scarcity for drinking water; and

(b) what steps have been taken by Government to address the situation?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI A. NARENDRA)

(a) Based on the Comprehensive Action Plan, 1999 and the subsequent coverage reported by the Government of Gujarat, out of the 30,269 rural habitations in the State, 30,233 have been fully covered with drinking water supply schemes to provide 40 litre per capita per day (lpcd), and the remaining 36 habitations partially covered to provide 10-40 lpcd drinking water supply. However, the coverage position is dynamic and due to erratic rainfalls, some parts of the State face scarcity of drinking water, particularly during summer season. Based on the detailed assessment of the rainfall and its impact on drinking water supply, Government of Gujarat has notified 626 villages in 8 talukas of Kutch, Banaskantha and Sabarkantha districts as semi-scarcity affected villages.

(b) Government of Gujarat has prepared a Master Plan for taking measures like drilling and developing additional tube-wells, rejuvenation of existing water supply schemes and supply of drinking water through tankers to tackle drinking water scarcity. Though drinking water is a State subject, the Central Government is rendering financial and technical support to the State Governments, including Government of Gujarat, under a Centrally sponsored scheme, namely Accelerated Rural Water Supply Programme

(ARWSP). Funds allocated to the Government of Gujarat under different components of ARWSP during the current year (2005-2006) are as under: - 


ARWSP (Normal)			Rs.111.86 crore
ARWSP (DDP)			Rs. 11.53 crore
ARWSP (Swajaldhara)		Rs. 16.29 crore

records.qtitle: LOSS DUE TO FLOODS IN H.P. .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that parts of Himachal Pradesh were flooded recently following increase in the level of water in the Parchoo river;

(b) if so, the extent of losses caused by these floods and the steps taken to help the State; and

(c) what is the current status of the Parchoo river?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI S. REGUPATHY)

(a): Some parts of the State of Himachal Pradesh were affected by flash floods caused due to heavy rains and breaches in the artificial lake formed by landslides on the river Parechu.

(b): In the first Memorandum submitted by the Government of Himachal Pradesh, in the wake of these flash floods in June 2005, the estimated damage was reported at approximately Rs. 610 crore. Thereafter, in the second Memorandum submitted by the State Government which covers damage caused due to heavy rains and floods in some parts of the State in July 2005, was estimated at Rs. 398 crore.
The Central Government extended timely required logistic and financial support to the State Government to meet the situation. The logistic support extended to the State by the government of India included the deployment of manpower and air support to supplement the efforts of the State Government in rescue and relief operations and also for the restoration of connectively with the affected areas.
The Government of India has released both the installments of Central share of Calamity Relief Fund (CRF) aggregating to an amount of Rs. 75.52 crore for the year 2005-06 and an ad hoc release of Rs. 100 crore from National Calamity Contingency Fund

(NCCF). An Inter Ministerial Central Team has visited the flood affected areas of the State on two occasions to asses the damage and requirement of funds for relief operations by the State Government. The report of the Central Team, for providing additional assistance, is considered as per the extant norms and laid down procedure.

(c): As per available information, the artificial lake formed due to landslides on the river Parechu has broken down and at this stage, it does not pose any major potential threat to the downstream areas of Parechu river.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the Prime Minister visited France along with Air Chief Marshal recently; and

(b) what are the details of deals/issues discussed and finalised?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF DEFENCE

(SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE)


(a) No, Sir.

(b) Air Chief Marshal SP Tyagi visited France during June, 2005. During this trip the Chief of Air Staff visited the Paris Air Show, interacted with the French Chief of Air Staff and visited their operational and training establishments. He also visited Istres Airbase (France) to witness the Indo-French Air Exercise `GARUDA-II`.

records.qtitle: SAMPLES OF DRINKING WATER SUPPLIED BY DJB .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that a large number of the samples of drinking water supplied by the Delhi Jal Board were tested in the last week of March this year in six of the City’s 12 civic zones and in some hospitals and dispensaries;

(b) whether it is a fact that at least 280 samples failed that test; and

(c) what steps have been taken by Government to fix responsibility in the matter and address the situation to save the Capital from Cholera and water borne diseases?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES

(SHRI JAI PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV)

(a) Delhi Jal Board (DJB) have informed that 36 samples were lifted by DJB from Hindu Rao Hospital, Lok Nayak Jai Prakash Hospital, I.D. Hospital Kingsway Camp, Swaroop Nagar Hospital, Swaroop Nagar, Paramanand Hospital Civil Lines, Tirathram Hospital, Maya Muni Ram Jain Hospital Pitampura, All India Institute of Medical Sciences and Dispensary Mangla Puri in the month of March 2005. Out of them 12 water samples were lifted in the last week of March 2005 & quality of all the samples was found fit.

(b) & (c) The Delhi Jal Board have also informed that they have lifted 9825 water samples from public places, individual houses, public stand posts, complainant houses etc., all over Delhi in the month of March-2005. Out of them 276 water samples were found unfit for human consumption. These were due to leakages in individual service connections, use of online boosters during non supply hours, surcharging of sewer etc. The same were attended to on priority. DJB have informed that such local contaminations are a possibility, considering the total pipe network of more than 9000 km. and there is no individual responsible for the above. Further, as informed, there had been no epidemical problems like cholera etc. in Delhi due to the water supplied by DJB.

records.qtitle: REPAIR OF BRIDGE ON PILGRIMS YATRA ROUTE TO AMARNATH .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that bridge on yatra route of the holy Amarnath cave in the Pahalgam area of Anantnag district in South Kashmir was blown up by militants;

(b) whether the same has since been repaired/reconstructed to facilitate pilgrims` yatra; and

(c) if not, by when it is likely to be reconstructed? NSWER
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

( SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL )

(a) to (c): As per the available reports, on May 24, 2005, an Improvised Explosive Device(IED) blast took place under the bridge at Sadoopadaw, Police Station Pahalgam, Anantnag (Jammu and Kashmir) and due to this blast an iron bridge on Lidder river got damaged. The bridge was, however, repaired within seven days.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are considering a proposal to reduce prices of life saving drugs and pain killers; and

(b) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS & MINISTER OF STEEL( SHRI RAM VILAS PASWAN )

(a) to (b): The Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 1995 (DPCO,95) does not make any distinction between Life Saving drugs and other drugs. There is no specific norms or guidelines to determine as to which drugs can be classified as life saving drugs. Every drug, in general, is considered useful in saving and prolonging of life.
Presently 74 bulk drugs specified in the First Schedule of the Drugs

(Prices Control) Order, 1995 (DPCO, 95) and the formulations based thereon are under price control and their prices are fixed/revised by the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) in accordance with the provisions of the DPCO, 95. These drugs have been identified for inclusion under price control in the DPCO, 95 on the basis of criteria mentioned in the ‘Modifications in Drug Policy, 1986’, announced in September, 1994. These criteria take into account the extent of usage and the market competition in various drugs.
Prices of non-Scheduled formulations are fixed by the manufacturers themselves keeping in view the various factors like cost of production, marketing/selling expenses, R&D expenses, trade commission, market competition, product innovation, product quality etc. Due to these factors there is a wide variation between the production cost and selling price of these medicines. The Government takes corrective measures where the public interest is found to be adversely affected.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether computerization in Postal Department has increased the paper work instead of reducing it and added to the possibilities of frauds and embezzlement in the absence of security precautions; and ;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor and the steps taken to address the situation?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY

(DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD)

(a) & (b) No, Sir. The computerization in the Department of Posts has helped in reduction of paper work. The application softwares, currently in use in post offices, have several in-built security features and they are constantly improved upon. Detailed security instructions to be followed in computerized Post Offices have also been issued to guard against fraud and embezzlement.

records.qtitle: REQUIREMENT OF LOWER LEVELS SURVEILLANCE RADARS .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that IAF has only one-third of its requirements in respect of lower level surveillance Radars;

(b) if so, what are the reasons that it has not been allowed to procure the requisite number of Radars; and

(c) by when these requirements are likely to be met?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF DEFENCE

(SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE)


(a) A large number of radars are available with the Air Force. It is not in the interest of national security to disclose the details.

(b) & (c): Induction of new radars including lower level surveillance radars, is a continuous process based on the requirement of the Air Force.

records.qtitle: SATELLITE BASED RECONNAISSANCE AND SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the indigenous satellite-based reconnaissance and surveillance system, a Rs. 1050 crore joint ISRO- DRDO project to augment surveillance over the country`s airspace, is running behind schedule; if so, what are the reasons therefor; and

(b) by when it is now likely to be completed?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF DEFENCE

(SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE)


(a) Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) has undertaken a programme for satellite based surveillance and reconnaissance (SBS) for ground surveillance. Programme is in advanced stage of development and is planned to be completed by January 2007. Validation of Technologies has taken more time than anticipated.

(b) The project is likely to be completed by January 2007.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the work on the proposed refinery in Lohgada (near Allahaba

(d) has started; if so, the details thereof;

(b) if not, the reasons therefor and by when the work is likely to start; and

(c) if the reply to part

(a) above be in the affirmative, the status thereof?.
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS AND PANCHAYATI RAJ

(SHRI MANI SHANKAR AIYAR) z

(a) Land has been acquired and walled-off but construction is yet to begin.

(b) & (c) As at present, the implementation of the refinery project for Uttar Pradesh is slated to be taken up after completion of the Central India Refinery Project at Bina

(Madhya Pradesh). The scheduled completion of Central India Refinery Project is projected in 2009-10.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware that the wads of currency notes reissued by the Public Sector Banks contain a large number of mutilated, partially cut, two pieces, mismatched and very old notes that have completed their life;

(b) whether the practice is not in conformity with the directions issued by RBI; and

(c) the steps proposed to be taken to address the situation and avoid inconvenience to the customers ?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM)

(a) :- Reserve Bank of India (RBI) have reported that they have not come across any such complaints in the recent past.

(b):- In terms of the Reserve Bank directives and guidelines currency chest branches are required to verify, to process and to sort all the banknotes received by them both directly and from other branches and ensure that (a) banknotes unfit for further circulation are returned to the Reserve Bank and

(b) good quality banknotes are reissued.

(c):- RBI has created public awareness to insist on issue of clean banknotes by the banks. Banks are also authorised to accept and exchange soiled, mutilated, etc., banknotes. Reserve Bank has directed that the currency chest branches are equipped with appropriate machines to expedite the process of verification, processing and sorting of banknotes. While some banks have already installed such machines, banks with more than 100 currency chests have been given time upto November 30, 2005, to install the machines.

records.qtitle: REDUCTION IN FARES IN GULF SECTOR .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there has been a record reduction in the fares to and fro Gulf countries by Air India, Indian Airlines and other carriers;

(b) if so, how this has been made possible despite the rising cost of fuel; and

(c) what has been its impact on passenger traffic?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION ( SHRI PRAFUL PATEL )
(a),(b)&(c):- The airlines engaged in international air services to/from India are not required to file the fares with the Government and Government does not maintain details about air fares charged by airlines. According to Indian Airlines, there is no reduction in the IATA or Published fares applicable to/from Gulf countries. The actual fares quoted in the market are, however, much lower as these fares are based on demand/supply, seasonality and product features like frequency, timings, direct/indirect operations etc. There are frequent upward and downward movements of fares in response to market needs by various carriers operating on these sectors.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) the number of Supreme Court Judges who have either retired or are due to retire this year;

(b) whether Government have completed its exercise to fill up the resultant vacancies expeditiously;

(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and

(d) by when the appointments are likely to be finalized?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF LAW AND JUSTICE (SHRI H. R. BHARDWAJ)

(a), (b), (c) &(d) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House
Statement referred to in reply to parts (a),(b)&(c) and (d) of the Rajya Sabha Starred Question No. 216 for answer on 8.8.2005
Since January, 2005, 2 Judges of the Supreme Court have retired. During the remaining period of the year i.e. upto December, 2005, 4 more Judges of the Supreme Court will be retiring on attaining the age of superannuation.

2. After the Supreme Court Judgment of October 6, 1993 in the Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record & Anr. Vs. Union of India, read with their Advisory Opinion of October 28, 1998, the entire process of initiation of proposal for appointment Of a Judge of a Supreme Court lies with the Chief Justice of India.

3. Government has not received any proposal, so far, from the Chief Justice of India for appointment of Judges in the vacancies already available in the Supreme Court or those which will be falling vacant till December, 2005.

records.qtitle: ACUTE SHORTAGE OF DRINKING WATER AT RAILWAY STATIONS .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is an acute shortage of drinking water at various railway stations being faced by 98 per cent of the passengers; and

(b) the steps Government have taken to address the situation?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS


(SHRI R. VELU)


(a) & (b) Indian Railways have more than 8000 stations. Railways endeavour is to provide drinking water to passengers at all stations. Some small stations do not have adequate water source either due to absence of water supply from municipality or presence of brackish water, inadequate ground water yield from hand pumps. Further, even at some of those stations where piped/hand pump supply exists, water scarcity comes up in summer due to lesser supplies by municipality, lowering in ground water table etc. and increased demand. In such cases, availability of drinking water is ensured at stations by arranging water through private water tankers. Even water special trains are run in areas facing heavy shortage of water. Water coolers, mobile water trollies, matkas are arranged for better availability of water to the passengers. Many Non Government Organisations also supplement water supply to passengers. In addition, packaged drinking water/natural mineral water is made available for sale through static as well as mobile catering/vending units.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.min_name: CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are considering a proposal to import wheat, if so, the details thereof including the rates at which it is proposed to be imported;

(b) whether Government exported wheat a couple of months back, if so, the details thereof including the rates at which it was exported;

(c) the justification for the proposed import and the exports made; and

(d) whether Government have examined the possibility of the vested interests in the two deals?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD & PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION ( DR. AKHILESH PRASAD SINGH )

(a): There is no proposal to import wheat.

(b) & (c): Fresh allocation of foodgrains from the Central Pool, for commercial exports, has been stopped w.e.f. 11.8.2003. Only a quantity of 48,240 MTs of wheat has been exported by PEC Ltd. a Government of India, Enterprise, out of which 46,224 MT was exported on behalf of World Food Programme, (WFP), as part of humanitarian assistance. The exports were made at a rate of US $ 161.50 to US $ 168.00 per MT (FOB).

(d): Safeguard mechanism is an integral part of any import or export policy to ward off vested interests and had been provided in the export scheme as well.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government have examined the possibility of the country becoming a nucleus of stem cell research; and
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY AND MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE DEPARTMENT OF OCEAN DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI KAPIL SIBAL)


(a) & (b) A statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT IN RESPECT OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.177 TO BE ANSWERED ON 04/08/2005 REGARDING STEM CELL RESEARCH


(a) Yes Madam. Brainstorming meetings on stem cells were organized to identify priorities and to examine the possibilities to enhance research in this area in the country. The main features of strategy include promotion of stem cell research for therapeutic applications using adult and embryonic stem cells as well as other more readily available sources such as bone marrow, peripheral blood and umbilical cord blood cells.

(b) Major initiatives have been taken to develop stem cell research programmes for limbal, haematopoitic, neural, liver, cardiac, embryonic and human corneal stem cells and the stem cell preservation. Limbal stem cells are being used at L.V. Prasad Eye Institute (LVPEI), Hyderabad to repair cornea surface disorders caused by limbal stem cells deficiencies. Under the programme supported at Christian Medical College (CMC), Vellore, a technology has been established for collection, purification and haplo-identical haematopoietic stem cell transplantation. The studies conducted at the National Centre for Cell Science (NCCS), Pune and the Indian Institute of Science (IISc.), Bangalore showed that banana lectins have stem cell preservation activities. Long and short term training programme have been initiated. National and International conferences on the various aspects of the subject are being periodically organized. Inter institutional city clusters programmes have been implemented at Vellore and Pune by involving basic researchers, clinicians and industry. This includes sharing of information, exploration of collaboration and discussion on emerging policy issues etc. Bangalore, Hyderabad and Delhi city cluster programmes are being considered. It is also proposed to establish Centres of Excellence for stem cell research initially at 2 or 3 places to initiate focused, targeted programmes on human stem cell research by involving basc researchers and clinicians. An advertisement to invite proposals o identifiy sdathe programmes and the sites has been widely publicized.

records.qtitle: COOPERATION WITH PAKISTAN IN I.T. SECTOR.
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
:-

(a) whether Government have explored the possibility of cooperation with Pakistan in the field of Information Technology; and

(b) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE FOR COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY(DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD)



(a): Yes, Sir.


(b): In the Indo-Pak Bilateral Talks on Economic and Commercial Cooperation held at Islamabad during 11th-12th August, 2004, India made a special offer for full cooperation in any area of importance to Pakistan in IT sector, e-governance, e-commerce, IT enabled services.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
:-

(a) whether it is a fact that currently the power to govern the internet rests with the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (ICANN), based in California;

(b) whether Government are contemplating to wrest control of internet on expiry of MoU in September, 2006 between ICANN and the Department of Commerce of the USA; and

(c) if so, the details in this regard?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE FOR COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY(DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD)


(a): ICANN is an internationally organized, non-profit corporation that has responsibility for Internet Protocol (IP) address space allocation, protocol identifier assignment, generic

(gTLD ) and country code (ccTLD) Top-Level Domain name system management, and root server system management functions. As a public-private partnership, ICANN is dedicated to preserving the operational stability and security of the Internet.


(b) and (c): No Sir, Government after consultation with all stakeholders have declared that governments and all stakeholders should have effective say in all deliberations on Internet policy. These should be transparent, inclusive and democratic.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether there is any possibility of Free Trade Agreement materialising among Asian countries; if so, the details thereof; and

(b) what is likely to be the impact of this agreement on the automobile industry in the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY

(SHRI KAMAL NATH)

(a): The Government of India has signed the South Asia Free Trade Area (SAFTA) Agreement comprising SAARC members, Framework Agreement with Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) on Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement (CECA), Framework Agreement for Bay of Bengal Initiative Multisectoral Technical & Economic Cooperation Free Trade Agreement (BIMSTEC FTA), Bilateral CECA with Singapore, Bilateral Free Trade Agreements with Nepal, Bhutan and Sri Lanka, and is negotiating bilateral CECA with few other Asian countries. However, at present, there is no move for entering into a single Free Trade Agreement among all Asian countries.

(b): The coverage of goods and the tariff liberalization programme under various Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) are finalized after due consultation with domestic stakeholders, which includes the automobile industry in the country, so that their views and sensitivities are taken into account in the negotiations.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) what is the estimated number of Nepalese gurkhas in the country;

(b) whether it is a fact that with fewer jobs left in the army, many Nepalese gurkhas are taking up arms for the Maoists; and

(c) the steps Government are contemplating to address the situation?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL)

(a): The Government does not have data on Nepalese gurkhas . However, as per 2001 census, there are 6,40,862 persons who have reportedly been born in Nepal and enumerated in India.

(b): There are no reports to indicate that Nepalese gurkhas are taking up arms for Maoists in the wake of lesser job opportunities in the Army.

(c): Does not arise.

records.qtitle: SELF SUFFICIENCY BY INDIAN ARMED FORCES .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that on the occasion of celebration of Taknik Diwas by Defence Research and Development Organisation Prime Minister is reported to have stated that the Indian Armed Forces will have to attain self-sufficiency;

(b) what is the current status of the Indian Armed Forces vis a vis self-sufficiency; and

(c) whether the goal can be achieved in a time-frame?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF DEFENCE

(SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE)


(a) Yes, Sir. Prime Minister stated that self-reliant military is essential for our strategic autonomy.

(b) Government has the policy of progressively enhancing indigenous content of weapon systems in the Armed Forces. We are self reliant in several areas of military technology i.e. arms & ammunition, combat and armoured vehicles, guided missiles, aircraft, communication, radars and sonar systems.

(c) Self-sufficiency is dictated by threat perception in a region which is a continuously changing phenomenon. India is moving steadily in the direction of achieving the goal of self-sufficiency.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Rajasthan seems to set for a spell of water crisis and consequently the riots; and

(b) the steps Government have taken to address the situation?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES

(SHRI JAI PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV)

(a) As per Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB) that regulates Sutlej and Ravi-Beas waters, the position of water availability in BBMB’s reservoirs, due to the normal monsoon this year so far, is very comfortable and has enabled BBMB to meet the full water requirements of the Partner States including Rajasthan. Further, BBMB has delivered an average of 13,488 cusecs to Rajasthan from 1st to 28th July, 2005 against Rajasthan’s share of 13,025 cusecs and BBMB has even requested the Partner States to maximize their drawals notwithstanding their respective shares so as to avoid the wastage of water downstream of Madhopur and Ferozepur Headworks. Water availability in important reservoirs monitored Central Water Commission has also indicated that the aggregate current year’s storage as on 22.7.05 in Mahi Bajaj Sagar, Jhakam and Rana Pratap Sagar reservoirs in Rajasthan is about 1.45 thousand million cubic metres, which is 240% of the last year’s storage and 197% of the last 10 year’s average storage during the corresponding period.

(b) Handing over of successful exploratory wells by Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) to the Rajasthan State Government and technical assistance from CGWB to the State for promotion of rain water harvesting and artificial recharge of ground water etc. are some of the on-going steps and will be of help in a crisis situation.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text: MINISTER OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS & PANCHAYATI RAJ(SHRI MANI SHANKAR AIYAR)
records.ans_text:
(a): whether it is a fact that the country is running out of oil with 0.4 per cent of the world’s oil reserves left in the country for 15 per cent of the world’s population;

(b): what is the status of the oil reserves of other countries vis a vis their population;

(c): whether the self-sufficiency in oil has now become a distant dream, if so, what is the annual production in the country at present and projections for the next five years; and(d): the steps Government are contemplating to address the situation?

(a) & (b): As on 1.4.2005, proven oil reserves in the country are to the order of 740 Million Metric Tonnes(MMT), which are about 0.5% of the total proven reserves of the world. India has about 28 billion tonnes of prognosticated hydrocarbon reserves, out of which, only 8.2 billion tonnes of hydrocarbon reserves have been established so far. The status of oil reserves vis-à-vis population is annexed

(source:B.P statistics)

(c): Given the present demand scenario and the status of production of oil in the country, self-sufficiency is not envisaged in the near future. The production of crude oil for the year 2004-05 was 33.980 MMT. According to current estimates the projections of crude oil production for the next 5 years are as follow:- 
 

(figures in MMT)	2005-06   2006-07   2007-08    2008-09  2009-10 
			34.67      35.90    39.62      37.26    37.07 

(d):  The following steps have already
been taken to enhance oil security:- 

(i)	Accelerating domestic hydrocarbon exploration. 

(ii)	Implementation of Improved Oil Recovery(IOR)/Enhanced Oil Recovery(EOR) projects to
enhance oil recovery. 

(iii)	Offer new acreages through New Exploration Licensing 
Policy(NELP).  Already 108 exploration blocks have been awarded including 18 exploration 
blocks offered under fifth round of NELP. 

(iv)	Acquisition of overseas oil and gas assets. 

(v)	Development of alternate sources such as Coal Bed Methane(CBM), Underground Coal 
Gassification(UCG) and Gas Hydrates. 

(vi)	Storage of oil. 

(vii)	Conservation of oil.

records.name: N.R. GOVINDARAJAR
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that a large number of companies which entered the capital market from 1993 to 1995 have disappeared with a sum of about Rs.1700 crores;

(b) whether it is also a fact that despite prosecution, proceedings and arrests in some cases, not a single rupee has so far been recovered and restored to investors;

(c) whether the prosecution agencies like CBI are now taking the plea behind various definitions of the terms like investors etc. and openly denying the possibility of restoration of invested funds to their investors; and

(d) if so, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF COMPANY AFFAIRS

( SHRI PREM CHAND GUPTA)


(a) 71 companies stand identified as on date as Vanishing Companies which came out with IPOs during the period 1993-1995, for raising a sum of Rs.607.65 crores from the public.

(b) Even though prosecution and disgorgement proceedings have been initiated in a few cases, a final outcome in these cases still awaited as it involves court process.

(c) & (d) This Ministry has not referred any case of Vanishing Companies to CBI for investigation. However, Prosecutions have been filed against these companies under various provisions of the Companies Act,1956. FIRs have also been filed under the provisions of Indian Penal Code (IPC) and investigations are under progress by Police Authorities in various States.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have reviewed the arrangements in connection with Commonwealth Games 2010; if so, with what results;

(b) whether it is a fact that distractions near the Games Village including railway track and Akshardham Temple, traffic bottlenecks and venues being located far away from city`s airports are some of the problems; and

(c) the steps contemplated to address the situation?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE PRIME MINISTER`S OFFICE

(SHRI PRITHVIRAJ CHAVAN)

(a) Government of India has constituted a Core Group of Ministers (GOM) for coordinating the work relating to the organization of the Commonwealth Games, 2010. An Apex Committee for overseeing and coordinating the Games has been set up. An Organizing Committee under the Chairmanship of President, IOA for conduct of the Games has been constituted.
The arrangements for holding the Commonwealth Games 2010 at Delhi are underway. A review of existing infrastructure in the city of Delhi in context of Commonwealth Games 2010 has been undertaken. The existing infrastructure with Sports Authority of India (SAI), Delhi Development Authority (DDA) and New Delhi Municipal Corporation (NDMC) with required upgradation and renovation would be used for most of the disciplines covered under the Commonwealth Games.
A Task Force for upgradation/renovation of SAI`s infrastructure has been set up and the consultancy on SAI`s existing infrastructure has been assigned to CPWD. Condition Survey of SAI`s existing five Stadia at Delhi has been undertaken.
Regarding construction of a Commonwealth Games Village, a site off the Nizamuddin Bridge has been identified. Delhi Development Authority has also commenced the action to prepare preliminary designs in respect of new venues & Games Village proposed to be constructed by it.
A core Committee has been set up by Government of NCT of Delhi under the Chairmanship of Chief Secretary, Delhi to prepare a master plan for improvement/up gradation of civic amenities in Delhi for Commonwealth Games, 2010. The Government of NCT of Delhi is in the process of finalizing plans for up gradation of roads, health care, civic amenities, traffic management and parking for the Commonwealth Games.

(b) DDA have engaged M/s Event Knowledge Service for Venue Reappraisal Study who have submitted a draft report. The draft report has flagged issues like traffic bottlenecks, proximity to Akshardham Tample & a railway track, distance from airport, etc.

( c) The matter is being discussed with various stakeholders to meet these concerns.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that reappearance of mosquitoes throughout the country has resulted in revival of Malaria;

(b) whether Government have conducted any research on Malaria repellants like planting of Marigold flowers or other such measures; if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether inadequate sewerage in cities and towns is one of the factors for reappearance of mosquitoes and revival of Malaria; and

(d) if so, the steps Government have taken to deal with the situation?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

( SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)

(a): The mosquito nuisance is determined by several factors like unplanned urbanization, physical environment, life style of the people and water-management system. There are several species of the mosquitos which have different breeding habits. The mosquito for spread of malaria i.e. `Anopheles` usually breeds in clean water. The effective control of mosquito can be achieved by environmental modifications & manipulations. The National Malaria Control Programme was started by the Govt.of India in 1953 which was converted to National Malaria Eradication Programme in 1958. There was spectacular reduction of malaria incidence as well as deaths. However, during late 1970`s there was resurgence of malaria due to operational, technical and administrative factors. With the introduction of Modified Plan of Operation in 1977, the number of malaria cases declined from 6.4 million to below 2 million in 2002. Since then the number of cases of malaria has remained below 2 million.

(b): Though there are some reports in literature about the insecticidal and repellent activity of the extracts of Tagetus (Marigold), these have not been used/studied as malaria repellent by planting of Marigold flowers and other plants in the country.
There is however a report on a study conducted by scientists from Kenya and Ethiopia on live potted plants including Tagetus (Marigold) tested as mosquito repellent which did not show any significant repellent effect of Tagetus.

(c) & (d): Bad sewerage system cause breeding of Culex mosquitos but malaria transmitting Anopheles mosquitos do not breed in sewer water.
The Govt.of India has a well defined Programme viz. National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme(NVBDCP) for control of malaria in the country adopting strategies which include surveillance, early diagnosis and prompt treatment of cases, sustainable vector control including Indoor Residual Spray with insecticides treated bednets, use of larvivorous fish etc. besides Training & Information, Education and Communication to enlist community involvement. Urban Malaria Scheme is also being implemented in 131 Towns in the country to reduce density of mosquitoes and to prevent spread of malaria.

records.qtitle: PERFORMANCE OF KISAN CREDIT CARD SCHEME QUESTION .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) what has been the performance so far of the Kisan Credit Card schemes and the extent of its acceptance by farmers;

(b) what is the credit limit and the rate of interest under the scheme;

(c) whether the scheme is available throughout the country and if not, the reasons therefor; and

(d) whether Government are considering any proposal to extend it to all parts of the country and if so, by when ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THF, MINISTRY OF FINANCE
(SHRI S.S.PALANIMANICKAM)

(a) Kisan Credit Card(KCC) Scheme has emerged as a widely accepted mechanism for delivery of hassle-free crop loan to farmers. The scheme, introduced in August 1998 as an innovative credit delivery mechanism, has been progressing satisfactorily. About 4.80 crore KCCs have been issued till 31st January, 2005. The scope of the scheme has been recently enlarged to cover the term loans for agriculture and allied activities including a reasonable component to meet consumption needs besides the existing facility of providing crop loan limit.

(b): No ceiling has been envisaged for sanction of credit limit under the scheme. However, the banks may fix the credit limit to farmers on the basis of their land holding, cropping pattern and scale of finance recommended by the District Level Technical Committee. The Co-operative Banks also take into account the individual maximum borrowing power fixed by the Registrar of the Co-operative Societies while fixing the credit limit under the scheme which may vary from State to State. As the interest rate regime has been deregulated by the Reserve Bank of India, banks have been provided freedom to fix the rate of interest on credit limit sanctioned. Hence, no uniform rate of interest is applicable to KCC in respect of Co-operative Banks and regional Rural Banks. records.qtitle: AMERICAN AID TO SILL LANKA FOR TSUNAMI RELIEF
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Sri Lanka decided to accept 1500 US Marines as a part of fire US contribution to Tsunami relief work in the island without taking India into confidence first;

(b) if so, whether Government have expressed their concern in this regard and if so, in what manner; and

(c) the final outcome thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI E. AHAMED)

(a), (b) & (c) According to figures released by the US Embassy in Colombo a total of about 830 US Armed Forces personnel were deployed on the ground in Sri Lanka. This included about 700 US Marines. This excludes US personnel manning ships deployed off the coast of Sri Lanka who would probably have numbered between 700 to 900.
The tsunami disaster in Sri Lanka and other Indian Ocean rim countries attracted a very high degree of international attention mad evoked an enormous outpouring of compassion and international assistance to the affected countries, including Sri Lanka. The scale of the devastation caused was so great that all relief contributions were welcome. India was a key player in this major international humanitarian effort in Sri Lanka and other affected countries and was, along with the United States, a member of` the Core Group that coordinated relief in the initial phases.
The Indian Navy launched ``Operation Rainbow` the day the tsunami struck. The first Indian naval Dornier carrying 650kg of medical supplies and a medical team arrived in Sri Lanka on December 26 itself Almost simultaneously, four Indian naval ships steamed towards the ports of Galle and Trincomalee. These vessels, which picked up relief supplies on the way, reached Sri Lanka just over 24 hours afterwards and immediately commenced relief and damage control operations. Tiffs deployment was stepped up to include stationing of an air detachment of ten aircraft for three weeks, about fifteen naval ship-loads of supplies, fifteen medical teams including a mobile field hospital (140 men) that was airlifted and specialist doctors, a 45-bed hospital ship (INS Jamuna) that was anchored of Galle and Trincomalee for two weeks, ten teams of naval divers mad a 8 I-member. composite Army disaster management team.
Sri Lankan President Kumaratunga, Prime Minister Rajapakse and several Sri Lankan Ministers have expressed the gratitude of the people of Sri Laaaka for Indian assistance. President Kumaratunga also dispatched Foreign Minister Lakshman Kadirgamar as Special Envoy to thank India for its generous contribution to the relief efforts.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI M.A.A. FATMI)

records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that he made a statement at Chennai while releasing the book - India Untouched : the Forgotten Face of Rural Poverty, on 8th September, 2004;

(b) if so, whether it is a fact that he stated inter-alia that it will take 200 years to wipe out poverty;

(c) what is the basis of his statement and whether this statement is at variance with the stated position of Government; if so, the reasons therefore; and

(d) the other points he made in the statement?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM)

(a) to (d) A book entitled `India Untouched: The forgotten face of Rural Poverty` written by Dr. Abraham M. George was released by Hon`ble Finance Minister on 6th September, 2004 in Chennai. Hon`ble Finance Minister had inter-alia pointed out the decline in the quality of the delivery systems, and how state intervention had stifled the spirit of enterprise and initiative in the villages. He went on to commend the Constitutional amendments which introduced Panchayati Raj and called upon both the Central Government and the State Governments to devolve functions and funds upon Panchayati Raj institutions.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a)

(a) what is the source and amount of blood collected by Blood Banks in the country with details of authorised Blood Banks ;

(b)

(b) whether blood is also imported from foreign countries ;

(c)

(c) if so, the details in this regard, with amount spent on such imports annually and measures put in place to ensure the imported blood is not contaminated/infected;

(d)

(d) whether it is a fact that blood imported from U.K. was infected with ‘Mad Cow Disease’ virus ; and

(e)

(e) if so, the details of such imports and the action taken to assess the damage caused by infected blood and contain further damage ?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

( SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)

(a) Blood is collected in the country from voluntary and replacement donors. During 2003, 1988344 units of blood through voluntary and 1949122 units of blood through replacement donations were collected. As per the information received from Drugs Controller General (India), there are 1854 licensed blood banks in the country. The details are at annexure.

(b) No Sir.

(c) The question does not arise.

(d) & (e) There is no import of blood from U.K. However, blood products derived from human plasma were imported from U.K. Investigations conducted by Drug Controller General (India) revealed that 22 vials of Vigam-S 5 g (Human Normal Immunoglobulin) batch No. VGC 085 manufactured by M/s Bio Products Laboratory, U.K. was imported in India from a blood donor in U.K who later developed variant Creutzfeldt-Jacob Disease (vCJD). M/s Bio Products Laboratory, U.K. exported this consignment to M/s Genexx Chemicals Pvt. Ltd, New Delhi in 1997. The manufacturing date of the said Lot was July 1997 and expiry date August 1999.
According to the WHO, there is no credible instance of transmission of vCJD through blood products. The Government has not received any reported incidents of vCJD disease through blood products in the country so far.

records.qtitle: NON ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF LETTERS BY UTI
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether he is aware that UTI does not acknowledge receipt of letters from investors regarding change of residential address for long-term schemes;

(b) if so, whether this attitude of UTI is likely to cause

(c) inconvenience to investors and loss of confidence about the administrative functioning of UTI; and (c ) the remedial steps Government have taken in this regard?
records.ans_text:
FINANCE MINISTER

(SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM)

(a) to (c): A statement is placed on the Table of the House.
Statement referred to in the reply to the Rajya Sabha Starred Question No. 200 raised by Shrimati Jaya Bachchan, Member of Parliament, for 14th December, 2004 regarding `Non-acknowledgement of letters by UTI`.

(a) The Specified Undertaking of UTI (SUUTI) has reported that all letters from investors addressed to the UTI Mutual Fund/ Specified Undertaking of UTI are acknowledged before being forwarded to the Registrars for necessary action. The Registrars of the schemes of UTI Mutual Fund/SUUTI have confirmed that they acknowledge/confirm the letters received from investors regarding change of address. Investors can also submit letters relating to any service, including change of address, to any of the branch offices of UTI Mutual Fund. The branch offices promptly acknowledge receipt of such letters and forward the same to the Registrars for necessary action.

(b) & (c) : In the last one year ending November 2004, SUUTI handled more than one crore transactions of investors - including requests for change of address. However, SUUTI is committed to resolve all issues regarding any service offered, including change of residential address, in respect of the schemes of the erstwhile UTI.

records.qtitle: NON RECEIPT OF OPTION LETTERS OF UTI SCHEMES
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware that UTI has not responded to letters from investor in respect of schemes that were foreclosed, like Children Gift Growth Fund in April this year;

(b) if so, the fate of the investments made by the investors in this scheme who failed to exercise any option under the scheme due to non-receipt of option letters sent by UTI; and

(c) whether Government propose to direct UTI to immediately inform such investors? SHRI S. S. PALANIMANICKAM
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(a) As informed by the Specified Undertaking of the UTI

(SUUTI), the Registrars of the foreclosed schemes including Children`s Gift Growth Fund (CGGF) have confirmed that they have responded to the letters/option forms received from the unit holders. Based on the option exercised, either the redemption amount was paid or the proceeds were converted to the Assured Return Scheme(ARS) Bonds guaranteed by the Government of India .

(b) CGGF-86, CGGF-99, Rajlakshmi Unit Plan (RUP)-94, and RUP-99 were launched in the years 1986, 1999, 1994 and 1999 respectively. The total number of investors were around 36 lakhs. A number of investors had not indicated the guardian`s name, to whom reminder letters have been sent. In other cases, where no option was exercised within the stipulated time by the unit holders, the redemption proceeds were converted into ARS Bonds.

(c) As and when any such case is brought to the notice of the Government, SUUTI is advised to take appropriate action in the matter.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that transactions carried over interact are no longer safe; and

(b) if so, the details of steps contemplated to ensure safety of internet transactions?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM)

(a): No, Sir. ,

(b): To ensure safety of internet transactions, the Reserve Bank of India has issued guidelines on Internet Banking in India to all Scheduled Commercial Banks. The guidelines were based on the recommendations of the `Working Group on Internet Banking set up by the Reserve Bank of India to examine the different aspects of Internet Banking. The guidelines, which were issued for implementation by banks, focus on Security and Technology standards, apart from dealing regulatory and Supervisory issues as well as Legal. issues pertaining to Internet Banking. All banks offering Internet Banking services are required to strictly adhere to the Security and Technology Standards prescribed in the guidelines. Their compliance with the standards is also checked in course of the annual financial inspection of the banks carried out by the Reserve Bank of India.

records.ans_text:
(a) & (b) : The inflow of FDI depends on a numbers of factors both external and internal. Besides policy dispensation, global economic environment, corporate strategy of transnational corporations and domestic economic situation play a major role in determining the FDI inflows,

records.qtitle: LIMIT TO CROSS SHARE HOLDING OF BANKS .
records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have decided to tighten the cross share holding roles of the entire banking industry;

(b) if so, what are the details thereof; and (€) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM)

(a) & (b) Reserve Bank of India monitors cross holding of capital among banks and financial institutions. A bank`s aggregate investment in Tier II Bonds issued by other banks and financial institutions is permitted upto I0 percent of the investing bank`s capital funds. They also should not acquire any fresh stake in a bank`s equity shares if by such acquisition the investing banks/FIs holding exceeds 5 percent of the investee bank`s equity capital. The above ceiling are applicable to all types of instrument listed below which are issued by other banks/FIs and are eligible for capital status for the investee bank/FIs:-

(i) Equity shares
(ii) Preference shares eligible for capital status;
(iii) Subordinate debt instruments;
(iv) Hybrid debt capital instruments, and
(v) Any other instrument approved as in the nature of capital

(c) Does not arise.

records.name: Jaya Amitabh Bachchan
records.qn_text:

(b) If so, the details thereof; and

(c) the steps Government have taken to meet the shortage and the result thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS & MINISTER OF STEEL

(SHRI RAM VILAS PASWAN)

(a) to (c): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.

Statement referred to in reply to parts (a) to (c) of the Rajya Sabha Starred Question No. 367 to be answered on 20.8.2004.

(a): There is an increase of about 57% in the sale of MOP to farmers upto 31.7.2004 during current Kharif 2004. 5.53 lakh MT MOP has been sold upto 31.7.2004 as compared with the sale of

3.51 lakh MT in the corresponding period last year. Some of the State Governments have reported inadequate supplies of MOP.

(b) & (c): There was an unprecedented increase in the price of MOP in the international market, this year, because of which there was delay in finalisation of MOP price. The Government has now decided to consider this hike in international prices for announcement of concession/subsidy and imports are now taking place in adequate quantities.

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT

(SHRI SIS RAM OLA)


(a) to (c): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.

Statement referred to in reply to parts (a) to (c) of Rajya Sabha Starred Question No. 342 due for reply on 19.08.2004 by Shrimati Jaya Bachchan and Shri Amar Singh regarding recruitment of ex-Servicemen to guard U.S. installation in Iraq
..

(a): No, Sir.

(b): Does not arise.

(c): However, attention of the Government was drawn to media reports about irregular recruitment of Indian ex-Servicemen for duties in Iraq by three agencies, namely,
(i) M/s. Trig Guardforce Ltd., Mumbai;
(ii) M/s. IBI Detectives Pvt. Ltd., Mumbai; and
(iii) M/s. Gemini Veterans Global Placements, New Delhi. It was also reported that in January, 2004, M/s. Trig Guardforce Ltd., Mumbai had sent three officers and 40 (forty) men for deployment in Iraq. The Protector of Emigrants, Mumbai has filed a complaint with the Mumbai Police against both M/s. Trig Guardforce Ltd., Mumbai and M/s. IBI Detectives Pvt. Ltd., Mumbai for violation of the ban placed by the Government on recruitment for employment in Iraq. Both these agencies are not registered as recruiting agencies. M/s. Gemini Veterans Global Placements, New Delhi is a registered recruiting agency. They were served a show-cause notice. ...
